priorities.description: MAKE articles.json's DERIVED COUNTS SELF-MAINTAINING, OR STOP CARRYING THEM. On 2026-09-05 a recompute found 54 OF 104 RECORDS -- better than half -- carrying a stale word_count or open_questions. Two causes. (1) Nothing recomputes them: they are written by hand whenever an article is edited, so they drift from the moment they are set, and a reader has no way to tell a current figure from a year-old one. (2) Six articles numbered their Open Questions list from 0 rather than 1, so every count taken off those lists was short by one; all six are now renumbered. The word_count field also uses Python str.split() semantics, which do not match `wc -w` -- a difference that misled this project's own operator report today until it was checked directly. FIX: either add a builder like scripts/plaque/build_index.py and have data_integrity.py assert the file matches it -- the pattern this repo already uses for the multi-year index and which works -- or drop both fields, since a stale number is worse than no number. Prefer the builder: word_count and open_questions are genuinely useful for triage, and p_412 showed how quickly an unmaintained field stops being read at all. | COMPLETED 2026-09-05. Builder route taken, not the drop-the-fields route. scripts/wiki/build_article_counts.py now generates word_count, open_questions and article_count, and data_integrity.py regenerates wiki/articles.json into a scratch copy and fails if the committed file differs -- the arrangement the plaque index already uses. Fifty of 104 records carried a stale open_questions and article_count read 93 against 104 records, eleven articles behind. word_count was already current (all 104 matched), so the definition it was computed under is the one the builder keeps, documented in the module docstring including why it is not `wc -w`. open_questions is now the count of entries that are still OPEN: an entry struck through, or opening with an unqualified [Resolved]/[ANSWERED] tag, is not counted, while [Partially resolved] and [Largely resolved] are, because a remainder is a remainder. That is why most counts fell -- 103 of 470 listed questions are answered in place. STILL OPEN, deliberately: three articles number their Open Questions lists 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,7,8 (coeducation-gender), 1..7,9,10,8 (myths-and-legends) and 1..7,7,8,9 (camp-songs-cheers). The builder reports them and does not renumber, because other articles cite questions by number ('billy-ball Open Question #8') and shifting a number silently re-points a citation at a different question. Renumbering needs a pass over the citing articles at the same time.

priorities.description: SETTLE WHETHER KANAWANA'S KATIMAVIK IS NAMED FOR THE FEDERAL KATIMAVIK PROGRAMME, and read the 1977-79 record around the opening. Three things sit together in 1978 and nothing connects them (f_4833): the camp opened a recreation hall called Katimavik; staff member John Lawrence was living inside the federal Katimavik programme, created 1977, per Ka-News October and December 1978 (f_4832); and Pierre Elliott Trudeau, whose government created that programme, sent the camp a congratulatory letter (f_4828). A camp naming a building in Inuktitut in the 1970s needs no federal explanation, so this must not be written up as a connection on the coincidence alone. WHERE TO LOOK: the full Ka-News run for 1977-79 (several issues are already cached and were read only for other purposes), the 1977 and 1979 director's reports, and the $850,000 reconstruction file behind f_2443 -- a building that size will have a naming decision somewhere. ALSO WORTH ASKING ANYONE WHO WAS THERE. SECOND QUESTION, SAME SOURCES: what stood on the Katimavik site before 1978, which places-and-locations.md Open Question 3 still carries. THIRD: whether other framed correspondence hangs at camp -- this letter was unknown to the project until the operator photographed it, and a Prime Minister's letter is unlikely to be the only thing on those walls. || FULL READ OF THE 1977-79 KA-NEWS RUN DONE 2026-09-06 (eleven issues, every word). THE KATIMAVIK NAMING QUESTION IS UNTOUCHED BY IT: 'Katimavik' occurs three times in the whole run and every occurrence is John Lawrence's federal placement, not the building -- an October 1978 address 'c/o Katimavik, Box 354, Bridgetown, N.S.' shared with a Peter Porteous, and the December line 'John Lawrence is really enjoying Katimavik, he heads out west soon with his group.' THAT DOES CONFIRM THE FEDERAL PROGRAMME as the thing Lawrence was in -- a placement, a group, and a cross-country move are what the federal Katimavik did -- but the newsletter never mentions the camp's building at all, in the year it is supposed to have opened. So the coincidence is still a coincidence and must stay one. WHAT THE READ DID PRODUCE, all now in the KB: Walsh's resignation letter of 5 February 1979, which resolves derek-walsh.md open question 2 against the way the article had it (f_5219, f_5220); a date for John Cleghorn's Montreal YMCA chairmanship (f_5221); the autumn 1978 septic and renovation programme (f_5222); the 1979 tightening of staff terms and a 1978 Quebec lifeguard-certification law relevant to p_388 (f_5223); a Hong Kong staff exchange that went nowhere (f_5224); a magazine article now queued as p_457 (f_5225); and the 1 December 1977 line that the new-site construction had not started, 'so here we go again with another last summer' (f_5227). THE SECOND QUESTION -- what stood on the Katimavik site before 1978 -- IS ALSO UNANSWERED by these issues. Remaining Ka-News in the cache: 1980-05, 1981-02-06, 1981-04-21, unread as of this note.

priorities.description: THREE ANNUAL REPORTS, THREE SEASONS: 1911, 1914 AND 1920. After both fills of 2026-09-05 the attendance series has exactly three seasons with no evidence of operation at all, and each needs one specific volume: the YMCA of Montreal annual reports covering those seasons, published in 1912, 1915 and 1921. NONE IS IN THE DIGITIZED RUN -- it jumps 1910 to 1913, the 1915 volume carries no Kanawana content, and it jumps 1920 to 1921-1922. WHY IT MATTERS: the 126-consecutive-seasons claim (1894-2019) is the one superlative that survives the continuity test, and these three are the only years left where it rests on silence. WHERE TO LOOK: Concordia Archives holds the YMCA of Montreal fonds and the full report series in print (add to the p_282 letter); Internet Archive may hold volumes catalogued under a title this project has not searched; BAnQ and the McGill and McCord collections hold Montreal association material. ALSO WORTH ONE PASS: the Montreal Gazette for July and August of 1911, 1914 and 1920 -- the paper covered the camp in 1918 and would likely have noticed a season that did not happen.
priorities.source: p_403 second fill, 2026-09-05

priorities.description: ASK THE TAYLOR STATTEN CAMPS WHETHER EASTAUGH'S CEREMONY DOCUMENT SURVIVES. Writing in Canadian Camping in Spring 1973, Jack Eastaugh, Assistant to the Director of the Taylor Statten Camps, offered readers 'a complete and detailed description of the rituals, ceremonies, games and organization' of the Indian Council Ring on request. THAT IS THE VERSION KANAWANA'S LEADERS WERE TAUGHT. p_368 has now established that the printed ancestor is Seton's Book of Woodcraft of 1912 and traced the closing chant to Alice Fletcher's Omaha fieldwork, but between Seton's book and a Laurentian camp's script stands Taylor Statten's teaching of the 1920s, and Eastaugh's document is the closest surviving form of it. ASK: the Taylor Statten Camps (Camps Ahmek and Wapomeo, Canoe Lake, Algonquin Park) directly; the Ontario Camping Association fonds at Trent University Archives, which holds the association's own papers and taped interviews (p_348); and the Ahmek/Statten family papers if they are deposited anywhere. NEEDS A HUMAN or a written enquiry.
priorities.source: p_368 Seton comparison, 2026-09-05

priorities.description: WRITE TO THE COMMISSION DE TOPONYMIE DU QUEBEC. Its fiches for Lac Kanawana (no_seq 31996), the lieu-dit Kanawana (31995), Lac Wilson (67247) and Camp Kanawana (144200) all say "L'origine de ce nom et, le cas echeant, sa signification n'ont pu etre determinees jusqu'a maintenant" and carry a standing invitation: "La Commission de toponymie invite toute personne detenant une information sur l'un ou l'autre de ces aspects a lui en faire part." Last updated 7 October 2020. THIS PROJECT HOLDS PART OF THE ANSWER. The 1951 Kamp Kanawana history states that the 1910 site-search committee located "Lake St. Louis, the present site" and that "the name of the lake was also changed from Ste Louis to Lake Kanawana" (f_2372), and that "Mr. J. W. McConnell purchased the land around Lake Desjardins. This he presented to the Y.M.C.A., and the lake was renamed 'Lake Wilson' after Mr. McConnell's son" (f_2371). Both are sourced to a document in the Internet Archive and can be cited. WHAT TO SEND: the two former names with the 1951 history as the citation, the camp's founding date, and an explicit statement that the MEANING of "Kanawana" is not established by any source this project has found -- do not offer the "lots to eat" camp lore as an etymology, since Dawson's 1933 history says the meaning was not learned until years after the name was adopted. ASK IN RETURN: whether the Commission's working file holds anything not printed on the public fiche, and on what basis Origine_linguistique is recorded as Algonquin in the open dataset when the fiche disclaims knowing the origin. Contact through the Nous joindre page at toponymie.gouv.qc.ca. NEEDS THE OPERATOR: it is a letter, and it puts this project's name on a submission to a provincial body.
priorities.source: p_264 toponymy campaign, 2026-09-06

priorities.description: CAMP OLIER AND CAMP DE L'AVENIR: two camps three kilometres from Kanawana that this project has never heard of. Both are OFFICIAL QUEBEC TOPONYMS in Sainte-Anne-des-Lacs, entity class Camp -- CAMP OLIER at 45.82833/-74.15333, officialised 1985-11-07, and CAMP DE L'AVENIR at 45.83555/-74.15889, officialised 2005-12-08, both recorded as French in origin (f_4891). Neither appears in kb/facts.json, in any wiki article, or in the Quebec camp landscape article's lists. They are closer to Kanawana than Tamaracouta is. WHAT TO DO: fetch each fiche from toponymie.gouv.qc.ca for its 'Origine et signification' note, which for Ile Jones ran to a full paragraph with a cited book (f_4889); then search for each camp by name -- 'Camp Olier' is very likely Catholic (Jean-Jacques Olier founded the Sulpicians, who held the seigneury of Montreal), which would make it a third confessional camp in the immediate district beside Kanawana's Protestant YMCA one. Check the ACQ and CCA directories this project has already read for either name, the Sainte-Anne-des-Lacs municipal history, and the Societe d'histoire et de genealogie des Pays-d'en-Haut. IF EITHER IS SUBSTANTIAL, it belongs in connections/related-camps/quebec-camp-landscape.md and possibly in points-of-contact.md. Note the method that surfaced them: the register's 'Camp' entity class is a list of named camps with coordinates, and it has not been swept province-wide -- doing that would give this project a map of Quebec's camps that no directory provides. CORRECTION 2026-09-06, SAME DAY, TO THIS PRIORITY'S OWN CLOSING SENTENCE. The province-wide sweep was run immediately and the claim that the register's Camp class 'would give this project a map of Quebec's camps that no directory provides' IS WRONG. There are 87 entries; about forty are on Ile d'Anticosti and most of the rest are outfitters' camps in wildlife reserves, and 32 of the 87 were officialised in 2026 alone in two mapping batches. A hunting camp and a children's camp are the same word in that file. WHAT THE SWEEP DID PRODUCE (f_4893, written into quebec-camp-landscape.md): seven children's camps that appear NOWHERE in this project -- CAMP HIAWATHA (Sainte-Agathe-des-Monts, 1984, origin recorded as MOHAWK, twenty kilometres from Kanawana and directly relevant to the naming argument in indigenous-names-and-land.md), Camp Olier, Camp de l'Avenir, Camp Aurelda, Village-des-Jeunes, Colonie de Granby and Camp Glen Emma -- plus OLD BREWERY MISSION registered as a camp at Wentworth-Nord in 1986, which puts Montreal's oldest homeless mission twenty kilometres west of Kanawana. And a caution: Camp Tamaracouta is not a registered camp at all, only its lake is, so presence in this file tracks nothing about a camp's size or age. STILL TO DO, and this is now the whole of this priority: fetch the fiches for Camp Olier, Camp de l'Avenir and CAMP HIAWATHA for their 'Origine et signification' notes, and search each name against the ACQ and CCA directories this project has already read. DONE 2026-09-06 (the fiche half). CAMP DE L'AVENIR: "Ce camp de vacances, situe sur la rive sud du LAC OUIMET, fut fonde en 1964 par les CLERCS DE SAINT-VIATEUR" -- a dated founding, a named order and a named lake for a camp three kilometres from Kanawana that appeared nowhere in this project. CAMP OLIER: named for Jean-Jacques Olier (Paris 1608-1657), founder of the Sulpicians and, with La Dauversiere and Chevrier, of the Societe de Notre-Dame de Montreal that founded Ville-Marie -- so the guess written into this priority was right and is now confirmed by the Commission. CAMP HIAWATHA, OLD BREWERY MISSION, CAMP MARIAN and CAMP AURELDA all return the Commission's standard 'origine... n'ont pu etre determinees'; Hiawatha's dataset classification is MOHAWK while its fiche disclaims the origin, the same split as Kanawana's ALGONQUIN (f_4878). Facts f_4894, f_4895; four fiches cached; quebec-camp-landscape.md 26 -> 28 sources. STILL OPEN: neither Olier nor l'Avenir has been searched against the ACQ and CCA directories already read here, and the Clercs de Saint-Viateur's own archives would date and describe l'Avenir properly. CLOSED 2026-09-06. The directory search was the missing half and it worked: BOTH CAMPS ARE IN THE JANUARY 1975 CCA DIRECTORY ALREADY CACHED IN THIS REPO, repeated in January 1976, under names nobody here had looked up. "OLIER (1954) -- M. COME LALANDE, PSS -- 60 GARCONS 12-16" at Ste-Anne des Lacs; PSS is PRETRES DE SAINT-SULPICE, so the camp was RUN BY the order Olier founded, not merely named for him. "HIAWATHA (1932) -- Mr. & Mrs. B. JACOBSON -- 85 BOYS 5-16, 85 GIRLS 5-16", season June 24-August 18 -- CO-ED FROM 1932, thirty-six years before Kanawana admitted girls and thirty-three before Kanawana declined an internal recommendation to. Facts f_4896, f_4897; written into quebec-camp-landscape.md with a cross-ref to coeducation-gender.md. RULE 7 AGAIN, THE HARD WAY: this was in a source this project had already read word for word, and it took the toponymic register to know what name to grep for. SPAWNED NOTHING NEW BUT WORTH NOTING: the de-officialised register renamed 'Lac des Freres' to LAC COME-LALANDE at Sainte-Anne-des-Lacs in 2005, almost certainly the same priest, and nothing read here says so.
priorities.source: toponymic register sweep, p_264 extension

priorities.description: DECIDE WHICH COPY OF THE DUPLICATED CACHE FILES IS CANONICAL, THEN COLLAPSE THEM. Measured 2026-09-06 (f_4900): of 921 non-empty files in sources/cache, 51 are byte-identical copies of another cached file, in 50 groups -- about six per cent of the corpus. sources/cache/green-triangle/ is entirely redundant: all 42 of its files have identical twins, none is unique, and only 5 source records point at it against 625 pointing at sources/cache/ymca-montreal-fonds/. sources/cache/brochures/ duplicates the fonds directory too. WHY IT MATTERS: a grep across the cache double-counts, so any 'appears in N issues' figure taken that way is inflated, and a coverage sweep of 'how many issues are cached' overstates -- 42 and 38 files across the two directories for 37 distinct Green Triangle issue dates. NOT DONE AUTONOMOUSLY, deliberately: these are cached primary texts, deleting them is hard to reverse, and the five source records pointing at the redundant paths would break. THE WORK, once someone says which side wins: repoint those five source records' cache_path to the surviving copy, delete the redundant files, and re-run data_integrity.py, whose new advisory reports the count and names the groups. Low risk, small diff, and it removes a trap that has already cost one verify pass an hour.
priorities.source: p_284 verify pass byproduct

priorities.description: FETCH THE PLATE IN THE 1899 ANNUAL REPORT CAPTIONED 'THE ASSOCIATION SUMMER CAMP, LAKE ST. JOSEPH.' The YMCA of Montreal's report for the year ending 30 April 1899 carries a photographic plate with that caption; the caption is all the cached OCR preserves and the page image has never been fetched (f_4910). It would be among the EARLIEST KNOWN PICTURES of the camp this project's history begins with, five years after the first season, and camp-otoreke.md's open questions ask for exactly this. THE ROUTE IS KNOWN AND CHEAP and is the one that worked on the 1900 manuscript on 2026-09-06: get the Internet Archive item id for the 1899 report, download its _jp2.zip, convert the pages to greyscale PNG with PIL, and read them by eye -- watching for leaves scanned 180 degrees, which happened on four of the eight leaves of the 1900 report. WHILE THERE, DO THE SAME FOR EVERY OTHER PRE-1911 ANNUAL REPORT: the OCR of these volumes preserves captions but not plates, so any photograph of the Lac St. Joseph camp in the 1894-1910 reports is invisible to every text search this project has ever run. That is a whole class of material nobody has looked for. ALSO WORTH READING PROPERLY WHILE IN THERE: these reports are marked read_state 'skimmed -- full-text-cached-and-keyword-swept-not-read-closely', and two short close reads on 2026-09-06 produced six facts nobody had (f_4902, f_4904 to f_4909). DONE for the 1899 plate, 2026-09-06, and A BETTER ROUTE THAN THE ONE THIS PRIORITY PROPOSED. Downloading the 45 MB _jp2.zip is unnecessary: archive.org/download/<id>/page/n<leaf>_w1600.jpg serves a single page as a 700 KB JPEG, PROVIDED you follow redirects (-L) and send a Referer of the item's details page -- without the Referer the earlier 302 looks like a dead end. And the LEAF NUMBER comes free from the item's _djvu.xml: split on <OBJECT>, join the <WORD> contents per page, and search; the djvu OBJECT index is 1-based while the page/nN endpoint is 0-based, so subtract one. The 1899 plate is on djvu leaf 15 = page n14. THE PHOTOGRAPH IS DESCRIBED at f_4914, cropped to assets/images/documents/1899-association-summer-camp-lake-st-joseph.jpg, registered in assets/images/credits.json as img_association_summer_camp_1899, and written into camp-otoreke.md. Four tents, a flagpole with a flag flying, and no building in frame -- stated as what the image shows, not what the site held. STILL OPEN, and this is now the whole of this priority: THE SAME SWEEP FOR EVERY OTHER PRE-1911 ANNUAL REPORT. Each one's _djvu.xml can be searched for plate captions in minutes, and any photograph in the 1894-1910 volumes is invisible to text search. One volume took about fifteen minutes end to end. SECOND PLATE FOUND 2026-09-06, AND A BETTER DETECTION METHOD THAN THE CAPTION SWEEP. Ranking an item's djvu pages by WORD COUNT and looking at the sparsest finds plates whose captions the OCR mangled, which the caption sweep (f_4917) cannot. That turned up the 1904 report -- 'MEN OF MONTREAL: Fifty-Third Annual Report AND SUMMER CAMP NUMBER, 1904' -- whose FRONT COVER is a halftone captioned 'CAMP CLUB HOUSE, LAKE ST. JOSEPH', showing the Log Club House with a dozen or more boys on its veranda and steps (f_4918, filed to assets/images/documents/). THE WHOLE 1904 VOLUME IS A CAMP SOURCE and was substantially unread: it gives the ELEVENTH ANNUAL summer camp opening 16 July 1904 under H. Ballantyne, which counts the first at 1894 in the association's own ordinal against the 1931 report's claim of 1898 (f_4919); the entire plant, programme, rates and committee (f_4920); and 'the Association also owns SEVERAL islands immediately adjoining', which with the 1901 auction purchase shows the holding still growing and is annotated onto c_008 (f_4921). REMAINING: 1894-95, 1895-96, 1896-97, 1897-98, 1900, 1901, 1903, 1905, 1906, 1907, 1908, 1909, 1910. The 1900, 1902 and 1907 djvu files are already downloaded to scratch; 1902 leaf 8 is a full-page plate whose OCR is noise and has NOT been looked at. SWEEP COMPLETED 2026-09-06 ACROSS ALL FOURTEEN PRE-1911 VOLUMES (f_4922). TWO CAMP PLATES EXIST AND BOTH ARE NOW RECOVERED: 1899 and the 1904 cover. Everything else is city work -- the 1903 report's photo montages (captions printed INSIDE the photographs, so no text search can ever see them), the 1906 report's class and staff plates, and the 1908 report's plates whose captions the OCR read upside down. 1907 and 1909 have no sparse pages at all. TWO FAILURE MODES OF THE METHOD ARE RECORDED AT f_4923: blank versos score the same as plates in the djvu word count (three did), and the fix is to measure the fetched image -- a blank leaf reads mean brightness ~237 with stdev <4 and no dark pixels, a halftone ~158 with stdev ~70 and about forty per cent dark. Measure before you look. STILL NOT READ: leaf 37 of the 1903 report, fetched and unexamined; it is very probably a third city montage. THIS PRIORITY IS ESSENTIALLY CLOSED for the pre-1911 annual reports. THE SAME METHOD HAS NOT BEEN RUN on the 1911-1960 reports, where Kanawana itself is the subject, and that is where it should go next. 1924-1930 SWEPT 2026-09-06 AND THE ANSWER IS NO (f_4924). All seven volumes of the decade in which Kamp Kanawana is a standing contents-page item have NO low-text interior pages at all -- every sparse page is a cover, a title page or the recurring 'THE Y.M.C.A. IN GREATER MONTREAL' display page. On this evidence the 1920s reports are not illustrated with photographs. The single caption found is a MONTREAL CITY MAP in the 1924 report, read upside down by the OCR, showing the building branches and the districts they serve -- not a camp map. THE LIMIT IS STATED IN THE FACT: this finds pages that are mostly picture, so a SMALL photograph set into a page of text is invisible to it and none of these pages has been looked at. REMAINING UNSWEPT: 1913-1923 and 1931-1960, about forty volumes. Given that the 1920s came back empty, the yield here now looks low and this should not be the next thing a session does; the earlier finds came from the 1899 and 1904 volumes, which are illustrated in a way the later ones are not.
priorities.source: p_253 close-reading campaign

priorities.description: READ THE REST OF FONG'S McCONNELL BIOGRAPHY THROUGH OPEN LIBRARY'S SEARCH-INSIDE ENDPOINT. One passage of a 700-page book has been read (f_4934, scan leaf 766) and it answered a question this project had recorded as a confirmed dead end. The endpoint (f_4933) can be pointed at the rest. SPECIFIC TARGETS, each a phrase to query: chapter 5 on the 1909 YMCA fundraising campaign, which this wiki has only from secondary summaries; 'Kanawana' again in other windows (the phrase returns hits on leaf 766 only so far, but 'Kamp Kanawana', 'Saint-Sauveur', 'St Sauveur', 'summer camp', 'Wilson Griffith', 'boys' work' and 'Y.M.C.A.' are untried); the McConnell Foundation's later dealings with the camp; and anything on the land purchase itself, since Fong's sentence does not say whether McConnell bought the lake or the whole site. METHOD: overlapping phrase queries, ~2s apart, joining the windows; cache each reconstruction under sources/cache/openlibrary-search-inside/ with the queries that produced it, as the two files there do. Every reconstruction is a reconstruction and must say so.
priorities.source: Open Library search-inside sweep, 2026-09-06 (f_4933)
priorities.notes: | RESOLVED 2026-09-06 for camp purposes. The Kanawana paragraph was walked out in both directions and is now complete (f_4934, extended). AND THE PHRASE 'Camp Kanawana' OCCURS ON EXACTLY ONE LEAF of Fong's seven-hundred-page book, so there is no rest of Fong to read for the camp. What the surround adds: Fong's own summary is 'although he never devoted himself full-time to the organization, McConnell's support for the Y was to continue through his life' -- more measured than the camp's literature -- and the purchase is an aside inside an argument about fundraising METHOD, the 1912 YMCA campaign having provided the model for McGill's. THE PRIORITY'S OTHER TARGETS -- chapter 5 on the 1909 campaign, 'Wilson Griffith', the McConnell Foundation's later dealings -- are about McConnell rather than the camp, and belong to j-w-mcconnell.md if anyone wants them; they are not camp research and are not pursued here.

priorities.description: SWEEP THE INTERNET ARCHIVE BOOK CORPUS FOR KANAWANA THROUGH OPEN LIBRARY, SYSTEMATICALLY. The first query ever run (2026-09-06) returned eight books containing 'Camp Kanawana' and several more containing 'Kanawana' alone, most of them unknown to this project. WHAT IS ALREADY IDENTIFIED AND NOT YET READ: (a) 'Le Quebec en plein air' (Quebec Amerique, 2016) -- 'ce camp existe toujours: c'est maintenant le camp Kanawana. En 1911, le Camp Nominingue, le premier camp...' which is a claim about the camp's own identity and predecessor and MUST be read out in full; (b) 'Les Laurentides, peintures et paysage' (1977) -- 'dans des colonies de vacances comme le camp Kanawana de la YMCA sont venus dormir sous la...'; (c) Michael Kutz, 'If, by miracle' (Azrieli Foundation, 2013) -- 'wheelchairs, as well as for diabetic children from Camp Kanawana', with an index entry 'Camp Kanawana, 87'; (d) 'Retenue par un fil' (Azrieli Foundation, 2013) -- 'il a pour sa part rejoint le camp Kanawana du YMCA. Il m'a ecrit de longues lettres decrivant...', a survivor's account of a boy at Kanawana, LETTERS FROM CAMP described in a published memoir; (e) Mike Gutwillig, 'My Canada-Such a Mechiah!' (1967) -- 'if you were really fortunate, getting Camp Kanawana or Tameracouta for two weeks'; (f) L. Ian MacDonald, 'Politics, people & potpourri' (2009) -- 'she recently went on a five-day canoe trip at Camp Kanawana'. QUERY VARIANTS STILL UNTRIED: 'Kamp Kanawana', 'Kanawanna', 'Camp Kanawanna', 'Lake Kanawana', 'Lac Kanawana', 'Kanawana, Que', and the camp's people by name.
priorities.source: Open Library search-inside sweep, 2026-09-06 (f_4933)
priorities.notes: 2026-09-06: TWO OF THE SIX BOOKS ARE DONE. (c) Michael Kutz, 'If, By Miracle' -- the passage read out and written into programs-activities.md; the Knights of Pythias, the Montreal Children's Hospital, and diabetic children FROM Camp Kanawana, which is a programme nothing else in this project records (f_4938). (d) Judy Abrams, 'Retenue par un fil' -- read out and written into postwar-gap.md; a boy at Kanawana in the early or mid 1950s writing her long letters about his canoe trips, which is the first evidence this project has that camper letters from the empty decade were ever written (f_4937). He is not named in the recovered text and nothing is inferred. STILL TO READ: (a) 'Le Quebec en plein air' (2016), which makes a claim about the camp's own identity and a predecessor -- 'ce camp existe toujours: c'est maintenant le camp Kanawana. En 1911, le Camp Nominingue, le premier camp...' -- and is the highest-value of the four left; (b) 'Les Laurentides, peintures et paysage' (1977); (e) Mike Gutwillig, 'My Canada-Such a Mechiah!' (1967); (f) L. Ian MacDonald, 'Politics, people & potpourri' (2009). The query variants listed in this priority are also still untried. | 2026-09-06, later: (a) 'Le Quebec en plein air' also done, and it is not a find but a WARNING. Larue and Belec write 'Connu longtemps sous le nom d'Otoreke, ce camp existe toujours: c'est maintenant le camp Kanawana' -- right about the institution, wrong about the site, and it erases Camp Otoreke's 1910-1982 life at Lac Saint-Joseph. Written into camp-otoreke.md so the correction travels with the sentence, because a mainstream Quebec press title is what a researcher reaches first. The same page dates Camp Nominingue to 1911 against the QCA directory's 1925; queried, not corrected, in quebec-camp-landscape.md. Fact f_4939. THREE BOOKS LEFT: 'Les Laurentides, peintures et paysage' (1977), Gutwillig's 'My Canada-Such a Mechiah!' (1967), and MacDonald's 'Politics, people & potpourri' (2009).
priorities.resolution: ALL SIX BOOKS READ OUT. Kutz (diabetic children from Camp Kanawana, the Knights of Pythias and the Montreal Children's Hospital, f_4938) and Abrams (a boy's long letters home about canoe trips, early or mid 1950s, f_4937) went into programs-activities.md and postwar-gap.md. Larue and Belec's 'Le Quebec en plein air' went into camp-otoreke.md as a WARNING rather than a find, because its sentence 'ce camp existe toujours: c'est maintenant le camp Kanawana' is right about the institution and wrong about the site and erases Otoreke's 1910-1982 life (f_4939). The remaining three -- the 1977 exhibition catalogue 'Les Laurentides, peintures et paysage', Gutwillig's 'My Canada -- Such a Mechiah!' (1967) and MacDonald's 'Politics, People & Potpourri' (2009) -- add NOTHING about how the camp ran and are recorded anyway, in a new section of meta/sources-index.md, for what they show about the name: none of the three explains what Kanawana is, and in two of them it stands for camp-going in general rather than for itself (f_4940). That is a kind of evidence this project has almost none of -- not what the camp did, but what its name meant to somebody who was not there. THE QUERY VARIANTS LISTED IN THIS PRIORITY ARE STILL UNTRIED and are the natural next sweep: 'Kamp Kanawana', 'Kanawanna', 'Lake Kanawana', 'Lac Kanawana', 'Kanawana, Que', and the camp's people by name. A sweep on people's names is the one most likely to pay, on the evidence of how the Roy Locke obituary turned up.

priorities.description: KANAWANA HAD ITS OWN POST OFFICE, AND THE ALMANACS DATE IT. Found incidentally 2026-09-06 in the Open Library sweep. The Post Office Department's annual report for 1915 lists under mail service 'Kanawana - St. Sauveur des Mont[s]' among railway-station and mail-catch points; a Sessional Paper lists 'Kanawana (summer office) P.Q.'; the Canadian Almanac's post-office tables carry 'Kanawana' in a run of entries between Kananaskis and Kandahar in at least two editions; and a modern gazetteer indexes 'Kanawana, UP (Que.) 18 F4' -- UP being an unincorporated place. SO THE CAMP, OR THE PLACE, WAS A POST OFFICE OF THE DOMINION OF CANADA, seasonal at least in part. NOTHING IN THIS WIKI SAYS SO. What to establish: the opening and closing dates (the Canadian Almanac ran annually and the postal guides are on the Internet Archive, so the run can be walked year by year); whether it was a summer office only; who the postmaster was, since almanac tables often name them; and what the mail route was. Library and Archives Canada holds the Post Office Department's post-office and postmaster records, which give exact opening and closing dates for every Canadian post office, and that is the authority. This bears on the camp's dating: a post office implies a settled seasonal population and an address. || CHARACTERISED 2026-09-06 (f_5213): LAC's Collection Search is behind a **CLOUDFLARE JAVASCRIPT CHALLENGE** -- 403 with `cf-mitigated: challenge` and a 'Just a moment...' body -- not a policy refusal. Same mechanism as HathiTrust's babel and the same class as Concordia's AtoM challenge. NOBODY IS REFUSING THIS PROJECT; this environment cannot solve a JS challenge because its browser dies at the proxy tunnel. A PERSON WITH AN ORDINARY BROWSER REACHES IT IN ONE CLICK, and no letter or permission is needed. The federal open-data CKAN API does answer (200) but publishes only LAC's ADMINISTRATIVE datasets -- 71 of them, none collection-level -- so it is not a substitute.
priorities.source: Open Library search-inside sweep, 2026-09-06 (f_4933)
priorities.resolution: THE EXISTENCE IS ESTABLISHED AND WRITTEN UP; THE DATES ARE NOT. All four sources were read out of the full djvu text rather than left at the snippet: the Post Office Department's 1914-15 annual report (Kanawana in 'Non-Accounting Post Offices -- Revenue, Salaries and Allowances', with NO opened/closed letter prefix, so already running and not closed that year; and the mail-transportation route 'Kanawana -- St. Sauveur des Mont[s]' in the Montreal Division), the Sessional Papers for 1919 ('Kanawana (summer office) P.Q.', the parenthesis being the Department's own and used there for Kahshe Lake and Kawartha Park), and the Canadian Almanac's 'Post Offices and Railroad Stations in Canada' in BOTH the 1917 and 1918 editions (edition years read from the running headers, since the Internet Archive metadata gives the series start date of 1848 for both). Written into the-kanawana-site.md, with a footnote in places-and-locations.md: the earlier assumption that 'P.O.' on the camp map meant Post Office was wrong about the map and right about the institution, and the map correction stands. Three source records, three cache files each headed by what could NOT be read from it -- the revenue and allowance figures on Kanawana's row, and the almanac's railway columns, are OCR column runs that cannot be aligned to their rows with any confidence. Fact f_4936. STILL OPEN, and this is what the priority should now be read as: the opening and closing dates, the postmaster's name, and whether the office served the camp alone or a wider seasonal settlement. Library and Archives Canada's Post Offices and Postmasters database answers all three and REFUSED THIS PROJECT AT THE NETWORK GATEWAY, HTTP 403 -- an access failure, not an absence. Untried: bac-lac.gc.ca through a different path, the Post Office Department's other annual reports year by year on the Internet Archive (the 1914-15 volume was downloadable in full, so the series probably is), and the Canadian Almanac's other editions, which would bracket the office by their own presence and absence. || EXTENDED 2026-09-06 the same day: three more Canadian Almanac editions found -- 1943, and two of the 1950s -- so the office is documented from at least 1915 to about 1955, forty years, not to 1918. The 1943 row's columns are legible where 1917's and 1918's were not: "Kanawana ... Terrebonne ... Q | St. Sauveur 529 or Piedmont 535", with no population figure, which marks an unincorporated place. The two 1950s volumes carry no legible year; one prints calendars for 1951-52 and the other for 1954-55, and they are dated no closer than that. The remaining question is unchanged and is now sharper: LAC's Post Offices and Postmasters database would give the exact opening and closing dates and the postmasters' names, and it refuses this environment at the gateway. || OPENING DATE BRACKETED 2026-09-06, WITHOUT LAC. The Universal Postal Union's Dictionnaire des bureaux de poste (Lausanne, November 1909) lists every member country's post offices as at 1 March 1909 and does NOT contain Kanawana; its Supplement of August 1912, Part I 'Bureaux a ajouter', does, as 'Canada, Quebec'. So the office opened between March 1909 and June 1912, across the YMCA's 1910 purchase of the site. Fact f_4944. Two reading traps recorded in the cache file: the Internet Archive dates the whole item 1909, which at face value would put the office before the YMCA arrived; and the scan splits names and countries into separate column runs, so the alignment was checked against Kanawyer, a real place in California, rather than assumed. WHAT REMAINS: the exact opening date, the closing date, the postmaster's name, and the catchment. LAC's Post Offices and Postmasters database still answers all four and still returns 403 at the gateway. TWO NEW ROUTES from the same sweep, both unrestricted on the Internet Archive and neither tried: the 'Guide officiel du service postal Canadien, 1917' (item guideofficieldus00cana), which should give the office's particulars in a Canadian rather than an international source; and the McGraw-Hill Directory and Almanac of Canada, 1966 (three items), which cross-references 'Kanawana, PQ, see St-Sauveur-des-Monts, PQ' and may date the closure. || 2026-09-06, the Canadian side: the Guide officiel du service postal Canadien 1917 is done. It carries Kanawana twice -- the national alphabetical list, and 'Bureaux de poste dans la province de Quebec, arranges suivant les districts electoraux' under TERREBONNE -- which dates the Terrebonne attribution to 1917 rather than 1943 and puts the office among Entrelac, Fourteen Island Lake, Ivry Nord, Lac Charlebois, Lac Duhamel, Lac Echo, Lac Guindon, Lac Manitou Sud and Lac Marois, all Laurentian cottage places. The dagger and asterisk prefixes in those lists were NOT decoded: the legend was not found in the front matter, Kanawana carries no prefix in either list, and the symbols are not interpreted. Remaining route from this sweep: the three McGraw-Hill Directory and Almanac of Canada 1966 items, which cross-reference 'Kanawana, PQ, see St-Sauveur-des-Monts, PQ' and may date the CLOSURE, which is now the only end of the run still open. || 2026-09-06, the bracket narrowed again: Rand McNally's Indexed Pocket Map and Shippers' Guide of Quebec for 1911 (unrestricted, downloaded whole) carries "Kanawana, Terrebonne, (Summer P. O.)". So the office existed BY 1911, not merely by June 1912, and it opened either just before or just after the YMCA bought the site in 1910. That entry also puts 'summer' on the office eight years earlier than the Sessional Papers of 1919. WHAT IS LEFT: the exact opening date, the CLOSING date, and the postmaster. The closing is now the only end of the run genuinely open -- the office is documented to about 1955 in the Canadian Almanac -- and the McGraw-Hill Directory and Almanac of Canada 1966, which cross-references 'Kanawana, PQ, see St-Sauveur-des-Monts, PQ', is the untried source most likely to date it.
priorities.notes: 2026-09-06, THE McGRAW-HILL ROUTE TRIED AND NOT USABLE AS IT STANDS -- recorded so the next session does not repeat it or, worse, use it. The McGraw-Hill Directory and Almanac of Canada, 1966, carries "Kanawana, PQ, see St-Sauveur-des-Monts, PQ" in at least two of its Internet Archive copies (mcgrawhilldirect0000unse leaf 874, _f4f5 leaf 882). Its neighbours run "Kananaskis, Alta, see Exshaw, Alta CP / Kanasuta, PQ, see Arntfield, PQ ON / Kanata, Ont O / Kandahar, Sask S CP", so the trailing letters are railway codes and the list is of PLACES WITH THEIR RAIL SERVICE, not of post offices as such. THE LIST'S OWN HEADING WAS NOT RECOVERED, and without it the 'see' cannot be read as evidence that the post office had closed -- it may mean only that the place was served through St-Sauveur-des-Monts. NOTHING IS RECORDED AS A FACT FROM IT. A third copy, mcgrawhilldirect0000unse_j6s5, returns the same alphabetical run WITHOUT Kanawana ("Kanaka, BC CP / Kempt..."), which is either a different edition or a two-column layout the OCR has interleaved; that too is unresolved. To use this source, recover the heading of the list first. | 2026-09-06: THE CLOSING BRACKET IS FOUND, and this priority is now half-answered. The McGraw-Hill Directory and Almanac of Canada, mid-1960s, carries "Kanawana, PQ, see St-Sauveur-des-Monts, PQ" in a list headed "POST OFFICES IN CANADA (Sub post offices and closed and renamed post offices appear in italics. The correct postal address for each closed post office appears immediately below the closed post office name.)" -- so Kanawana is in the italicised class and its mail goes to Saint-Sauveur. Against the Canadian Almanac's run of the office to about 1955, THE OFFICE ENDED BETWEEN ABOUT 1955 AND THE MID-1960s (f_4954). TWO THINGS IT DOES NOT SAY: which of the three italicised categories applies -- the name was never changed, so it is closed or reduced to a sub-office, and the list cannot distinguish them -- and the year of the volume, because the Internet Archive dates FOUR different printings of this series 1966 and no internal year was recovered. WHAT REMAINS: the exact date, the postmaster, and whether the office served the camp or a wider settlement. Library and Archives Canada's Post Offices and Postmasters database answers all three in one lookup and still refuses this project at the gateway (HTTP 403). THIS IS NOW A ONE-LOOKUP HUMAN TASK for anyone with ordinary browser access.

priorities.description: IDENTIFY THE KANAWANA DIRECTOR IN WHO'S WHO IN CANADA 1965. Found 2026-09-06 through Open Library search-inside, item whoswhoincanada0000unse_r1d7, scan leaf 1546: '...Association of Canada. Clubs: Kimberley Ski (President, 1960); Redbirds Ski; Kamp Kanawana (YMCA), Director[.]' The subject's NAME was not recovered -- Who's Who entries run long and the name sits at the head, beyond the reach of the phrase-walking used here. Redbirds is the McGill ski club and Kimberley Ski Club is in British Columbia, so this is a McGill man who was president of a BC ski club in 1960 and a director of Kamp Kanawana. He is not obviously any of the directors this wiki holds for the 1960s (Seaman 1959-68), so 'Director' here may mean a member of the camp's governing committee rather than the camp's director -- which would itself be new, since this project has almost no committee names for the period. ROUTES: borrow the volume (a human with an Internet Archive account can, for an hour); query more phrases from the same leaf to walk backwards to the name; or find the same man in an adjacent Who's Who edition where the OCR breaks differently.
priorities.source: Open Library search-inside sweep, 2026-09-06 (f_4933)
priorities.notes: | RESOLVED 2026-09-06. The name is OWEN ERNEST OWENS, Ph.D., Vice-President for Exploration at Cominco, born Montreal 30 March 1925, educated at St. George's Montreal and Westmount High School with three McGill degrees to a 1955 doctorate, listed under CLUBS as 'Kamp Kanawana (YMCA), Director, 1965' (f_4971). TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS PRIORITY'S OWN TEXT. (1) THE ITEM IS NOT LENDING-RESTRICTED. This priority worked it through search-inside snippets; the whole 5 MB djvu text downloads freely, and 'Kanawana' occurs exactly once in the volume. THE ZEROTH STEP APPLIES TO RESTRICTION TOO: check archive.org/metadata/<id> before assuming a walk is necessary. (2) THE VOLUME IS NOT 'WHO'S WHO IN CANADA 1965'. The Internet Archive dates it 1911 (the series start) and the entry's own latest datum is February 1976, so it is 1976 or later. The '1965' in the snippet is the year of his Kanawana directorship; the words 'IN CANADA' beside it are a running head. AND A BEARING ON ANOTHER ARTICLE: his only son is DAVID NORREY, which corroborates reading O. N. H. Owens as 'Owen NORREYS Harrington' -- order-of-owens.md's Open Question 1 -- without proving it. A Montreal birth record for 30 March 1925 would name his father and settle it.

priorities.description:
SWEEP THE INTERNET ARCHIVE BOOK CORPUS ON THE CAMP'S PEOPLE AND ITS OTHER NAMES, not on 'Camp Kanawana'. The first name sweep, run 2026-09-06 on a handful of names, produced three finds in about twenty minutes and two of them were invisible to any query containing the phrase 'Camp Kanawana': Stuart McLean's own account of the camp in The Vinyl Cafe Notebooks (f_4941), found by pairing 'Kanawana' with 'Sir George Williams'; the Kanawana Outing Club described in the 1976 guidebook Montreal Inside Out (f_4942), found the same way; and W. H. Spearman as 'Manager, Beaver Club, Spring Garden' in the 1943 Canadian Almanac, a Montreal post this project did not have (logged in p_238). NAMES NOT YET SWEPT: every director in directors-index.md; Hedley S. Dimock; T. Duncan Patton; Murray B. Shantz; Ralph Dawson; R. L. Charlton; O. N. H. Owens; Nelson McEwen; James H. Turner; Leo J. Robitaille; G. David Twynam; Bruce and Jay Netherwood; and the Kanawana Committee chairmen. TWO LEADS ALREADY OPEN FROM THE FIRST PASS: Henry Foss Hall, 'The Georgian Spirit: The Story of Sir George Williams University' (1967), which thanks 'my friend, Mr. Harold C. Cross, dedicated professional leader and historian' -- so the SGW history was written with the Montreal YMCA historian's own research and records, and it has not been searched for the camp; and the International Council of Religious Education Yearbook 1936, which lists 'President -- Harold C. Cross, 1441 Drummond St., Montreal', a dated 1936 office for Cross that this project does not hold, and which is NOT lending-restricted so it can be downloaded whole. OTHER NAME FORMS UNTRIED for the camp itself: 'Kamp Kanawana', 'Kanawanna', 'Lake Kanawana', 'Lac Kanawana', 'Kanawana, Que'.

AMENDMENT 2026-09-06, AND THIS IS NOW A WORKLIST RATHER THAN A PROPOSAL. The sweep was finally run PROPERLY: every earlier pass searched the phrase "Camp Kanawana" and got eight books; a bare "Kanawana" returns SEVENTY-SIX. About half are noise -- a different Kanawana in South American ethnography, and OCR garbage in Japanese dictionaries -- and the Canadian ones are listed here by group, with the item id, so nobody has to run the enumeration again.

ALREADY DONE (do not redo): jwmcconnellfinan0000fong (f_4934) · canadianobituary0000stam_b1t2 (f_4935) · ifbymiracle0000kutz (f_4938) · retenueparunfil0000unse (f_4937) · lequbecenpleinai0000laru (f_4939) · leslaurentidespe0000unse, mycanadasuchmech0000mike, politicspeoplepo0000macd (f_4940) · vinylcafenoteboo0000mcle (f_4941) · montralinsideo00buxt (f_4942) · n24annualreport1915cana, n08sessionalpaper54canauoft, the five canadianalmanacd0000unse_* volumes (f_4936) · dictionnairedesb00univ (f_4944) · whoswhoincanada0000unse_r1d7 (p_429, name not recovered).

STILL TO READ, in the order I would take them:

1. FIVE SUMMER-CAMP DIRECTORIES, 1983 to 2008, which on the pattern of the 1975 and 1976 national directories will each give Kanawana's capacity, ages, fees, session structure and DIRECTOR for a year this project is thin on: summercampsprogr0000gold (1983) · guidetosummercam0000unse (1983-84) · guidetosummercam0000port (1987) · canadiansummerjo0000unse (2006) · canadiansummerjo0000unse_q4r4 (2008). The 1983 and 1987 volumes fall inside the 1980s, which between-centennials.md calls the second thin decade.

2. FOUR CANADIAN KEY BUSINESS DIRECTORIES, 1994, 1997, 1999 and 2000 (canadiankeybusin1994unse, 1997, 1999, canadiankeybusin2000unse). The 1999 volume already showed, in a snippet, "Y M C A de Montreal Kamp Kanawana Div Of 1441 rue Drummond" with named officers beside it. FOUR YEARS OF NAMED OFFICERS FOR THE 1990s, which is the decade this project has least of.

3. TWO MORE POSTAL SOURCES, both unrestricted: guideofficieldus00cana, the Guide officiel du service postal Canadien 1917, which should give the office's particulars in a Canadian source; and the three McGraw-Hill Directory and Almanac of Canada 1966 items (mcgrawhilldirect0000unse, _v4j7, _f4f5), which cross-reference "Kanawana, PQ, see St-Sauveur-des-Monts, PQ" and may date the closure. See p_428.

4. THREE OUTDOOR GUIDES that bear on the Outing Club and the trails: lespistesdeskide0000veil, 'Les pistes de ski de fond au Quebec' (1977), ONE YEAR AFTER the Montreal Inside Out entry at f_4942 and likely fuller · guidepleinairque0000unse (1991) · atlasroutierduqu0000mapa (2001).

5. TWO EARLY ONES worth a look for their own sake: highschoolmagazi00high, 'The High School Magazine, Montreal, Canada' (1916) -- a Montreal school magazine naming Kanawana six years after the camp arrived, and the only schoolboy-audience source in the list; and randmcnallycosin00rand, Rand McNally's indexed pocket map and shippers' guide (1911), which would put Kanawana on a commercial map in the year after the purchase.

6. THREE POSSIBLE MEMOIRS, unexamined: moonwastiredofwa0000belt (1992) · dearsamgrievingd0000jane (2007) · boxfrombraunauin0000elvi (2009). Also guidepetitfuteci0000coll, the Petit Fute Montreal city guide 2011-12, and swimmingwatersaf0000unse (1995) and basiccampmanagem0000ball_r5m1 (2012), both of which may simply cite the camp as an example.

NAME QUERIES: the name sweep proper is barely started. 'Hedley S. Dimock' returns 235 hits because he wrote the movement's textbooks, so pair names with 'Montreal' or 'Y.M.C.A.' or with 'Kanawana' itself. Directors not yet swept: every name in directors-index.md. Two leads already open are in the note field. [THE THREE CARRIED-OVER ITEMS ARE CLOSED 2026-09-06, ALL AS FALSE FRIENDS OR NEAR-MISSES, and the sweep that closed them turned up a bigger problem. moonwastiredofwa0000belt: 'Kanawana' there is THE TAPIRAPE TERM FOR THUNDER -- a whole cluster of the 76 is that same word in South American ethnography, and one item says so outright. swimmingwatersaf0000unse: 'Kanawana Magazine' is an OCR ERROR FOR KANAWA MAGAZINE of the Canadian Recreational Canoeing Association, checked by a separate query returning 20 items, not assumed. atlasroutierduqu0000mapa: genuinely ours but only a ROAD-ATLAS MAP LABEL for lac-des-Kanawana, carrying nothing about the camp. THE BIGGER PROBLEM, f_4998: THE OPEN LIBRARY SEARCH-INSIDE API PAGES AND THIS PROJECT HAD NEVER PAGED IT. A query reports total 76 and RETURNS TWENTY; the parameter is &page=N, and &from= and &offset= are accepted and silently ignored. The figure 76 has been carried since the capability was found and was being worked from its first page. All four pages are now enumerated with registration status and a snippet each, at sources/cache/openlibrary-search-inside/2026-09-06-all-76-kanawana-items-enumerated.txt. THE REASSURING HALF: every item in the 76 that is actually about the camp was ALREADY REGISTERED. The first page had the substance. REMAINING IN THIS PRIORITY: only the ~50 unswept names in the name-sweep log -- and note that any earlier name sweep run through this API saw one page per name, so a name that returned 'nothing relevant' may simply have had its relevant hit on page 2.] || WORKED 2026-09-06 (evening). NAME FORMS FOR THE CAMP ARE NOW EXHAUSTED, and the nulls are logged so nobody runs them again: 'Kanawanna' 0, 'Lac Kanawana' 0, 'Kanawana, Que' 0, 'Lake Kanawana' 1 (Stuart McLean's Vinyl Cafe Notebooks, already held). 'OTOREKE' -- WHICH THIS PRIORITY DID NOT LIST -- returns 15 and had never been run; it produced four new sources and f_5196 through f_5200. PEOPLE: the first name swept was O. N. H. OWENS (4 hits) and it paid, giving his day job and his leading given name (f_5204). THE QUERY THAT WORKED WAS THE INDEX FORM 'Owens, O. N. H.', not the running form -- directories and indexes invert the name, and the running form returns the company entries but not the man's own. USE THE INDEX FORM FIRST for every remaining name. STILL UNSWEPT and these are the next ones: 'McGerrigle' (346 hits, needs pairing), 'Duncan Patton' (107), 'Hedley S. Dimock' (269), plus Murray B. Shantz, Ralph Dawson, R. L. Charlton, Nelson McEwen, James H. Turner, Leo J. Robitaille, G. David Twynam, the Netherwoods, and the two names surfaced today, DORIS ROBERTSON (the 1936 linocut) and RONALD HUPFIELD. || SECOND PASS SAME DAY, index-form queries, totals recorded so nobody re-runs them: 'Shantz, Murray B.' 0, 'Robitaille, Leo J.' 0, 'Netherwood, Bruce' 0 -- CLEAN NULLS, those three men are in no digitized book. 'Twynam, G. David' 2, both false friends (a transport-planning report index and a leisure-research author index). 'McEwen, Nelson' 13, NOT YET INSPECTED. 'Patton, T. Duncan' 9 and it PAID -- see f_5205: two published books corroborate the first-basketball-game roster the article had only from web sources, and ROB RAINS'S JAMES NAISMITH (Temple University Press, 2009) INDEXES PATTON ON FIVE PAGES, 28/35/45/60/192, none of them recovered because the book is lending-restricted and its running text uses the surname alone, which the window-walking method cannot reach. THAT IS A NAMED UNREAD SOURCE, not a dead end: a library copy settles it. 'Dimock, Hedley S.' 272 and 'Robertson, Doris' 121 are too many unpaired and need a second term. STILL UNSWEPT: Ralph Dawson, R. L. Charlton, James H. Turner, Ronald Hupfield, and the Kanawana Committee chairmen. || THIRD PASS: 'Charlton, R. L.' (24) PAID -- see f_5206, the Point St. Charles Institute's 1895 benefactors page. 'Robertson, Doris M.' (1) is a false friend, a Boston residents list, and three web searches for her found only other artists; the null is logged inside f_5197 with the untried archives named. STILL UNSWEPT AND HIGH-COUNT, needing a pairing term rather than a bare name: 'Dawson, Ralph' 551, 'Dimock, Hedley' 468, 'Turner, James H.' 447, 'Hupfield' 663.

priorities.notes: 2026-09-06: ONE OF THE TWO LEADS IN THIS PRIORITY IS DONE. The International Council of Religious Education Yearbook 1936 was downloaded whole (it is not lending-restricted) and gives Harold C. Cross as PRESIDENT OF THE RELIGIOUS EDUCATION COUNCIL OF THE PROVINCE OF QUEBEC, at 1441 Drummond Street -- the first thing anyone has found in the ten-year hole between his Kanawana directorship and the 1938 memo (f_4943). 'Kanawana' does not occur anywhere in that volume. OTHER YEARS OF THE SAME YEARBOOK SERIES ARE UNTRIED and would bracket his presidency. The second lead, Henry Foss Hall's 'The Georgian Spirit' (1967), is NOT settled: a paired query on 'Kanawana' with 'Georgian spirit' returned nothing, but that pairing requires the book to use its own title in its text, so it is not a null about the camp. It needs a direct query on distinctive phrases from that book. ALSO FOUND IN PASSING: the McGraw-Hill Directory cross-references 'Kanawana, PQ, see St-Sauveur-des-Monts, PQ', which is a fourth kind of source confirming Kanawana as a mapped place name (p_428). | 2026-09-06: two of the worklist's postal items are done -- the UPU Dictionnaire (f_4944) and the Guide officiel du service postal 1917 (folded into f_4936). A CAUTION for whoever takes the Canadian Key Business Directories: the officer names visible in a snippet beside the Kanawana line belong to whatever entry the page sets next to it, not necessarily to the YMCA division. A directory page packs many companies, and adjacency in a twelve-word window is not attribution. Walk the entry from its own heading or leave the names alone. | 2026-09-06, group 1 begun and NOT finished. 'Summer Camps & Programs' (1983) gives Kanawana a TWO-PAGE entry, pp. 172-173, and the head of it is read: 190 boys and girls aged 7-19, both addresses and both phone numbers matching the 1975-76 national directories, and a Director field reading 'Louis Jean' (f_4945, conflict c_065). THE WALK STOPPED AT THE FEES because the endpoint began returning non-JSON under rate limiting -- two printed pages remain unrecovered, and they may carry the fuller name that would settle c_065. RESUME THERE, more slowly. The other four directories in group 1 are untouched, and the two Porter Sargent guides (1983-84 and 1987) both carry Kanawana in their Canadian camp lists. THREE MORE MEMOIRS surfaced from the query 'Kamp Kanawana' that the bare-'Kanawana' listing did not make obvious: dearsamgrievingd0000jane, 'Dear Sam: Grieving the Death of My Son' (2007), whose subject was a CIT and counsellor at the camp and whose funeral drew 'counselors and kids from Kamp Kanawana' -- HANDLE WITH CARE, see the separate note in this priority; and boxfrombraunauin0000elvi, 'The Box from Braunau' (2009), 'that summer, Dad and Georgie went off to Kamp Kanawana, a YMCA camp located on a remote lake', indexed at page 24. | 2026-09-06 later: GROUP 1 IS THREE-FIFTHS DONE. 'Summer Camps & Programs' (1983) finished on a slower second pass -- sessions, fees ($370 residential / $385 wilderness per fortnight), 1,000 acres, and the bilingual sentence (f_4945). BOTH PORTER SARGENT GUIDES done, 1983-84 and 1987 (f_4946): they name PETER G. GODDARD and JAY NETHERWOOD respectively, print 'Est. 1894' twice, and carry The Voyageurs Program as fourteen-day wilderness canoe tripping for teenagers 13-18. c_065 is now heavily weighted toward Goddard and stays open only because 'Louis Jean' still needs accounting for. STILL TO DO in group 1: the two Canadian Summer Job Directories, 2006 and 2008, whose snippets already show a fuller job description and a changed address, 1435 rue Drummond rather than 1441. RATE LIMITING IS REAL: the endpoint returns non-JSON in bursts under a two-second sleep. Six seconds between calls works; when it starts refusing, wait thirty to forty seconds rather than retrying immediately. | 2026-09-06: GROUP 1 IS COMPLETE. All five summer-camp and summer-job directories are read: Summer Camps & Programs 1983 (f_4945), Porter Sargent 1983-84 and 1987 (f_4946), and the Canadian Summer Job Directory 2006 and 2008 (f_4947). Between them they gave the 1980s three directory entries where the article had none, corroborated two directors from outside the YMCA's files, carried the Voyageurs programme a decade further with a stated shape, and added three rows to the acreage table -- one of which, 500 in 2006 against 550 in 2008 in identical copy, dates the arrival of the figure the YMCA uses now. GROUPS 2 TO 6 REMAIN, and group 2 (the four Canadian Key Business Directories) carries the standing caution about attributing officer names from adjacency. | 2026-09-06: group 5's Rand McNally 1911 is done and was worth more than its group placing suggested -- "Kanawana, Terrebonne, (Summer P. O.)" narrows the post office's opening bracket to 1911 and dates the 'summer' description eight years earlier than anything this project had (f_4936, f_4944). ALSO ATTEMPTED AND NOT SETTLED: group 4's ski guides. 'Les pistes de ski de fond au Quebec' (1977) contains 'Kanawana' somewhere but no query yet run has returned a window centred on it, and the 1991 'Guide plein air Quebec' returns a line -- 'Domaine des Prte 932.7161 Mont-Laurier Kanawana 819.623.5258 Saint-Sauveur Y CountryCamp 849.5331 Huberdeau' -- whose COLUMN ALIGNMENT IS AMBIGUOUS in exactly the way the UPU dictionary's was. An 819 area code is Mont-Laurier, not Saint-Sauveur, and 849.5331 is the YMCA's Drummond Street number, so the columns are certainly scrambled. NOTHING FROM EITHER BOOK IS RECORDED, and nothing should be until the alignment is worked out against a control the way Kanawyer served as one for the UPU list. | 2026-09-06: group 5's second item done. The High School Magazine (Montreal, 1916) is NOT lending-restricted and carries a Kamp Kanawana ADVERTISEMENT giving the 1916 season (24 June to 12 August) and the fee ($5.00 a week), which extends the fee series back two years and shows a sixty per cent wartime rise to the $8.00 of 1918 (f_4948). A LEAD DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN: the article printed immediately before the advertisements is 'A Week in the Woods', an unsigned canoe-trip narrative naming Lac Diable, Lac Cypres, Lac Daby, Lac Clef, Lac Caribou, Lac Boisfranc, Lac Bois, Lac Batiment and Lake McLaren, and mentioning a 'dining pavilion' and an 'Old Guard'. It names no camp and no YMCA. An advertisement's position is bought, not editorial. IF SOMEONE CAN PLACE THAT ROUTE against Kanawana's known trip country -- the 1920s brochures and the Gas Bag runs would do it -- the question reopens, and a 1916 first-person camper narrative would be the earliest this project holds by a decade. | 2026-09-06, THE TEST I SET WAS RUN THE SAME HOUR AND HALF-ANSWERED. The 'A Week in the Woods' route is now PLACED: five of its nine lakes fall in one block in the Lac-Legendre and Saint-Donat country of Matawinie, about seventy-two kilometres north of Kanawana, with Lac Batiment and Lac McLaren each UNIQUE IN THE PROVINCE as the control (f_4948). Two of the names return nothing anywhere and are probably OCR manglings. That does NOT settle whose trip it was, and the attribution stays unmade. THE REMAINING TEST IS NARROW AND CHEAP: none of the nine names appears anywhere in this project's source cache outside the file recording them, so search the 1920s brochures, the Gas Bag runs and the directors' reports for SAINT-DONAT, LAC-LEGENDRE, LAC BATIMENT, LAC McLAREN or the ROUGE-MATAWIN. One hit attributes a 1916 first-person camper narrative to the camp; no hits leave it where it is, which is honest either way. CAPABILITY NOTE: geogratis.gc.ca/services/geoname/en/geonames.json?q=<name>&province=24 answers a plain GET with name, municipality, RCM and coordinates, and is a faster route than the Commission de toponymie's fiches when the question is WHERE rather than WHY A NAME. | 2026-09-06, AND THE REMAINING TEST WAS RUN TOO: NEGATIVE, SO THE LEAD IS CLOSED. The cache was searched for Saint-Donat, St. Donat, St-Donat, Legendre, Matawin and Rouge-Matawin, and no Kanawana source names any of them -- the hits are other camps' addresses in the 1975 directory, a 1968 camp at St. Donat, and a person called Esther Legendre in the 1988 annual report. 'A Week in the Woods' is NOT attributable to Kanawana on anything this project holds, and f_4948 says so. Do not reopen it without a Kanawana document naming that country. THE ADVERTISEMENT IS UNAFFECTED and stands as the finding from that magazine. | 2026-09-06: GROUP 2 IS COMPLETE AND THE STANDING CAUTION WAS RIGHT. All four Canadian Key Business Directories name Kamp Kanawana as a division of the Y M C A de Montreal at 1441 rue Drummond, and five MORE volumes of the same directory (1993, 1995, 1998, 2001 and one undated) carry the association entry without the camp's name -- do not read the on-off pattern as history, it is OCR or the publisher's rotating detail. THE OFFICER NAMES BESIDE THE LINE WERE NOT TAKEN ON ADJACENCY AND DID NOT NEED TO BE: the entry was walked from the D-U-N-S number that opens it to the one that opens the next. THE CONTROL THAT SETTLED IT: the query '20-765-0813' returns 24 hits in older volumes, every one reading YOUNG MENS CHRISTIAN ASSOC MTL at the same address, so the D-U-N-S is the association's, the camp had none, and 'Emp Here 55' is the downtown office and NOT a camp staff count -- which is the trap, because 55 sits right beside David Leduc's 75. Four association officers are recorded (Micheal Novak, Jacques Luys, Nina Caputo, Paul Dunne) with the pairing to their four titles flagged as an inference from order. The one thing that follows for the camp: 1441 rue Drummond through 2001 against 1435 in 2006 dates the move to between those years (f_4951). PAGE IMAGES ARE 403 on lending-restricted items, with the item's own details page as Referer -- a DIFFERENT failure from the missing-Referer 43-byte GIF under HTTP 200, and worth keeping distinct. | 2026-09-06: TWO ITEMS THE EARLIER ENUMERATION MISSED, both found by querying 'Kamp Kanawana' rather than 'Kanawana' and reading the full thirteen-item list. (a) canadianliterary0362unse is DICTIONARY OF LITERARY BIOGRAPHY VOL. 362, CANADIAN LITERARY HUMORISTS (Gale, 2011), whose Stuart McLean entry by DAVID C. GREER independently gives the 1969 counsellor job, the 1971 section directorship and the 1974-75 assistant directorship, dates the Vinyl Cafe recording at the camp to JULY 2005, and quotes an UNPUBLISHED 19 MAY 2010 INTERVIEW with McLean at length (f_4949). That interview is a live lead: it was conducted for the volume and Greer presumably holds it, and it is the only extended interview about the camp by someone who then wrote a full biographical entry. Opened as Open Question 6 in stuart-mclean.md. (b) basiccampmanagem0000ball_r5m1 is the AMERICAN CAMP ASSOCIATION's own textbook, Basic Camp Management (2012), which calls Kanawana CANADA'S FIRST ORGANIZATIONAL CAMP, 1894 -- recorded, and argued down to what it is worth, in canadian-camping-movement.md: it cites nothing, 'organizational camp' is a category term that does not engage the Big Cove question, and it is a year out on Keewaydin (f_4950). GROUPS 3, 4 AND 6 REMAIN, minus the two items just done. | 2026-09-06: TWO OF GROUP 6's MEMOIRS ARE DONE, and both were worth more than 'possible memoirs' suggested. (a) The Box from Braunau (2009) gives a LAST-DAY, WHOLE-CAMP, UNDRESSED MORNING DIP that its author calls 'the camp ritual' -- a tradition absent from every one of the camp's own publications this project has read, for the obvious reason that a brochure prints the 6.30 dip and not that one. Also a date bracket (the family reaches Drummondville in 1926, the boys go 'every summer' after) and a catchment fact nobody here had thought to ask about: an AMERICAN family posted to DRUMMONDVILLE sending two boys a hundred kilometres to the Montreal Y's camp (f_4952). (b) Dear Sam (2007) is by Janet Torge about Sam Lazarus, both already in this wiki -- the book had been CITED SINCE MARCH 2026 FROM A BOOKSELLER'S LISTING AND NEVER READ. It answers sam-lazarus.md's own open question: camper 'practically every summer since he was eight', so from 1986; the CIT application came AFTER he left school rather than at sixteen and is UNDATED, so do not convert it to a year by arithmetic; and 'Counselors and kids from Kamp Kanawana are everywhere, many at their first funeral' (f_4953). A LEAD, NOT AN IDENTIFICATION: the 2003 Junior Boys counsellors plaque carries a 'Sam L' and a 'Sam W', and 2003 would have been his last summer -- consistent, not proof, and deliberately NOT folded into the plaque index. THE WALK ON DEAR SAM WAS DELIBERATELY STOPPED at the camp material: it is a mother's letters to a dead son, everything found is recorded, and nothing was withheld. STILL IN GROUP 6: moonwastiredofwa0000belt (1992), guidepetitfuteci0000coll, swimmingwatersaf0000unse (1995). basiccampmanagem0000ball_r5m1 is DONE (f_4950). GROUPS 3 AND 4 REMAIN UNTOUCHED SINCE THE LAST ATTEMPT. | 2026-09-06: GROUP 3 IS DONE, and its own instruction -- recover the heading first -- was the whole job. The McGraw-Hill list is headed "POST OFFICES IN CANADA (Sub post offices and closed and renamed post offices appear in italics...)", which turns "Kanawana, PQ, see St-Sauveur-des-Monts, PQ" from an ordinary gazetteer cross-reference into a closing bracket: the office ended between about 1955 and the mid-1960s (f_4954, p_428). NOT 1966: the Internet Archive holds FOUR printings of this series and dates every one of them 1966, which is the same catalogue that dates every Canadian Almanac volume 1848 and dated the UPU 1912 supplement 1909. A FOURTH item of the series surfaced in passing, mcgrawhilldirect0000unse_j6s5, not on this priority's list. GROUP 4 (the ski guides, still needing an alignment control) and the remainder of GROUP 6 (moonwastiredofwa0000belt, guidepetitfuteci0000coll, swimmingwatersaf0000unse) ARE ALL THAT REMAIN of the worklist, plus the name sweep proper across directors-index.md. | 2026-09-06: GROUP 4 IS DONE, AND THE ALIGNMENT PROBLEM IS SOLVED. Alignment checked by three postal-code and address controls, all straight. (b) 'Guide plein air Quebec' (1991): the scrambled row IS NOW DECODED. Four controls, all documented from inside the corpus rather than from memory -- 849-5331 is the YMCA of Montreal (a Montreal guidebook prints 'Drummond (849-5331) YM-YWHA: 5500, Westbury (737-6551)' on one line), 737-6551 is the YM-YWHA, the 'Y' Country Camp is the YM-YWHA's camp AT HUBERDEAU per the Directory of Canadian Camps 1974, and 819-623 is the Mont-Laurier exchange. The straight reading fails all three at once (f_4956). THE OFFSET APPLIES TO EVERY OTHER CAMP ON THAT LIST and is written into the cache file for whoever wants them. FOURTH TIME this method has worked -- after Kanawyer, Lac Batiment and the D-U-N-S number -- and it is now stated as a rule: do not read across a scrambled row, find the field whose value is unique in the corpus, query that field on its own, and let it tell you which row it is in. It is the Directory of Canadian Welfare Services / Repertoire des services sociaux canadiens (Canadian Council on Social Development, 1974), and it is worth a great deal on its own: it lists the YM-YWCA of Cornwall with A. ROSS SEAMAN as Executive Director, which answers an open question in a-ross-seaman.md. WHAT REMAINS OF THIS PRIORITY: three items of group 6 (moonwastiredofwa0000belt, guidepetitfuteci0000coll, swimmingwatersaf0000unse), atlasroutierduqu0000mapa from group 4, the name sweep proper across directors-index.md, the untried spellings, and the Georgian Spirit lead. | 2026-09-06: GROUP 6's Petit Fute IS DONE, AND THE WORKLIST UNDERSOLD IT. This priority described guidepetitfuteci0000coll among items that 'may simply cite the camp as an example'. It carries the LONGEST FRENCH-LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION OF KANAWANA'S PROGRAMME THIS PROJECT HOLDS: season 28 June to 20 August, stays of six days to eight weeks, residential 6-12 days for 7-16 and leadership/adventure for 11-20, five activities held nowhere else here (trampoline aquatique, ecole du rock, danse, theatre, cours de survie), a named biodiversity activity ('La faune gagne du terrain'), the Explorateurs and Aventuriers four-day excursions, and AVENTURIER EXTREME called 'tout nouveau' -- which DATES that programme's introduction to 2011 or 2012, the only date this project has for it (f_4957).
