AND HOW IT WAS FOUND MATTERS: not from this worklist, but from the query 'Kanawana' + 'Westbury' run to control a telephone number in the 1991 ski guide. A worklist entry written from a catalogue title underestimated the item, and a control query for a different book found what was in it. GROUP 6 NOW HAS TWO ITEMS LEFT: moonwastiredofwa0000belt (1992) and swimmingwatersaf0000unse (1995). | 2026-09-06: THE UNTRIED NAME FORMS ARE NOW TRIED, AND THEY ARE NULLS. 'Kanawanna' 0 hits; 'Lac Kanawana' 0 hits; 'Kanawana, Que' 0 hits; 'Lake Kanawana' 1 hit, and it is the already-read McLean passage. Logged so nobody runs them again. 'Kamp Kanawana' remains the one spelling that added items (two). THE NAME SWEEP PROPER IS BEGUN, and its first four names produced a real find. Lemuel P. Ereaux: 0. Allan B. Cornell: 0. Edwin M. Crawford: 65 hits, all an American university-relations officer, none ours. F. H. SPINNEY: TWELVE HITS, AND ONE OF THEM IS HIM -- 'The School' (Toronto, 1912-13) gives 'F. H. Spinney, Principal Alexandra School, Montreal' as the author of an eight-part national column on teaching, 'In the Little Red Schoolhouse', with a second series commissioned (f_4958). This project had a surname, two initials and 'Educational Director' and nothing else. FOUR of Spinney's twelve hits are a DIFFERENT F. H. Spinney of Hudson, N.H., a Harvard Observatory variable-star observer -- recorded so he is not re-found. NAMES STILL TO SWEEP: everyone else in directors-index.md, which is about forty more, plus the Kanawana Committee chairmen. AND A NEW LEAD: 'The School' ran to 1935 and its later volumes are unsearched -- they cover every year of Spinney's Kanawana service, see p_432. | 2026-09-06: THE NAME SWEEP NOW HAS A LOG, at sources/cache/name-sweep/2026-09-06-directors-index-name-sweep.txt, which is the authoritative record of which names have been run -- if a name is not in it, it has not been swept. Nine names done. SIX NULLS OR NEAR-NULLS: Ereaux (0), Cornell (0), Hanagan (0), Paterson (0), Brandon (0), Crawford (65 hits, all an American university-relations officer), Holliday (243 hits, all an Indianapolis art collector). TWO REAL FINDS: F. H. Spinney (f_4958, p_432) and HAY FINLAY (f_4959) -- The McGill You Knew (1975) gives Kanawana's 1922 Senior Section Director as McGill's GYMNASTICS AND SOCCER COACH and has him and Van Wagner developing Camp Nominingue, 'known as Camp McGill to all the residents of the area'. THAT ONE ALSO EXPOSED A DEFECT OF THIS PROJECT'S OWN: canadian-camping-movement.md's Open Question 4 said 'no named individual confirmed on both sides of the Kanawana-Nominingue connection', and f_2641 and f_3039 had ALREADY MADE THAT JOIN, in their own text, weeks ago. The question was not unanswered, it was unread. Both articles are now fixed and the correction is written where a reader can see it. ONE OPEN LEAD: Johnston W. Abraham, Kanawana's Business Manager from about 1914, is named as the PROVENANCE of a fonds at Library and Archives Canada, MG 28 (I 280), 1917-1978, in the Union List of Manuscripts supplement 1979-80 -- the collection's name could not be recovered from the two-column OCR and the identification is unconfirmed. A person with browser access resolves it in one LAC lookup; this environment cannot (p_428). ABOUT FIFTY NAMES REMAIN, listed in the log. | 2026-09-06: THREE MORE NAMES, AND A PATTERN. C. B. Powter (19 hits, most a modern Alberta land-reclamation editor) is in the Commercial and Technical High School's Prospectus for Session 1908-1909 as PHYSICAL TRAINING master, and in the guide-souvenir of Montreal's first child-welfare exhibition (October 1912) on the 'Programme des Amusements' committee ALONGSIDE D. J. EVANS, who took charge of Kanawana the next year -- and directing the English schools' 'milice et choeur' with W. H. Smith, the music master on his own school's staff list (f_4960, f_4961). BOTH ITEMS ARE UNRESTRICTED and were downloaded whole. Greig Macdiarmid 0, Howie Langille 0, J. G. MacKinnon 244 hits all an econometrician and a Gaelic editor. THE PATTERN IS THE FINDING: three of this table's men now have day jobs -- Spinney a school principal, Powter a physical-training master, Finlay a McGill coach -- and all three are in education. The men the Montreal YMCA put in charge of its camps were schoolmasters. Written into directors-index.md, which had never said what any of these men did for a living. | 2026-09-06: THE NAME SWEEP HAS OPENED A WHOLE REFERENCE SERIES. Running 'Harold C. Cross' returned four real items, and one is the YMCA YEAR BOOK AND OFFICIAL ROSTERS (Association Press, 1921) -- UNRESTRICTED, downloaded whole, and a series this project had never heard of. Annual, continent-wide, every association's complete named paid staff branch by branch, plus an employed-officers index giving each man's post AND HIS YEAR OF ENTRY INTO ASSOCIATION WORK. From the one volume: Harold C. Cross documented as Boys' Work Secretary at Victoria B.C. with an entry year of 1912, seven years earlier than anything held here; full first names for GRANT D. BRANDON and JOHN G. MacKINNON; Hay Finlay's exact post; D. A. Budge's 1874 start; Nelson F. McEwen's middle initial; and the association's 1921 address of 127 Drummond St. See p_433 for the rest of the series. ALSO FROM THE SAME QUERY: the second standing lead in this priority, Henry Foss Hall's THE GEORGIAN SPIRIT (1967), IS NOW CLOSED AS A NULL. Its acknowledgement reads 'The research and records of my friend, Mr. Harold C. Cross, dedicated professional leader and historian of the Montreal YMCA, have been invaluable and are hereby acknowledged.' Pairing that phrase with 'Montreal' returns the item, proving the AND works; pairing it with Kanawana, Kamp Kanawana, summer camp, boys camp, camping and Laurentians returns ZERO every time. The Montreal YMCA's own historian supplied the research for the university's history AND THE CAMP IS NOWHERE IN IT. AND: Harold C. Cross wrote for the AMERICAN ROSE ANNUAL 1970, from St. Anne de Bellevue, Quebec, on 'North American Rose Gardens of 1851' -- a retirement address and a second subject, unpursued.

priorities.description: WAS KANAWANA A FOUNDING MEMBER OF THE QUEBEC CAMPING ASSOCIATION? The Guide Petit Fute Montreal 2011-2012 calls the camp 'membre fondateur de l'Association des camps du Quebec' (f_4957). This project holds the association's English Section as founded in 1937, incorporated by Federal Charter in 1949 and provincially in 1961, and holds NO MEMBERSHIP ROLL FOR 1937. So the claim is new here, unverified, and -- unlike the primacy claim in the same sentence -- CHECKABLE. WHERE TO LOOK: the ACQ's own records and any published history; the English Section's minutes 1937-1949; the Canadian Camping magazine run, which this project has read word for word and which may carry an anniversary piece naming the founders; the Concordia YMCA of Montreal fonds, where a camp that helped found a provincial association would have committee correspondence about it; and the 1975 CCA Directory Issue's Quebec section, which already gave this project the association's own corporate self-description. NOTE THE DIRECTION OF PROOF: a tourist guide repeating the camp's own copy is not evidence, and a null in the association's records is not disproof either, since 1937 membership lists may simply not survive. What would settle it is a contemporary document naming the founding camps. [ADVANCED 2026-09-06, and the target has moved. NOT RESOLVED -- no independent source found either way. THREE THINGS ESTABLISHED. (1) EVERY INSTANCE OF THE CLAIM TRACES TO THE CAMP OR ITS PARENT BODY: the 2025 preparation guide, both the French and English 2026 parent guides, and the YMCA's own Pip Award release. The Petit Fute guide is repeating camp copy, not corroborating it (f_4991). (2) THE CLAIM CANNOT MEAN WHAT IT SAYS. Canadian Camping vol 13 no 3 (April 1961) gives the QUEBEC CAMPING ASSOCIATION as formed on 11 FEBRUARY 1937, and L'Association des Camps du Quebec as a SEPARATE FRANCOPHONE body 'founded about three years ago', i.e. c.1958, which joined the QCA under a joint charter approved 9 January 1961 (f_4990). Kanawana is an anglophone YMCA of Montreal camp; it would have been in the QCA, not in a French association founded twenty-one years later. For the claim to be true it must mean the QCA, whose merged successor carries the ACQ name today. (3) SO WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT IS NARROWER THAN THIS PRIORITY SUPPOSED, AND IT IS NOT THE ACQ'S RECORDS: it is a list of the camps party to the QCA'S FORMATION ON 11 FEBRUARY 1937. THE CONCORDIA ARCHIVES HOLD A QCA CONSTITUTION OF 1937 AND EXECUTIVE AND MEMBERS' MEETING RECORDS 1937-1942 (P0145/12N03 and P0145/12A) -- that is where such a list would be, and it is a physical-archive task. The Canadian Camping run has been read word for word and carries no membership roll, so that route is exhausted. Also recovered incidentally: the charter's four signatories (Alta R. Kahn, Kenneth Murray, Abbe Raoul Cloutier, Rene Saint-Onge) and the Charter Committee under Ernie Freedman with F. M. Van Wagner; and a CONTEMPORARY corroboration of the 1958-founding and 1961-joining sequence this project had held only from a 1969 announcement.]
priorities.source: f_4957, Guide Petit Fute Montreal 2011-2012
priorities.notes: Raised 2026-09-06 while recording the Petit Fute entry. Deliberately raised as a priority rather than written into an article, because the article would then carry the claim.

priorities.description: SEARCH THE LATER VOLUMES OF 'THE SCHOOL' (Toronto, 1912-1935) FOR KANAWANA AND FOR ITS PEOPLE. Volume 1 (1912-13) was downloaded whole and read for F. H. Spinney, and gave Kamp Kanawana's Educational Director as PRINCIPAL OF ALEXANDRA SCHOOL, MONTREAL, and the author of an eight-part national column on teaching (f_4958). 'Kanawana' occurs ZERO times in volume 1. THE RUN CONTINUED TO 1935 AND THE LATER VOLUMES ARE UNSEARCHED -- and they cover EVERY YEAR OF SPINNEY'S KNOWN CAMP SERVICE (about 1917 to 1922 and beyond), the whole interwar era, and the years in which Harold C. Cross, Allan B. Cornell and the other 'Educational Directors' were at the camp. A national education journal is exactly where a summer camp's educational programme, a schoolmaster's summer work, or an obituary of a Montreal principal would be printed. WHAT TO DO: enumerate the volumes on the Internet Archive (the series identifier pattern is schoolmagazinedeNNunivuoft), check which are NOT lending-restricted, download those whole, and grep each for Kanawana, Kamp Kanawana, Spinney, Cornell, Cross, Alexandra School, and 'summer camp'. Volumes that ARE restricted can still be searched through openlibrary.org/search/inside.json (f_4933). ALSO WANTED FROM THE SAME RUN: Spinney's first name, his dates, and whether the announced second series, 'Little Journeys to Rural Schools', was ever written. [COMPLETE 2026-09-06.] Eleven items exist under the identifier stem (schoolmagazinede01-11univuoft, plus a separate 1935 scan schoolmagazinede10ontauoft); VOLUME 3 IS NOT ON THE ARCHIVE. None of the ten available is lending-restricted; all ten were downloaded whole and searched. RESULT: 'Kanawana' occurs ZERO TIMES IN ALL TEN VOLUMES, 1912-1923 -- a clean null, f_4975. Cornell and Cross do not appear either. WHAT IT DID GIVE, all on Spinney: HIS FIRST NAME IS FREDERICK, printed fourteen times in vols 2, 4 and 5 (f_4972) -- the volume-1 search could not have found it because the OCR double-spaces and the single-spaced grep returns zero across the whole run; HE STARTED AN AFTER-SCHOOL BASKETRY CLASS at Alexandra School, 160 Sanguinet Street, about the autumn of 1914, reported in the Montreal Daily Star of 18 December 1915 and reprinted in vol 4 -- six years before the 1922 camp brochure has him teaching basketry at Kanawana, which is the fourth and least circumstantial point in the identification (f_4973); THE SECOND SERIES ANNOUNCED IN VOLUME 1 WAS WRITTEN, eight instalments through vol 2; and HIS RUN ENDS IN JUNE 1917, the year the brochures put him at the camp, with no valedictory note and no successor named -- recorded as a coincidence in date, not a cause (f_4974). Cached at sources/cache/periodicals/1913-1923-the-school-magazine-spinney-full-run.txt. Sources src_the_school_magazine_vol2_1913_14, _vol4_1915_16, _vol5_1916_17 and _vols6_11_null_sweep. Written up in wiki/people/directors-index.md note 42. LEFT OPEN, split out as p_434: volume 3 (1914-15), which is not on the Archive, and volumes 12 onward (1923-1935), of which only the 1935 scan was located and it was not read.

priorities.description: SWEEP THE YMCA YEAR BOOK AND OFFICIAL ROSTERS, YEAR BY YEAR. [CORRECTED 2026-09-06, within the hour: this priority was first written saying the series was 'unknown to this project'. IT WAS NOT -- five volumes, 1893 to 1897, were cached in this repo on 2026-09-05 under p_405 and marked read. They were read for their PROVINCIAL NARRATIVE REPORTS and searched for 'camp', 'tent' and 'Ottawa', which reach nothing in a staff roster, so the rosters went unread. They are read now, see f_4966. The claim was written without running the grep rule 2 requires.] The 1921 volume (ymcayearbookoffi00youn, NOT lending-restricted, downloaded whole) turned up in the p_430 name sweep on 'Harold C. Cross'. It is an ANNUAL, CONTINENT-WIDE roster published by Association Press giving, for every YMCA in the United States and Canada: THE COMPLETE NAMED PAID STAFF, BRANCH BY BRANCH, and an ALPHABETICAL LIST OF EMPLOYED OFFICERS in which every man's post is given WITH HIS YEAR OF ENTRY INTO ASSOCIATION WORK. From one volume it produced: Harold C. Cross documented as Boys' Work Secretary at Victoria, B.C. with an entry year of 1912 (seven years earlier than anything this project had); full first names for GRANT D. BRANDON and JOHN G. MacKINNON, two Kanawana directors this table knew only by initials; Hay Finlay's exact 1921 post; D. A. Budge's entry year of 1874; Nelson F. McEwen's middle initial and 1918 start; and the association's 1921 address of 127 Drummond St. (f_4964, f_4965). FOR A PROJECT WHOSE HARDEST PROBLEM IS THAT ITS EARLY CAMP DIRECTORS ARE INITIALS ON A BROCHURE, THIS IS THE MOST USEFUL REFERENCE SERIES FOUND SO FAR -- better than the camping literature, which begins in 1936, while this does not. WHAT TO DO: enumerate the series on the Internet Archive (search the identifier stem 'ymcayearbook'), check which volumes are unrestricted, download those whole, and for each extract (a) the complete QUEBEC / Montreal roster and (b) the employed-officers index lines for every name in wiki/people/directors-index.md. Sweep from the 1890s to the 1950s. A year-by-year Montreal roster would let this project name the association's boys' work and physical staff for every season of the camp's first half-century, and the camp's directors were drawn from exactly those posts. KNOW THE LIMIT BEFORE STARTING: 'Kanawana' occurs ZERO times in the 1921 volume, and so do 'summer camp' and 'boys camp'. THE SERIES ROSTERS ASSOCIATIONS AND THEIR STAFF, NOT THEIR PROGRAMMES. It will never name the camp. It names the men, which is what is missing. || THE SERIES IS NOW ENUMERATED, so nobody need redo it. The Internet Archive scrape API (services/search/v1/scrape?q=identifier:ymcayearbook*) returns NINETEEN items: ymcayearbookof189[1-7]younuoft, ymcayearbookof190[678]younuoft, ymcayearbookoffi00youn (1921), ymcayearbookoffi01youn (1922), ymcayearbookand00amergoog (1907), 00assogoog (1896), 01amergoog (1882), 01assogoog (1921), 02amergoog (1886), 02assogoog (1891), and ymcayearbookoffi0000unse (1936). CAUTION: the catalogue's 'year' field gives 1890 for all ten younuoft scans and is wrong; the year is in the identifier and should be confirmed from inside the volume. ALREADY READ: 1893-97 (rosters, f_4966) and 1921 (f_4964, f_4965). STILL UNREAD: 1891, 1892, 1906, 1907, 1908, 1922, the four Google scans and 1936. THE 1906-1908 VOLUMES ARE THE NEXT ONES TO TAKE -- they would show who succeeded W. H. Ball Jr. as Montreal's Physical Director after his 1901/02 departure, and they sit either side of the camp's move to Saint-Sauveur. [ADVANCED 2026-09-06.] THE ENUMERATION WAS TOO NARROW AND THE ENDPOINT WAS LYING. Re-run on the series' TITLE rather than the identifier stem, it returns nine items under 'YMCA Year Book and Official Rosters' and FOUR MORE under a second title the same series used, 'Year Book of the Young Men's Christian Associations of North America' -- unreachable from the stem. One of those, yearbookyoungme01commgoog, is NOT lending-restricted and CONTAINS TWO ANNUAL VOLUMES, 1899 AND 1900, though its catalogue record names only 1899. That fills two years of the 1898-1905 hole. THE 1899 MONTREAL ROSTER IS NOW READ (f_4976): Budge, Calhoun, JOHN ROY (Asst., entered 1899), E. G. RANDAL (Educational Director, entered 1893 -- A NAME THAT OCCURS NOWHERE ELSE IN THIS PROJECT, and the earliest Educational Director it has by nearly twenty years), W. H. BALL, JR. (Physical Director, ENTERED ASSOCIATION WORK 1889, still in post in 1899), Crowe, Morrison, Grace. Also settled: John Roy and John W. Ross are two different men, listed in different sections of the same volume -- billy-ball.md open question 8. AND A TOOLING FINDING THAT OUTLIVES THIS PRIORITY, f_4978: archive.org/services/search/v1/scrape was observed returning THE RESULT SET OF A PREVIOUS QUERY while reporting it as the current one, and returning unrelated items when 'year' is added to fields. Use advancedsearch.php with output=json. STILL OPEN, split to p_435: the 1900 roster (unreadable OCR, page images untried), the other Google scans found by the title query, and the remaining gap years. || [CORRECTED 2026-09-06, LATER SESSION.] THE "STILL UNREAD" LIST ABOVE IS STALE AND WOULD HAVE SENT A LATER PASS TO REDO WORK ALREADY DONE. It names 1891, 1892, 1906, 1907, 1908, 1922, the four Google scans and 1936 as unread. Checked against sources/cache/ymca-yearbooks/ before writing this: 1906-1908 are cached as 1906-1908-ymca-year-book-montreal-roster.txt, 1922 as 1922-ymca-year-book-montreal-roster.txt, 1891-1892 as 1891-1892-ymca-year-book-ball-springfield.txt, 1898 and 1899-1900 each as their own roster file, and 1909 as well. The Google scans were all read into 2026-09-06-complete-ia-inventory-of-the-series.txt, which is the authoritative statement of what this series holds and what it does not. 1936 is lending-restricted on the Internet Archive and is the only IA volume genuinely unread. SO THE INTERNET ARCHIVE SIDE OF THIS PRIORITY IS FINISHED. What is left is not here: the 1900 roster's unreadable OCR (p_435), and 1901-1905 and 1910-1920, which exist only on HathiTrust behind a Cloudflare challenge (p_439). Do not re-enumerate.

priorities.notes: Raised 2026-09-06 out of the p_430 name sweep. NOTE ALSO what is NOT in the 1921 employed-officers list: Spinney, Powter, Ereaux, Charlton, Owens. That is not a null about those men -- the list is of PAID association officers, and f_4958 and f_4960 show Spinney was a school principal and Powter a physical-training master. Their absence corroborates that the camp's educational and section staff were volunteers and seasonal employees drawn from the schools. So the series will answer questions about the association's secretaries and will NOT answer questions about the camp's schoolmasters; use it accordingly. | 2026-09-06: the 1893-97 rosters are DONE and gave the founding-era staff of the association year by year, including 'W. H. Ball, Jr.' in all five volumes (the Jr. is new), W. F. Chapman as Assistant Secretary 1894-97, and C. B. Powter joining as ASSISTANT PHYSICAL DIRECTOR under Ball in the 1896 volume -- which completes Powter's career from assistant to the camp's founder, to running the Y's camp in 1898, to founding his own in 1902, to teaching physical training in 1908-09 (f_4966). | 2026-09-06: THE 1906, 1907 AND 1908 VOLUMES ARE DONE, and they were the right ones to take next. W. J. HOLLIDAY -- the man the association's own 1931 report calls 'the first camp director' of Kanawana -- entered Association work in 1906 as an Assistant Secretary at Montreal and was BOYS' WORK DIRECTOR from the 1907 volume, so the Junior Camp of 1908 and the opening of the Saint-Sauveur site in 1910 were run by the association's boys' work secretary rather than a seasonal appointee. JOHN W. ROSS is PRESIDENT of the YMCA of Montreal in all three volumes, which joins his 1894 Summer Camp chairmanship, his 1899 Permanent Camp Committee seat and his 1921 International Committee membership into one forty-year public life. W. H. BALL, JR. is absent from all three, the first outside confirmation of the 1901/02 departure. And W. S. MAGUIRE, Montreal's Assistant Physical Director in 1908, is Physical at VICTORIA in the 1921 volume on the same roster as Harold C. Cross -- a co-occurrence, not a claim, and a thread worth pulling (f_4967). STILL UNREAD: 1891, 1892, 1922, the four Google scans (1882, 1886, 1896, 1907, 1921) and 1936. THE 1922 VOLUME IS THE NEXT ONE: it would catch the association a year after the 1921 roster and in the season Lemuel P. Ereaux directed the camp and Hay Finlay ran its senior section. | 2026-09-06: THE 1922 VOLUME IS DONE, the tenth of the series read. W. J. HOLLIDAY is SECRETARY OF THE NORTH BRANCH, 2300 Park Ave., which answers directors-index.md's 'how far past 1910 he continued is not stated' -- 1906 to 1922 at least. HAY FINLAY is gone from Central's assistant physicals, dating his move to McGill between the 1921 and 1922 volumes and matching the 1922 brochure's 'ex-Central YMCA' exactly. MacKINNON and BRANDON both moved to district postings (Cote St. Paul, Verdun). D. A. BUDGE's entry into Association service is given TO THE MONTH -- 'Mar. 1874' -- on a continent-wide list of secretaries entering before 1893 and still employed in April 1922, with only four men ahead of him. And T. D. PATTON is ASSISTANT Territorial Secretary at Toronto, where his article compresses 1922-26 into 'Territorial Secretary' (f_4968). STILL UNREAD: 1891, 1892, the four Google scans and 1936. THE 1891 AND 1892 VOLUMES ARE NEXT and they are the important ones left -- they cover the years the camp committee was appointed (autumn 1892) and the Jones' Island trip (1891), and they would show whether W. H. Ball Jr. and T. Duncan Patton were both on the Montreal staff before the 1893 volume this project already has. | 2026-09-06: 1891 AND 1892 ARE DONE, and the 1892 volume is the best thing this series has produced. Its QUEBEC narrative, signed by Charles Cushing as Corresponding Member, says of the Montreal association: 'THE PHYSICAL DIRECTOR, W. H. BALL, JR., A NEW MAN, FROM THE SPRINGFIELD TRAINING SCHOOL, is doing excellent work.' That does not prove Kanawana's founder is the William Henry Ball of Springfield's class of 1891, but it REMOVES THE ONLY STRUCTURAL OBJECTION -- f_1245's 'his known career positions do not include Montreal' -- by documenting the Springfield-to-Montreal path from the Canadian end, in print, in 1892, from a source with no interest in the question (f_4969). The 1891 roster has NO physical director at Montreal at all, which is what 'a new man' means. AND R. L. CHARLTON, whom the corpus name sweep could not find, is on the ONTARIO AND QUEBEC PROVINCIAL COMMITTEE APPOINTED FEBRUARY 1891, with D. A. Budge, Herbert Ames and George Hague -- three years before he joins the 1894 Summer Camp committee (f_4970). Rule 21 for the third time in a day. TWELVE VOLUMES NOW READ: 1891-97, 1906-08, 1921, 1922. WHAT REMAINS is the four Google scans (1882, 1886, 1896, 1907, 1921 -- mostly duplicate years, worth checking only for different printings) and ymcayearbookoffi0000unse (1936), which may be restricted. THE SERIES IS EFFECTIVELY EXHAUSTED FOR THIS PROJECT'S PURPOSES; the 1898-1905 and 1909-1920 years are simply not on the Internet Archive under this identifier stem and would need a different search.

priorities.description: THE TWO PIECES OF 'THE SCHOOL' THAT p_432 COULD NOT REACH. p_432 read ten volumes of The School (Toronto) covering September 1912 to June 1923 and found 'Kanawana' zero times, while recovering Frederick H. Spinney's first name and his 1914 basketry class. TWO GAPS REMAIN AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT IN KIND. (1) VOLUME 3, September 1914 to June 1915, IS NOT ON THE INTERNET ARCHIVE under the schoolmagazinede stem and has not been read anywhere -- this is a HOLE IN THE RECORD, not a null, and it sits precisely where Spinney's basketry class was getting started (the Star report of December 1915 says it began 'about a year ago'). Try: HathiTrust full view, the University of Toronto and OISE library catalogues, Canadiana.ca, and a scrape-API sweep on other identifier stems for the same title. (2) VOLUMES 12 ONWARD, 1923 to 1935 -- only a single 1935 scan (schoolmagazinede10ontauoft) was located and it was NOT read. Expected yield is low: Spinney had been absent from the magazine for six years by 1923. But an obituary of a Montreal principal is exactly the kind of thing this journal printed, and his death date is unknown. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: read schoolmagazinede10ontauoft for 'Spinney' and 'Alexandra', and enumerate whether any 1924-1934 volumes are digitized at all.
priorities.notes: Split out of p_432 on completion, 2026-09-06. Low weight deliberately: the ten volumes already read are the ones that overlap Spinney's camp service, and they gave a clean Kanawana null. This is the tail.

priorities.description: FINISH THE YEAR BOOK SWEEP NOW THAT THE ENUMERATION IS WIDE AND THE ENDPOINT IS TRUSTED. p_433 found the series lives under TWO titles and that an identifier-stem query reaches only a third of it. [JOB 1 IS ALREADY DONE, 2026-09-06, within the hour of writing this priority -- and it did not need page images. THIS PRIORITY FIRST SAID: 'READ THE 1900 MONTREAL ROSTER. It is bound into yearbookyoungme01commgoog after the 1899 volume, its catalogue record does not mention it, and its djvu OCR is too degraded to take a roster off... THE ITEM IS NOT LENDING-RESTRICTED, so page images are fetchable and would settle whether Ball is still Physical Director in 1900.' The Year Book lists the same staff TWICE, in an alphabetical list AND in a branch directory by city; only the alphabetical list is degraded, and the branch directory -- never looked at before that was written -- reads cleanly. THE 1900 ROSTER IS NOW READ, f_4979: Ball IS still Physical Director, which bounds his departure to 1901-1905; E. G. Randal is gone with NO Educational Director line at all, bounding his tenure to at most 1893-1899; Crowe and Grace are gone, their lines printed blank; and one assistant is added whose name the volume gives two irreconcilable ways.] TWO JOBS REMAIN. (2) DATE AND READ THE OTHER SCANS the title query surfaced: ymcayearbookand00amergoog, 00assogoog, 01amergoog, 01assogoog, 02amergoog, 02assogoog, and yearbookofyoungm0000vari, yearbookofyoungm00youn, yearbookyoungme00commgoog. Their catalogue years are 1907, 1896, 1882, 1921, 1886, 1891, 1892, 1881 and 1921 -- BUT THE CATALOGUE YEAR IN THIS SERIES IS UNRELIABLE AND AT LEAST ONE ITEM HOLDS TWO VOLUMES, so read each title page. 1882 and 1886 would be new to this project and predate the camp, giving the Montreal association's staff in the decade before it; any of them may hold a bound second volume in a gap year, as the 1899 item did. (3) THE REMAINING HOLES are then 1898, 1901-1905 and 1909-1920. Chase those on HathiTrust, Google Books and the Kautz Family YMCA Archives at the University of Minnesota, which holds the series in print. [JOB 2 PARTLY DONE 2026-09-06, and it changed what job 3 is.] All nine scans were downloaded and scanned WHOLE for title pages rather than read off their catalogue year -- and FOUR OF THEM HOLD MULTIPLE BOUND VOLUMES. ymcayearbookand00assogoog, catalogued 1896, holds FIVE: 1896, 1897, 1898, 1899 and 1900 (f_4981). THE 1898 VOLUME IS READ (f_4980) and it names Archibald McKellar -- the 'A. MacKellar' of the 1898 senior camp -- as an Assistant Secretary of the Montreal YMCA, appearing in exactly one of the five volumes, that year. ymcayearbookand02assogoog (catalogued 1891) shows title-page hits for 1891, 1892, 1894, 1895 AND 1898; ymcayearbookand01amergoog (catalogued 1882) for 1884, 1886 and 1888; ymcayearbookand02amergoog (catalogued 1886) for 1885, 1886, 1887, 1888 and 1890. NONE OF THOSE BOUNDARIES HAS BEEN CONFIRMED against the title-page signature (a real title page sits under 'NORTH AMERICA,' and above 'PRICE FIFTY CENTS'; a statistics heading names the PREVIOUS year) -- some will be statistics headings. CONFIRMED YEARS STILL UNREAD: 1881-82 (yearbookofyoungm00youn), 1885, 1886, 1887, 1888, 1890 if real. Those all predate the camp, so their value is the Montreal association in the decade before it -- Budge entered Association work in 1874 and Ball in 1889. WHAT REMAINS OF THE HOLE: 1901-1905 and 1909-1920. 1898 is now closed. And the 1900 volume bound into ymcayearbookand00assogoog is an INDEPENDENT SECOND COPY of the one whose alphabetical list is OCR-ruined -- read it before assuming the 1900 entry years are lost. [THE 1900 SECOND COPY IS DONE, 2026-09-06. Its alphabetical list is legible where the other scan's is ruined, and it settled two things this session had left open: the assistant is F. E. BURGESS (entered 1899), and '*Randal, E. G., Taunton, Mass., Sec., 93' places Montreal's Educational Director as GENERAL SECRETARY AT TAUNTON, MASSACHUSETTS by 1900 -- same initials, same entry year, same training-school star as his 1899 Montreal entry. f_4982. STANDING METHOD NOTE for the rest of this priority: a volume in this series may be bound into more than one scan, and where one scan's OCR fails the other's may not. Before recording a roster as lost, check for the same year in another item. That has now been the answer twice.] [1909 FOUND AND READ, 2026-09-06. ymcayearbookand00amergoog is catalogued 1907 and IS THE 1909 VOLUME -- title page 'May 1, 1908, to April 30, 1909 ... 1909', copyright 1909. It is the FIRST YEAR OF THE 1909-1920 HOLE and on its catalogue year it would have been skipped as a duplicate. It was ALSO missed by this session's own title-page sweep, whose pattern looked for 'For the Year NNNN' -- this volume dates itself by the ASSOCIATION YEAR and contains no such phrase (f_4984). ANY FURTHER SWEEP OF THIS SERIES MUST MATCH THE ASSOCIATION-YEAR FORM TOO, and must fall back to reading the front matter of every item that returns nothing. What it gave, f_4983: M. G. BROOKS as Boys' Work Director, entered 1905, a name occurring nowhere else in this project; W. J. HOLLIDAY -- Kanawana's first camp director -- listed as plain 'Asst.', which withdrew half of a claim in directors-index.md about the 1910 season; HERBERT C. PATTERSON, the first name behind the 1921 volume's 'H. C. Paterson'; J. E. Merritt's year of entry, 1894; FRED G. WHITE; and the Educational Director line printed blank.]

priorities.description: RE-SWEEP THE YMCA YEAR BOOK SERIES WITH A PATTERN THAT CAN SEE IT, AND CHASE 1910-1920. p_435 found the 1909 volume by accident: its catalogue year says 1907, and this session's title-page sweep -- which searched for 'For the Year NNNN' -- returned NOTHING from it, because that volume dates itself by the association year, 'May 1, 1908, to April 30, 1909' (f_4984). Two consequences. (1) RE-RUN THE SWEEP over every item already downloaded, matching BOTH forms -- /FOR (THE )?YEARS? 1[89]dd/ AND /(MAY|APRIL) *1?[.,]? *1[89]dd,? *TO/ -- and, for any item that still returns nothing, READ ITS FRONT MATTER DIRECTLY around the phrases 'YEAR BOOK', 'ASSOCIATION PRESS' and 'Copyright'. Items to redo: ymcayearbookand01assogoog, ymcayearbookand02amergoog, ymcayearbookand01amergoog, ymcayearbookand02assogoog, yearbookyoungme00commgoog, yearbookofyoungm00youn, ymcayearbookoffi00youn, ymcayearbookoffi01youn. Several showed multiple hits whose boundaries were never confirmed against the title-page signature (a real title page sits under 'NORTH AMERICA,' and above 'PRICE FIFTY CENTS' in the older setting; a statistics heading names the PREVIOUS year). (2) THE HOLE IS NOW 1901-1905 AND 1910-1920. 1909 is closed. For 1910-1920 the specific question is WHEN W. J. HOLLIDAY GOT THE BOYS' WORK DIRECTORSHIP BACK, IF HE DID -- he holds it in 1907 and 1908, has lost it to M. G. BROOKS by 1909, and opens the new camp site in 1910, which the 1910 Annual Report announces without giving him any boys' work title. The 1910 and 1911 volumes would settle it. Also chase M. G. BROOKS, who is new to this project entirely and was the association's Boys' Work Director in the year before the new site opened -- the Boys' Department ran the camp, so he is a candidate for a role in it that nothing yet documents. Surfaces: HathiTrust and Google Books full view for the series, and the Kautz Family YMCA Archives at the University of Minnesota, which holds it in print. [JOB 1 IS DONE, 2026-09-06. The re-sweep was run with both patterns AND with direct front-matter reads wherever both returned nothing, and THE SERIES IS NOW INVENTORIED IN FULL: thirteen Internet Archive items holding twenty-three annual volumes, six items holding more than one, one bound out of order (f_4985, and the table is in sources/cache/ymca-yearbooks/2026-09-06-complete-ia-inventory-of-the-series.txt). AVAILABLE: 1881-82, 1884, 1886, 1887, 1888, 1890-1900, 1906-1909, 1921, 1922, and a restricted 1936. NOT AVAILABLE ON THE ARCHIVE AT ALL: 1883, 1885, 1889, 1901-1905, 1910-1920, 1923-1935 -- and those holes survive four separately corrected search methods, so they are the shape of the Archive's holdings and not of a bad query. NOTE FOR ANYONE TEMPTED TO RE-RUN THIS: every pattern used failed at least once. 'FOR THE YEAR NNNN' missed the 1909 volume (which dates itself by the association year) and the 1882 volume (whose OCR reads 'FOB THE YEAR'). The pre-camp volumes were also read: W. H. BALL IS IN NONE of them, so his 1889-1892 gap stays blank; and two new names came out, CHARLES CUSHING as Quebec's corresponding member in 1887 and G. A. KUHRING as an assistant under Budge (f_4986). JOB 2 STANDS AND IS NOW THE WHOLE OF THIS PRIORITY: 1910-1920 is off-Archive and must be chased at HathiTrust, Google Books full view, or the Kautz Family YMCA Archives at the University of Minnesota.] [CORRECTION 2026-09-06: the inventory recorded ymcayearbookand02assogoog as holding '1891, 1892, 1898, 1894, 1895, BOUND OUT OF ORDER'. IT HOLDS 1891-1895 IN ORDER. The third volume's title page is OCR'd 1898 and is 1893. Nothing in this series is bound out of order. A THIRD TERM FOR THE DATING RULE: a catalogue year is worthless, a title page beats it, AND A VOLUME'S OWN CONTENTS BEAT ITS TITLE PAGE'S OCR. Where two items hold the same year, read both -- their disagreement is what exposed this.] [CLOSED 2026-09-06. THE MISSING YEARS ARE ON HATHITRUST, PUBLIC DOMAIN, WITH IDENTIFIERS -- f_4989 and sources/cache/ymca-yearbooks/2026-09-06-hathitrust-holdings-the-missing-years.txt. Two catalogue records hold the series and BOTH must be queried: OCLC 6996715 gives one, LCCN 29015142 gives that one plus a second carrying the single-year 1901-1906 run. Every hole now has an item id. BUT THIS ENVIRONMENT CANNOT READ THEM: HathiTrust's Bib API works and was control-tested, while every reading and search endpoint returns 403 behind Cloudflare. Recorded as an ACCESS FAILURE with the untried routes named, not as a null. Google Books returned 429 daily-quota-exceeded on the control query too, so it is also not a null -- retry on a later day. What remains is not agent-doable from here and is raised as p_439, a human task.]

priorities.description: WHO WAS CHARLES CUSHING, AND IS HE ONE OF THE CAMP'S CUSHINGS? The 1887 Year Book names 'Charles Cushing, Montreal' as the YMCA's CORRESPONDING MEMBER FOR QUEBEC -- the association's senior volunteer post in the province, held by General Secretary D. A. Budge himself in the 1886 volume (f_4986). The name occurs nowhere else in this project. IT MATTERS BECAUSE THE CUSHINGS ARE ALREADY IN THE FOUNDING STORY AND NOBODY HAS EVER ESTABLISHED HOW THEY RELATE TO EACH OTHER: LEMUEL CUSHING took a group of boys to Lake Saint-Joseph in 1892, two years before the conventional founding; W. E. CUSHING sat on the committee appointed in the autumn of 1892 alongside J. W. Ross, W. W. Wilson, T. Duncan Patton and W. H. Ball; PERCY H. CUSHING was the association's Assistant Secretary in the 1894 and 1895 volumes. A fourth Cushing holding the senior Quebec YMCA post in 1887 -- five years before any of that -- would make the family's involvement structural rather than incidental, and would reframe the 1892 Lake Saint-Joseph trip as something the association's own leadership circle did rather than a private initiative it later absorbed. OR HE IS AN UNRELATED MAN WITH A COMMON SURNAME, WHICH IS EQUALLY WORTH ESTABLISHING. WHAT TO DO: this repo already holds sources/cache/web-pages/cushing-genealogy-1905.txt -- READ IT FOR CHARLES FIRST, before any web search, per the zeroth-step rule. Then Lovell's Montreal directories of the 1880s (several years are on the Internet Archive and on BAnQ numerique), the Montreal Gazette via Google News Archive, Find A Grave and the Quebec Anglophone Heritage Network, whose article on the Saint-Adolphe-d'Howard camp is already a source here and discusses Lemuel Cushing. Also re-read the 1884, 1886, 1888 and 1890 Year Book volumes for him: they are downloaded and only the 1887 one was searched on this name. [FIRST STEP DONE 2026-09-06, and it corrected this priority's own premise. The zeroth-step rule was right twice over: the genealogy WAS in the repo, and so was CHARLES HIMSELF -- wiki/people/cushing-family.md has listed him among Lemuel Sr.'s eight sons since before this session. The claim that his name occurred nowhere in this project was written from a grep on the phrase 'Charles Cushing', and that article writes him as a table row headed by the surname. Corrected in place in f_4986 and in directors-index.md. WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW IS THE POST, not the man: that table gives him no YMCA connection at all, and he was the association's corresponding member for Quebec in 1887 -- f_4987, written up in cushing-family.md. A SECOND FIND FROM THE SAME READ, f_4988: the 'Percy H. Cushing' who was Montreal's assistant secretary in the 1894 and 1895 Year Books is probably PERCY HILL CUSHING, b. 9 July 1872, d. 22 DECEMBER 1896, son of Col. James Brock Cushing -- four converging fields, including the family's removal to Montreal in October 1890 and a death that explains his disappearance from the 1896 rosters. WHAT REMAINS: the 1884, 1888 and 1890 volumes are downloaded and were NOT searched on the Cushing names -- only 1886 and 1887 were. Do those next; they are already on disk. Then Lovell's directories and the Gazette for Charles's own YMCA activity, and for whether any Cushing sat on the camp committee before 1892.] [THE DOWNLOADED VOLUMES ARE NOW SEARCHED ON THE CUSHING NAMES, 2026-09-06, and the answer is bigger than the question. Charles Cushing is Quebec's corresponding member in the 1887, 1888, 1891 and 1895 volumes and SIGNS THE PROVINCE'S NARRATIVE REPORT IN THE 1898 VOLUME as 'Charles Cushing, Cor. Mem.' With f_4837's 1893, 1894 and 1895 that is 1887, 1888, 1891, 1893, 1894, 1895 and 1898 -- a tenure of at least eleven years spanning BEFORE, DURING AND AFTER the 1892 Lake Saint-Joseph trip and the 1894 founding. NO CUSHING in the 1882/1884 volumes or in 1881-82. ONE LOOSE END THAT IS NOW THE MAIN JOB: f_4837 says 'by the 1897 volume the office is held by William Tees', and the 1898 volume -- title page verified as 'NORTH AMERICA, FOR THE YEAR 1898' -- has Cushing signing again. Not a contradiction, since the statements are about different years and a man can return to a post, but the handover was not permanent. RE-READ THE 1896 AND 1897 VOLUMES ON BOTH NAMES before either version is treated as settled; both are on disk, in ymcayearbookand00assogoog (1896 at scan line 31596 is 1897; 1896 at line 259).] [CLOSED 2026-09-06, and the closing move was a correction. The '1898 Cushing signature' recorded an hour earlier DOES NOT EXIST: that volume is the 1893 one, its title page OCR'd 'FOR THE YEAR 1898' -- these scans confuse 3 and 8, and the same OCR renders Morrison's entry year 93 as 'SS'. Its contents are all 1892 and early 1893. The signature is the 1893 one f_4837 already had, and the 'tension' raised against f_4837's William Tees was built out of a misread digit. THE 1896 AND 1897 VOLUMES WERE THEN READ, WHICH WAS THIS PRIORITY'S LAST JOB: 1896 has no Cushing and no Tees; 1897 prints 'Quebec ... Wm. Tees, Montreal' and the province's report signed 'William Tees, Cor. Mem.', CONFIRMING f_4837 directly rather than challenging it. FINAL ANSWER: Charles Cushing held the Quebec corresponding membership in the 1887, 1888, 1891, 1893, 1894 and 1895 volumes -- six documented years across a span of at least nine -- with Tees in the post by 1897. He held it before, during and after the 1892 Lake Saint-Joseph trip and the 1894 founding. Also settled: no Cushing in the 1882, 1884 or 1881-82 volumes. WHAT REMAINS is not Year Book work: whether the Year Book's Charles Cushing is Lemuel Sr.'s son (an identification on name, city, period and calling, never a documented link), and whether any Cushing sat on the camp committee before 1892. Lovell's directories and the Gazette. Raised as p_438 rather than kept open here.]
priorities.notes: Raised 2026-09-06 from the pre-camp Year Book volumes. Weight 6 rather than higher because the join is a surname and nothing else so far -- but the payoff if it holds is a different account of how the camp began, and the first step is reading a file this repo already has.

priorities.description: IS THE YMCA'S CHARLES CUSHING LEMUEL SR.'S SON, AND WAS ANY CUSHING ON THE CAMP COMMITTEE BEFORE 1892? p_437 established that a Charles Cushing of Montreal held the YMCA's corresponding membership for Quebec in the 1887, 1888, 1891, 1893, 1894 and 1895 Year Books -- before, during and after the 1892 Lake Saint-Joseph trip and the 1894 founding -- with William Tees in the post by 1897 (f_4987). TWO THINGS IT COULD NOT SETTLE. (1) THE IDENTIFICATION. That the Year Book's Charles Cushing is the Charles Cushing born Chatham 1848, McGill B.C.L. 1869, Montreal notary, son of Lemuel Cushing Sr., rests on name, city, period and calling -- a professional man prominent in Congregational church work, aged thirty-nine in 1887. It is NOT a documented link and no source found joins them. Lovell's Montreal directories of the 1880s and 1890s (several years on the Internet Archive and BAnQ numerique), the Montreal Gazette via Google News Archive, and the Montreal YMCA's own annual reports of 1887-1895 would settle it: any of them naming the association's Quebec corresponding member with an address or an occupation closes the question. (2) THE COMMITTEE. This project's founding narrative has W. E. Cushing on the committee appointed in the autumn of 1892 and Lemuel Cushing taking boys to Lake Saint-Joseph that summer. If Charles was the province's senior YMCA volunteer throughout, THE QUESTION IS WHETHER THE 1892 TRIP WAS AN ASSOCIATION INITIATIVE RATHER THAN A PRIVATE ONE IT LATER ABSORBED -- which is the open question wiki/history/founding-1894.md has carried, unresolved, since July. The Montreal annual reports for 1891-1893 are the place: look for Charles Cushing in the officers and committee lists, not just in the narrative. [JOB 1 IS CLOSED AND JOB 2 HAS MOVED, 2026-09-06, from annual reports ALREADY IN THIS REPO'S CACHE that no previous pass had read for this family. THE IDENTIFICATION IS CLOSED: Charles Cushing sat on the MONTREAL YMCA'S BOARD OF DIRECTORS in the reports for 1890-91, 1891-92 and 1892-93, and was its RECORDING SECRETARY in 1892-93 (f_4992). A Charles Cushing of Montreal on the association's board in exactly the years a Charles Cushing of Montreal held the province's corresponding membership is the same man by any reasonable reading. William Tees, who takes that post by 1897, sits beside him on the same board and is Vice-President in 1892-93 -- the post passed between two Montreal board members. JOB 2: FOUR CUSHINGS WERE INSIDE THE ASSOCIATION IN 1892-93 (f_4993). Charles as recording secretary; PERCY H. CUSHING on the STAFF, two years earlier than the Year Book had him, and the man the Boys' Department sent to argue boys' work at the Kingston Convention in 1890-91, 'as a result' of which 'a new interest was awakened for work among boys'; W. E. CUSHING chairing a committee; and a WALTER CUSHING on another. The same staff list also puts C. B. POWTER on the association's staff in 1892-93, FOUR YEARS earlier than the 1896 Year Book had him, alongside W. H. Ball as Physical Director and T. Duncan Patton as Assistant Secretary -- two of the five men on the committee appointed that autumn. NONE OF THE REPORTS MENTIONS LAKE SAINT-JOSEPH, A CAMP OR A SUMMER OUTING in the passages read: this is a setting, not an event, and the question is now whether the association MINUTED the trip rather than whether a Cushing was involved. THE NEXT PASS IS ON DISK: the Boys' Department sections of the 1892-93 and 1893-94 reports READ IN FULL rather than searched for a surname, plus the Cushing hits in the 1893-94, 1894-95 and 1895-96 reports, which were counted and not read. Raised as p_440.]
priorities.notes: Raised 2026-09-06 on closing p_437. Weight 5: the identification is probably right and probably provable, but the payoff is context rather than a new fact -- except for job 2, which could change how the founding is told and is worth more than the weight suggests if the annual reports cooperate.

priorities.description: HUMAN TASK, OR A LATER RETRY: READ THE YMCA YEAR BOOK FOR 1901-1905 AND 1910-1920 ON HATHITRUST. Every one of these volumes is PUBLIC DOMAIN AND FULL VIEW on HathiTrust, and a person with a browser can open all of them; this environment gets HTTP 403 from every HathiTrust reading and search endpoint behind a Cloudflare challenge, while its catalogue API answers normally (f_4989). ITEM IDS: 1901 ien.35556001609783; 1902 ien.35556001609791; 1903 ien.35556001609809; 1904 ien.35556001609817; 1905 ien.35556001609825; 1909-1910 mdp.39015069245812; 1910-11 uiug.30112109814126; 1911/12 uiug.30112109814233; 1913/14 uiug.30112109814225; 1915/16 uiug.30112109814217; 1916/17 uiug.30112109814209; 1917/18 uiug.30112109814191; 1918/19 uiug.30112086367254; 1919/20 uiug.30112109814183. Open at babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=<id>. WHAT TO LOOK AT IN EACH: the QUEBEC BRANCH DIRECTORY, about a quarter of the way in, which lists the Montreal association's staff post by post; and the MONTREAL BLOCK OF THE ALPHABETICAL LIST OF EMPLOYED OFFICERS, about three-quarters in, which gives each man's year of entry into Association work. THE QUESTIONS, in priority order. (1) 1910-11 and 1911/12: IS W. J. HOLLIDAY BOYS' WORK DIRECTOR AGAIN? He holds that post in 1907 and 1908, is plain 'Asst.' in 1909 with M. G. BROOKS in it, and opens the camp's new site in 1910 -- and this project has already had to withdraw a claim that the 1910 season was run by the boys' work secretary. (2) Every volume 1910-1920: the Montreal Boys' Work Director year by year, which is the closest thing available to a list of the men over Kanawana through the First World War, the Boys' Department being what ran the camp. (3) 1901-1905: when did W. H. BALL leave the Physical Directorship? He holds it in 1900 and J. E. Merritt has it by 1906, so it is bounded only to that range. (4) M. G. BROOKS in any of them -- new to this project entirely. ALTERNATIVE ROUTES IF NO PERSON IS AVAILABLE: retry the Google Books API on a later day (it returned 429 daily-quota-exceeded, including on the control, so it is untested rather than negative, and the Illinois and Michigan scans were Google-digitised); or request HathiTrust Data API OAuth credentials. STILL MISSING EVEN FROM HATHITRUST: 1883, 1885, 1889, 1912/13, 1914/15, 1920/21. || TESTED 2026-09-06 (f_5207) AND THE OBSTACLE IS NOW NAMED. HathiTrust's BIBLIOGRAPHIC API (catalog.hathitrust.org/api/volumes/) returns 200 from this environment, but babel.hathitrust.org -- both full-text search (/cgi/ls) and page text (/cgi/pt) -- returns 403 with `cf-mitigated: challenge` and a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' interstitial. THAT IS A JAVASCRIPT CHALLENGE, NOT A HATHITRUST REFUSAL AND NOT THE AGENT PROXY: the proxy's status endpoint records no failure for that host. So 'public domain and full view' is true and irrelevant here -- the volumes are one click away for a person with a browser and unreachable for this environment, which is exactly what this priority's 'HUMAN TASK, OR A LATER RETRY' label already anticipated. UNTRIED TWO-STEP WORTH DOING FIRST: use the bibliographic API to identify each volume, then look for the same edition on the Internet Archive, whose full text this project reaches freely. Do that before treating HathiTrust as a dead end.
priorities.notes: Raised 2026-09-06 on closing p_436. Weight 9 because the material is known to exist, known to be public domain, and precisely located -- the only obstacle is a bot challenge. The 1910-11 volume alone would settle a question this project has already got wrong once.

priorities.description: READ THE BOYS' DEPARTMENT SECTIONS OF THE 1892-93 AND 1893-94 ANNUAL REPORTS IN FULL. p_438 searched six cached Montreal YMCA annual reports for the surname Cushing and found four Cushings inside the association in the year of the Lake Saint-Joseph trip, including the recording secretary and a staff member who had argued boys' work before the Kingston Convention (f_4992, f_4993). SEARCHING A REPORT FOR A SURNAME IS NOT READING IT -- rule 21, and rule 23. THE CAMP CAME OUT OF BOYS' WORK, so the Boys' Department's own section in the reports for the years ending 30 April 1893 and 30 April 1894 is the single most likely place in this project's entire cache for a contemporary account of the 1892 Lake Saint-Joseph trip and the committee appointed that autumn. THE 1890-91 REPORT'S BOYS' DEPARTMENT SECTION IS ALREADY KNOWN TO BE SUBSTANTIVE -- it carries the Kingston Convention paragraph and the line 'We also feel the need of a Secretary who will be able to devote his whole time to this department' -- so these sections are narrative, not just lists. FILES, ALL ON DISK: sources/cache/ymca-montreal-fonds/sgw-ymca-annual-report-1892-1893.txt and sgw-ymca-annual-report-1893-1894.txt. ALSO UNREAD: the Cushing hits in the 1893-94 (14), 1894-95 (11) and 1895-96 (13) reports, counted during p_438 and never opened. WHAT TO LOOK FOR: any mention of a summer outing, a camp, an island, Lake Saint-Joseph, Howard township, Sainte-Agathe, tents, or a vacation for boys; the Boys' Department's committee membership year by year; and whether Percy H. Cushing's illegible 1892-93 job title is spelled out anywhere in the narrative. [READ 2026-09-06, and the honest headline is how much was already held. THE 1894-95 REPORT'S CAMP MATERIAL -- 'our first Summer Camp... 23 workers and boys', the 53 members, the land and fishing rights leased from the Government on a lake near St. Agathe, the two parallel streams -- IS ALREADY IN THIS KB at f_2139, f_2141, f_2178 and f_0665 and in the attendance series. It was re-derived here before the grep that would have shown it; the grep came first the second time. THREE THINGS ARE GENUINELY NEW. (1) R. L. CHARLTON CHAIRED THE JUNIOR DEPARTMENT IN 1893-94, the camp's founding year, with P. H. CUSHING as secretary and W. E. CUSHING a member -- this project had Charlton only as an ordinary member of that committee in 1899, under R. B. Ross Jr., who is himself an ordinary member here in 1893-94 (f_4994). (2) THE 1892-93 AND 1893-94 REPORTS MENTION NO CAMP AT ALL -- searched for camp, tent, outing, excursion, St. Joseph, Howard and Agathe; the 1892-93 report returns nothing, the 1893-94 only a militia camp. A summer 1892 trip falls inside the 1892-93 report's year, so this extends this project's existing argument-from-silence across the years that actually matter (f_4995). (3) D. W. CORBETT resigned as the assistant secretary in charge of the Junior Department to become secretary of the HONOLULU ASSOCIATION, which dates and explains his disappearance from the Montreal roster. STILL NOT DONE: the Cushing hits in the 1893-94, 1894-95 and 1895-96 reports, counted during p_438 and still unopened.] [CLOSED 2026-09-06. The Cushing hits in the 1893-94, 1894-95 and 1895-96 reports are now read too, and they give PERCY H. CUSHING A WHOLE CAREER (f_4996): he did NOT start in boys' work -- D. W. Corbett held it until 'the departure of Mr. D. W. Corbett in June, 1893... but Mr. P. H. Cushing was secured as his successor'; he is ASSISTANT SECRETARY in the 1893-94 staff list and Secretary of the Junior Department under Charlton; and in September 1895 he 'resigned to enter the SPRINGFIELD TRAINING SCHOOL', succeeded by C. K. Calhoun of Lindsay, Ont. SO THE MAN IN CHARGE OF MONTREAL'S BOYS' WORK FROM JUNE 1893 TO SEPTEMBER 1895 -- SPANNING THE 1894 FOUNDING -- WAS PERCY H. CUSHING. The department's farewell says he had 'grown up among the boys... both as one of their members and as the Secretary of the Department'. If he is the genealogy's Percy Hill Cushing he died 22 December 1896, fifteen months later, at twenty-four. AND A SECOND DATE TO THE MONTH (f_4997): 'MR. POWTER WAS APPOINTED HIS ASSISTANT IN NOV. 1892' -- C. B. Powter was Ball's assistant from November 1892, four years earlier than the Year Book had him and therefore through the 1894 founding. A tension left open: the 1895-96 report lists him as 'secured as Assistant to the Physical Director' among that year's changes. Also W. F. CHAPMAN as OFFICE SECRETARY in 1893-94, an earlier title than the Year Books give him; and the report's own note that 'the men from Montreal have done our Association honor both while at Springfield', which is the pipeline that brought Ball.]
priorities.notes: Raised 2026-09-06 on advancing p_438. Weight 8 -- higher than most remaining items because the material is already on disk, has never been read, and sits exactly where a contemporary account of the camp's origin would be if one survives in this cache at all.

priorities.description: READ THE 729 SKIMMED SOURCES. THIS IS THE LARGEST REMAINING BODY OF WORK IN THE PROJECT AND IT IS ALL ON DISK. Of 1,666 source records, 734 carry read_state 'skimmed' and one blanket note: 'the text is held and has been keyword-swept repeatedly (Kanawana, Otoreke, director names, drownings, Owens, Patton), but this item has not been read closely and no fact has been extracted from it individually.' [CORRECTED within the hour of raising this priority. It first said: 'A random sample of ten confirms the label is honest -- none is cited anywhere in facts.json.' THE TEST WAS WRONG. Facts from this collection cite the COLLECTION-level id src_ia_ymca_montreal_fonds_collection, not the item-level src_ymf_* ids, so that check returns no for every item in the collection regardless of whether it has been read.] WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, on the three items checked properly: THEY ARE PARTIALLY EXTRACTED, ONE THEME AT A TIME. The 1938 Voice of Youth radio script is labelled skimmed and its MUSIC is fully in the KB at f_2112, while its skit, its cast of five boys, its rehearsal room, its letterhead and an attendance figure of 'over 250 campers and visitors' were all still sitting in it -- now f_5002. The two 1900 camp committee reports are extracted almost completely. So this is not 729 unread documents; it is 729 documents READ FOR SOMETHING, which is rule 21 at the scale of half the corpus, and the residue is real. HOW MUCH residue is unknown and was not measured (f_5001). SO ANYTHING OUTSIDE THAT SIX-ITEM KEYWORD LIST IS INVISIBLE IN ALL OF THEM. That is the same failure this session catalogued five times at the scale of a single query, reproduced at the scale of half the corpus. HOW TO WORK IT, in order of expected yield: (1) THE YMCA OF MONTREAL FONDS ITEMS (src_ymf_*) whose titles name a camp, a committee, a report or a person -- the two 1900 camp committee reports in this collection turned out to be extraordinary documents, giving the 1900 Junior Camp's dates, its 45 boys and 6 leaders by name, its finances and its chef. Others in the same collection are titled for Camp Otoreke songs, Camp Thunderbird, Camp Perrot annual reports, the North Branch, D. A. Budge, R. J. Colville, and 1930s radio broadcasts from Kanawana. (2) THE GREEN TRIANGLE ISSUES, the association's own periodical. (3) THE CANADIAN CAMPING back issues not covered by the word-for-word read. (4) The SGW/YMCA annual reports of the 1990s and 2000s, which bear on the modern era where this wiki is thinnest. BEFORE READING ANY ITEM, CHECK WHETHER ITS source_id ALREADY APPEARS IN facts.json -- at least two records carried the blanket note while having been fully read, and were corrected on 2026-09-06. AND WHEN AN ITEM IS READ, UPDATE ITS read_state, which is what did not happen for those two. HOW TO TEST AN ITEM BEFORE READING IT, since the obvious test does not work: pick strings DISTINCTIVE to that document -- unusual personal names, exact figures, a room, a place -- and grep those against kb/facts.json. Do NOT grep its source_id, and do NOT grep common capitalised phrases; both were tried on 2026-09-06 and both are useless, the second matching 'New York' and 'Park Avenue'. The Voice of Youth script was correctly diagnosed in about a minute by grepping 'Morry Cross', 'Willingdon Room' and 'John Houseman' (absent) against 'Farewell Rock' and 'Sandy Spence' (present). [STARTED 2026-09-06, and the first item read vindicates the priority. THE 1936 CFCF BROADCAST SCRIPT (src_ymf_1936_kamp_kanawana_broadcast_station_cfcf) was labelled skimmed and CITED BY NO ARTICLE. Tested by the per-document method above -- 'water shute', 'bird lore', 'metalcraft', 'leatherwork', 'playfields', 'soap bath', 'senior secretaries' all returned ZERO in facts.json and in the wiki -- and then read whole. It is the EARLIEST of the CFCF series and the ONLY one surviving as TEXT; the media article had recorded that Concordia describes the series as running 1936-1941 with only the 1939 and 1941 audio surviving. It gives the 1909 site purchase, the boys' camp at St. Adolphe de Howard opened 'as a branch of their men's camp', two playfields, the outdoor chapel and Council Ring, a director who is 'one of the senior secretaries of the Montreal Y.M.C.A.', THIRTY-FIVE counsellors with six or seven boys each, a McGill-graduate doctor, a chef of ten years, the daily soap bath and inspection, twelve named interest groups INCLUDING BASKETRY STILL IN 1936, boat- and cabin-building, Life Saving to National Council certificates, and the long water shute from the top of the hill into the lake. f_5003, written into programs-activities.md. NEXT IN THIS COLLECTION, by the same method: 1941-camp-otoreke-songs.txt (64 KB), 1928-report-on-camp-dorval.txt, 1920-biography-of-r-j-colville.txt, 1940-08-23-mr-d-a-budge.txt, the Camp Perrot annual reports, and the Green Triangle run.] [SAMPLE AFTER SIX ITEMS, 2026-09-06: TWO genuinely unread (the 1936 CFCF script, the 1941 Otoreke songbook), ONE partly read (the 1938 Voice of Youth, music extracted and everything else not), THREE already fully read with a stale label (the two 1900 camp committee reports and the 1928 Camp Dorval report). Roughly a third, a third and a third. That is a sample of six, not a measurement of 729, but it is the only honest figure this project has, and it means THE LABEL CANNOT BE TRUSTED IN EITHER DIRECTION -- the per-document test is the only way to know.] [PROGRESS 2026-09-06. FIRST DOCUMENT WORKED, AND IT WAS NOT EVEN IN THE POPULATION. The Lookout Vol. 1 No. 3, the 1993 alumni newsletter, was carrying read_state 'unread' on one record and 'extracted' on another. Read cover to cover: it yielded a signed season report from Director Bruce Netherwood on the 99th summer (99%+ capacity for the fifth consecutive year, four Voyageur trips and 38 camper trips, over 400 paddlers, an 80% staff return rate), an obituary and endowment fund for Maureen McBride, and Sheila Leigh, a 1970s section director named nowhere else in this project -- f_5008 through f_5011. The document had previously been extracted for exactly two things. This is the residue p_441 predicted, on a document outside its 729. [SECOND DOCUMENT, 2026-09-06: src_ymf_1920_biography_of_r_j_colville, read whole. Kanawana zero -- a genuine null, recorded as one. But two facts the keyword sweep could never have reached: a Provincial Convention at Toronto's West End building in JANUARY 1894 attended by '4. A. Budee of Montreal', almost certainly D. A. Budge, in the founding year (f_5014); and a two-week YMCA SUMMER SCHOOL on Stony Lake in the Kawarthas about 1889-90, a conference and not a camp but the institutional habit a camp grows out of (f_5015). The catalogue title calls it a biography; it is autobiographical, and the source title has been corrected. THE READING LESSON: a grep for 'Budge' fails on this page, which reads 'Budee'. The blanket skimmed note on these records says the item was keyword-swept -- that is exactly why nothing was found.] [THIRD DOCUMENT, 2026-09-06: src_ymf_1959_report_of_older_boys_camps_summer, read whole, and it is the best single find of the three. The Voyageurs' first season described by the people who ran it: called the OLDER BOYS CAMP, based ON LAKE WILSON AT KANAWANA and not in the park, six trips, five boys to a leader, and a permanent La Verendrye base as its FIRST RECOMMENDATION rather than a fact of that summer (f_5017). It also gives an institutional reason for the move that this wiki did not have -- 'the close proximity of K.K. retards the natural and full development of the OBC', plus a named prestige conflict with the Pathfinders (f_5018). And a SECOND, UNDATED DOCUMENT is bound into the same scan, a tripper's equipment-and-food letter written after the move (f_5019). Note the file-binding problem again: one scan, two documents, one catalogue date.] [FOURTH DOCUMENT, 2026-09-06: src_ymf_1967_les_voyageurs_de_la_verendrye_camp_directors_report, read whole, and the richest yet. SIX NAMES NEW TO THIS PROJECT: David Blake, Director 1967; trippers David Taube, Paul Mongraw and Bob Matheson; base camp staff Richard Holyoke and Harry Fox at $50.00 each for the summer (f_5020). Plus the pre-camp week at Kanawana as 'a patch and sew period' and a director's itemised tightening of a programme he found loose (f_5021); the routes, the 1938-vintage maps, Canadian International Paper as landlord and its new public campsite putting the camp on the fishermen's path, and a neighbouring Camp Kapitachouane on Lac Choiseul (f_5022); and the safety and liability passages -- 'the first aid kit proves itself to be something of a joke', a crew leaderless for 24 hours 'and legally wide open for action' (f_5023).] [FIFTH AND SIXTH DOCUMENTS, 2026-09-06: the 1928 and 1929 'Come to Kanawana' brochures, read whole, and they are the best yield of the day. HAROLD C. CROSS'S YMCA TITLE, which his article has been asking for since February: 'Executive Secretary of Westmount Y.M.C.A.' (f_5027). A GAP YEAR CLOSED: George Porteous, B.A., Boys' Work Secretary of North Branch YMCA, is Chief Director for 1929, so the directors index's '1929-1931' hole is now 1930-1931 (f_5029). A DOCUMENTED PERSON CROSSING FROM TAYLOR STATTEN'S CAMP: Karl R. Perry, 'for five years on the staff at Camp Ahmek in Algonquin Park', hired in 1928 to start Kanawana's craft department (f_5028). THE CAMP'S OWN SEASON COUNT: the 1929 brochure's cover says '20th SEASON', which puts season one at 1910 and dates the institution's self-understanding to the Saint-Sauveur site rather than to 1894 (f_5030). Plus roughly thirty named staff across the two years with their winter jobs, the plant and the fees, and a dated end for 'the old Otoreke Hike' (f_5031).] [SEVENTH DOCUMENT, 2026-09-06: src_ymf_1947_report_of_the_montreal_ymca_camp_perrot_for_boys_and_girls, read whole. Camp Perrot's 1947 leadership named -- O. N. H. Owens as Chairman (corroboration; the Order of Owens article already had him on that board) and A. T. DODDS as Camp Director, with his wife VERLIE DODDS signing the Girls' Camp report as Directress in her first administrative year, so a married couple ran the two halves of the season (f_5032). Plus about twenty-five more named staff, the branch quota table showing how a city association shared out a camp, the fourth-season confirmation of the 1944 founding, and two pressures on the site in the same document: a colony of cottagers arriving after 1946 and spring flooding that ate the shoreline (f_5033). SEVEN CACHED PERROT REPORTS REMAIN UNREAD -- 1948, 1950, 1951, 1952, 1953, 1954 and 1958 -- and on this evidence each carries a named staff.] [EIGHTH DOCUMENT, 2026-09-06: the 1948 Camp Perrot item, read whole, and it is A FIFTH KIND OF MISLABELLING. The catalogue calls it a season report; it is an unsigned 'Suggestions / Recommendations' list with no attendance figures and no staff. Source title corrected. It still pays: the barn's conversion to crafts and stage, the camp GIVING UP ITS GARDEN because 'the campers felt it was an imposition on their time', a tuck shop wanted to keep people away from 'the nearby and in my opinion, undesirable restaurant around the corner', a proposal to strip a dying tree for campers to carve their initials on, and the 1947 cottage-encroachment problem now named -- a triangle of farmland the committee was trying to buy, and next door the Lalondes, who were extending their house instead of selling (f_5034).] [NINTH AND TENTH DOCUMENTS, 2026-09-06: the 1943 Camp Thunderbird report and brochure, read whole, plus the Thunderbird passages of the 1943 and 1944 annual reports. A CAMP THIS PROJECT KNEW ONLY AS A FINDING-AID NUMBER (P0145/12I) NOW HAS AN ARTICLE. It was a one-week boys' camp on an island in the riviere des Mille Iles near Sainte-Rose and Sainte-Eustache, twenty miles from Montreal, run by Central branch in 1943 and 1944, twenty-two people, $7 a week, ration books to be handed in before departure. Directed by A. T. DODDS, Associate Boys' Work Secretary of Central -- the same man who directed Camp Perrot, with Mrs Dodds as dietician here and as Girls' Camp Directress there four years later (f_5035, f_5036). AND THE ASSOCIATION'S OWN VERDICT: 'an experimental near-the-city camp... our experience has proven the need for a permanent camp of this nature, which could be used by boys and girls throughout the summer' -- written in 1944, the year Camp Perrot opened as exactly that. The succession is left as an explicitly unproven reading (f_5037).] [ELEVENTH DOCUMENT, 2026-09-06: src_ymf_1961_the_otoreke_ymca_ski_lodge_a_review, read whole, and it ANSWERS A QUESTION camp-otoreke.md has carried since 25 August. That article's ski-lodge section was written from the finding aid alone and ends 'none of these files has been read'. This review gives the lodge's whole history: rented houses at Ste-Adele in 1940 and Piedmont in 1941, then a permanent site in 1945 on Elder's Farm, Christieville, found by Frank B. Peterson, Bud Horton and C. J. McGerrigle to criteria the committee wrote down -- 'handy to the railroad, immediately upon skiable hills, and away from towns' (f_5040). Capital expenditure of $31,550 itemised, income from the later 1940s to 1961 peaking at $10,345 in 1959 and falling to $6,200, membership 143 down to 45, and the note that everything but the purchase price came out of Otoreke camp and lodge income (f_5041). And a closing section explaining the decline that is the best social history this corpus has produced: the ski trains gone and with them 'the forest of skis stretching from the station gate away back to Jean Talon Street', the Autoroute making day-trippers, the rope tows at Mont Christie about to be replaced, and a group of former Otoreke campers choosing Stowe and Jay Peak instead -- 'Why not spend a weekend at the Y Lodge?' 'What with rope tows!' (f_5042). THE ARTICLE'S SECTION HEADING WAS ALSO WRONG, dated 1929-1959 from the finding aid's span while the lodge was still running in 1961-62; corrected.] [TWELFTH AND THIRTEENTH DOCUMENTS, 2026-09-06, AND BOTH ARE NEGATIVE RESULTS WORTH HAVING. (1) src_ymf_1938_11_07_kanawana_goes_on_the_air, read whole: THE FIRST DOCUMENT OF THIS PASS TO YIELD NOTHING NEW. Its letterhead names O. N. H. Owens as Chairman and W. J. G. MacDiarmid as Director, both already in the directors index and the order-of-owens article; the broadcast it announces is already f_2112 and f_5002. A one-page rehearsal notice signed 'CHIEF', fully mined. Marked extracted with that basis so nobody reads it a third time. (2) src_ymf_1971_09_07_rapport_ete_71_camp_de_langue_francaise, read whole: KANAWANA ZERO, a genuine null, and kept for association context rather than for Kanawana -- a French-language urban day camp in Little Burgundy the same summer, twenty-four children, eight staff, no park or outdoor pool in the district, swimming indoors at the Bain des Seigneurs, and the camp displaced through the school until it finished 'dans les douches attenantes au gymnase' (f_5043). NO ARTICLE SPAWNED: the subject is not Kanawana and CLAUDE.md's folder rules have no place for it. TWELVE OF THIRTEEN DOCUMENTS HAVE PAID; the rate is not going to hold and the negative results are being recorded so the ratio stays honest.] [FOURTEENTH DOCUMENT, 2026-09-06: src_ymf_annual_report_1976_125_colourful_years, read for its timeline and building-fund plan (the branch reporting is unread and the record says so). TWO FINDINGS THAT CHANGE OTHER ARTICLES. (1) AN ECOLOGY CENTRE AT KANAWANA WAS A FUNDING PLANK IN 1976: the $9.5M campaign's 'Camping & Outdoor Education' category lists a northern base camp for tripping and wilderness survival, YEAR-ROUND FACILITIES at Kanawana, and 'Development of an ECOLOGY CENTRE at Kamp Kanawana', with the summary promising to make the camp 'a year-round camping and outdoor education centre'. wiki/traditions/environmental-history.md dates that repositioning to a 2006 'virage vert'; it was proposed and costed thirty years earlier (f_5044). The amount is illegible -- the columns are right-aligned and the OCR drifts them -- and is NOT guessed. (2) THE ASSOCIATION'S OWN FOUNDING SENTENCE: '1894 The Y opened the first organized boys' camp at St. Adolphe de Howard. Shortly after the boys' section moved to St. Sauveur, and organized Kamp Kanawana.' It asserts primacy unqualified, corroborates Saint-Adolphe-d'Howard from institutional memory, and compresses sixteen years into 'shortly after' -- against the camp's own brochures, which had been counting seasons from 1910 since at least 1929 (f_5045). NEXT IN THIS SEAM: whether the 1976 ecology centre was ever built. The annual reports of 1977-1985 are cached.] [DOCUMENTS FIFTEEN TO TWENTY, 2026-09-06: the Camp Perrot annual reports for 1950, 1951, 1952, 1953, 1954 and 1958, read for their TITLE-PAGE OFFICER BLOCKS AND SIGNATURES ONLY -- the bodies are unread and the records say so. A near-continuous leadership line: A. Ross Seaman directing in 1951, then DONALD COCHRANE FROM 1952 TO AT LEAST 1958, seven seasons, which makes him Camp Perrot's longest documented director where this wiki knew him only as the author of a 1959 memo. Margaret Seaman as Girls' Camp Director 1952 and Maureen Ring 1958; Gordon Mackey and Scott F. Kneeland chairing; Hedley Dimock on the 1958 committee (f_5048). The reports' own ordinals -- eighth 1951, ninth 1952, tenth 1953 -- corroborate the 1944 founding twice more. AND A CROSS-CAMP NAME LEFT OPEN: Scott Kneeland ran Kanawana's workshop in 1929 and Scott F. Kneeland chaired the association's Boys' Camping Committee in 1952-54; uncommon name, same institution, plausible arc, NO DOCUMENT NAMING BOTH ROLES, so not identified (f_5049).] [DOCUMENT TWENTY-ONE, 2026-09-06: the 1960 Voyageurs report's promotion and appendix material, read (the equipment, food and rating sections are still unread and the record says so). The satellite recruited OUT OF THE PARENT CAMP BY NOMINATION: three thousand folders by 15 March, to previous Voyageurs, to all Montreal branches, and to 'all senior campers of Kamp Kanawana who the previous year were recommended by the Section Director and the Section Program Director'. And 'Jack was the only leader with previous experience with the Voyageurs' plus 'all previous Voyageurs' both presuppose earlier years, supporting the 1959 Older Boys Camp as the same programme under another name and telling against the 1963 report's 'three year history' (f_5050). A NEAR MISS WORTH RECORDING: the table of contents lists an appendix the OCR renders 'Suggested Nong', which I began to write up as SONGS -- relevant to the blocked p_048 -- before checking the report's own cross-references, which call Appendix 6 'the recommended menu' in one place and 'group development forms' in another. The appendices were renumbered and THE SCAN STOPS AFTER APPENDIX 4, so none of it is checkable. Recorded as an unresolved lead, not a song source. That is the fourth time today a one-character OCR reading nearly became a fact.] [DOCUMENT TWENTY-TWO, 2026-09-06: the 1963 Voyageurs annual report, read whole, AND THE FIRST OF THIS PASS TO NEED THE EMBARGO MACHINERY. Three findings. (1) LAC LANDRON IS NOT WHERE THE VOYAGEURS STARTED: 'this year the base camp site was moved from LAC NANOUATON to the lower end of Lac Landron', a place-name occurring nowhere else in this project, and the lease was still unobtained in 1963 and still being urged in 1966. The canoe-trips article had the 1959 choice and the Landron lease as one movement; it is four steps (f_5052). (2) THE CAMP WROTE DOWN ITS PHILOSOPHY and it is a critique of organised camping written by a camp -- 'in many camps a Program Director sets down a program they are to follow... our program is merely living in the bush' -- held to through a twelve-day fire closure that trapped the camp at base (f_5051). (3) THE STAFF SECTION assesses six named seasonal staff individually and is now REGISTER ENTRY r_0003, review 2040-01-01: written into canoe-trips.md inside an embargo marker with a note outside it, registered, and with two institutional elements deliberately left unembargoed -- a hiring experiment testing bush skills against youth-work experience, and an 'attitude scale of counselor prediction' attributed to Dr. Dimock (f_5053). THE 1974 AND 1979 VOYAGEUR REPORTS CAN NOW BE DONE THE SAME WAY; they were deferred this morning for want of this pattern.] [DOCUMENT TWENTY-THREE, 2026-09-06: the 1974 Voyageurs report, read whole with the embargo pattern now in hand. PAUL MONGRAW DATES HIMSELF -- 'I've worked for Les Voyageurs since 1967' -- closing from his own pen the arc f_5024 had noticed from outside, and adding that a tripper's summer pay was $450 in 1974, 'the same as I got for my first summer back in 1967'. He argues for bilingual parent forms in the year of Bill 22 ('we deserve abominations like Bill 22 if we make no effort to translate into French'), sets out the arithmetic of why a crew is six, and asks for a camper interview against the boy 'shanghaied by his parents' (f_5054). AND THE PROGRAMME'S LATE SHAPE: by 1974 Les Voyageurs had LOST ITS BASE CAMP for want of a truck and was operating out of Kanawana again, with its director forecasting that it 'will inevitably be absorbed by the Hike and Trip department of Kanawana and will cease to be a separate operation' -- the 1959 complaint returning fifteen years later. He also wanted out of La Verendrye entirely, the fees onerous and the fishing clubs touchy, eyeing the new James Bay roads '(ugh)' (f_5055). ONE NUMBERED POLICY ITEM IS NOW EMBARGO r_0004, review 2050: a sustained criticism of the unnamed Kanawana caretaker, which names a post rather than a person and is therefore recoverable from any roster of the season (f_5056). THE 1979 REPORT IS THE LAST OF THE DEFERRED PAIR AND CAN BE DONE THE SAME WAY.] [DOCUMENT TWENTY-FOUR, 2026-09-06: the 1979 Voyageurs report, read whole -- the second and last of the pair deferred this morning for want of the embargo pattern. TWO REVERSALS IN ONE DOCUMENT. COEDUCATION IS ROUTINE: 'two out of five trips this summer were coed trips... if registration permits then all girl trips should be encouraged.' AND THE CREW OF SIX IS ABANDONED for three canoes, two staff and up to seven campers -- exactly what Paul Mongraw argued against in 1974 -- justified by a sentence worth the whole document: 'anyway, THERE IS VERY LITTLE "WILDERNESS" LEFT IN THE LA VERENDRYE AREA and it is not as important as it once was to have highly mobile "disciplined" groups' (f_5057). Plus a SECOND STAFF grade this project had not recorded, camper information files begun that year, the age floor raised from 13 to 14, and a 1979 marketing plan of posters, weekend colour supplements, silkscreened T-shirts and a slide show. THE STAFF EVALUATIONS, more than half the report, are EMBARGO r_0005, review 2060 (f_5058). A THIRD SELF-CAUGHT ERROR IN THE EMBARGO MACHINERY: I put the roster in the embargoed fact and the names in the open article, and restricted_guard correctly flagged it -- a name held ONLY in an embargoed fact must not appear loose. Fixed by moving the roster into the open fact, which is also the right answer on the merits: who ran the camp is institutional, what one man thought of another's temperament is not.] [DOCUMENT TWENTY-FIVE, 2026-09-06: the 1970 Voyageurs director's report, read whole, AND IT MOVES A DATE BY FOUR YEARS. Mongraw's 1974 forecast that the programme would be absorbed into Kanawana's Hike and Trip department was not a premonition: THE PROPOSAL HAD ALREADY BEEN MADE IN 1970 and Yves St. Pierre wrote his refusal into his report -- 'it has been suggested that Les Voyageurs de la Verendrye as we know it be discontinued; that the operation be moved to Kamp Kanawana, and that the trips be reduced to two weeks.
