ALSO: free camperships for 'a group of INNER-CITY YOUNGSTERS who would not otherwise have had out-of-city holidays', 2,600 children in day camps and 'BACK-ALLEY PROGRAMS', and from the 1971-72 report, day camps at N.D.G. and Westmount 'AGAIN operated FRENCH-LANGUAGE SECTIONS FOR ENGLISH-SPEAKING YOUNGSTERS' with Verdun-Lasalle's 'a completely bilingual operation' -- the day-camp counterpart of the Living-in-French section introduced at the resident camp in 1969, and 'again' puts them earlier still (f_5111).] [DOCUMENTS SEVENTY-ONE TO SEVENTY-FOUR, 2026-09-06: the reports for 1973-74, 1974-75, 1976-77 and 1977-78. THE 1974-75 ONE I RE-READ WITHOUT GREPPING FIRST and it was already extracted and corrected in attendance-series -- rule 35 for the second time today. It still paid, because the re-read found two things the existing correction had not addressed. THE VOLUME NEVER STATES ITS YEAR-END MONTH: only 'the Association's 1974-1975 fiscal year' and financial columns headed '1973/74 1974/75'. The 31 May year-end for this era rests on the 1972-73 and 1981-82 volumes, not this one -- and since a year ending 31 May 1975 cannot contain the summer of 1975, the correction's conclusion implies either that this report describes a season after its own fiscal close or that its year-end is not 31 May. Flagged under p_450, correction not reopened (the camp's own report and the arithmetic both support it). AND 'SECOND HIGHEST REGISTRATION IN 25 YEARS', which attendance-series quotes without testing, IS FALSE FOR CAMPER COUNTS -- 475 ranks about tenth in 1950-1975 -- and nearly right for CAMPER-WEEKS, where 1,356 is third behind 1969 and 1970. The weeks reading is offered and not adopted, since the report does not say which it means (f_5112). THE 1973-74 REPORT IS A GREP NULL for 'kanawana' across 23,664 characters, recorded as 'swept' rather than read. THE 1976-77 REPORT has one item in both columns: 'commencement of the planning process for NEW FACILITIES at Kamp Kanawana', no detail. Four years after the completed all-season proposal and two years before Katimavik opened; THE SEQUENCE IS THE SHAPE TO TEST against the camp's own reports for those years, not a claim.] [DOCUMENT SEVENTY-FIVE, 2026-09-06: 'PROPOSAL FOR FRENCH LANGUAGE DAY CAMP, SUMMER 1968', Montreal YMCA International Branch, 3 May 1968, signed R.S. WILSON, Director. Read end to end, all 15,493 characters. NOT A KANAWANA DOCUMENT -- it never mentions the camp -- but it is where the French-language camping thread starts, two years before Kanawana's own Living-in-French section of 1969 (f_5103) and before the branch day camps the 1971-72 report says were 'again' running French sections (f_5111). NO DOCUMENT CONNECTS THEM AND NO DESCENT IS ASSERTED. THE 1967 EXPERIMENT ran with thirty children. THE PROBLEM AS THE BRANCH STATED IT is immigrant children facing French as a THIRD language: 'if he wishes to succeed within the educational system he is forced to learn a third language... this becomes an odious task... creates frustrations and fears'. Its neighbourhood 'has the largest immigrant population in the city' and is 'a series of villages between whom there is a minimum of communication'. THE CHILDREN'S OWN WORDS are recorded -- 'when someone speaks to me, I understand them. It makes sense' and 'it was not really learning at all... it was fun' -- as is the failure: 'the group leaders made the mistake of frequently conversing in English. Once this was established they had a continual battle to enforce the "French only" rule.' The 1968 plan was 200 children in two three-week periods on a $5,140 budget, ten counsellors at $350 for seven weeks including a week's training. ONE FIGURE NOT TAKEN AS PRINTED: the middle subsidy OCRs as '$ 360.' where the arithmetic requires $3,640, and the fact says so (f_5113, programs-activities label ifl). STILL UNREAD IN THIS CLUSTER: src_ymf_1968_french_day_camp_report (the season report answering this proposal), src_ymf_1971_01_25_french_program_summer_71, and src_ymf_1972_04_the_mile_end_francophone_project_submission -- which connects to the 'Projet Mile End West' named in the 1970-71 annual report. src_ymf_1971_09_07_rapport_ete_71_camp_de_langue_francaise is already extracted. [DOCUMENT SEVENTY-SIX, 2026-09-06: 'INTERNATIONAL Y.M.C.A. FRENCH DAY CAMP REPORT 1968', R. Wilson, read end to end -- the season report answering the May proposal. THE MONEY FAILED COMPLETELY: 'no support was found', with all TEN refusing organisations named, from the St-Jean-Baptiste Society and two Club Richelieu chapters to the Board of Trade and the Ministere des Affaires culturelles. AGAINST A TARGET OF 200 the periods took 73 and 53, and the report states the reason -- first-period campers 'wanted to return... but would not be able to because of the cost'. Six then fifteen campers subsidised, up to the full $12, with the director's own verdict that subsidy 'will never be completely effective in reaching all the people who are unable to pay'. THE METHOD IS RECONSTRUCTABLE: an hour of vocabulary each morning chosen for that day's activities, then used in the activity. AND THE SAME FAILURE AS 1967, FOLLOWED THROUGH TO ITS COST: the French-only rule was unenforceable in the children's own planning sessions, 'all the counsellors reported extreme difficulty', and so 'the amount of actual involvement of members in planning their own program was much less than is desirable' -- a camp noticing that two of its principles pulled against each other and writing it down instead of choosing (f_5114, programs-activities label ifl68). NOT TRANSCRIBED: the French test results appendix and the financial statement, both in the cached file. STILL UNREAD IN THIS CLUSTER: src_ymf_1971_01_25_french_program_summer_71 and src_ymf_1972_04_the_mile_end_francophone_project_submission. [DOCUMENT SEVENTY-SEVEN, 2026-09-06: 'FRENCH PROGRAM SUMMER 71', 25 January 1971, Kerry W. Johnston, Director, MILE END WEST PROJECT. Read end to end. 'KANAWANA' OCCURS ZERO TIMES -- a null for this wiki's subject, recorded as one on the precedent of f_5043, and kept because it dates and sizes every stage of the thread whose branch reached Kanawana in 1969. THE ARC: 30 children in 1967, 126 in 1968 with no funding, 300 IN 1970 on money from the SOCIAL ACTION BRANCH, CITIZENSHIP DEPARTMENT OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE, and a 1971 plan for 4,500 across twenty decentralised sites from St. Lawrence Boulevard to Baie d'Urfe. TWO THINGS CHANGED IN 1970 and the document says so: the emphasis moved from THE FRENCH LANGUAGE TO EXPOSURE TO QUEBEC CULTURE, and they began using UNILINGUAL COUNSELLORS -- which is the answer to the problem the 1967 and 1968 reports could not solve, since the French-only rule was unenforceable while the counsellors could speak English. THE FRAMING IS THE OCTOBER CRISIS, three months on: 'the recent Quebec crisis has had the effect of further polarizing this society... the "two solitudes" become more and more a reality', and the Y describing itself as 'a basically anglophone institution' with a responsibility to promote understanding. Budget $196,000, subsidy requested $96,000. THE DOCUMENT'S OWN ARITHMETIC IS INCONSISTENT -- narrative 4,500 children, income line 4,000 -- and I recorded that rather than reconciling it (f_5115, programs-activities label mew). NEXT IN THIS CLUSTER: src_ymf_1972_04_the_mile_end_francophone_project_submission, still unread, which should say whether the 4,500 happened; f_5043 already has the 1971 Petite-Bourgogne season report and the two want reading against each other. [DOCUMENTS SEVENTY-EIGHT TO EIGHTY-ONE, 2026-09-06. THE 1972 MILE-END FRANCOPHONE PROJECT SUBMISSION IS A CLEAN NULL: 'kanawana', 'camp', 'summer' and 'ete' occur ZERO TIMES in it. A community development submission about a Montreal neighbourhood with no camping component. Its social-conditions description is kept in f_5116 as context for the French camp cluster -- it tells you what the 'Mile End West Project' the 1971 camp submission was signed from actually was -- and is DELIBERATELY NOT IN ANY ARTICLE. Marked extracted so nobody opens it looking for camping. THE THREE DAY CAMP DOCUMENTS (July 1985, October 1987, and the recommendations of 26 February 1988) each name Kanawana once or twice and PAY: by the mid-1980s the camp was where the city day camps sent their SENIOR STAFF FOR TRAINING -- 1985 'took place in Kanawana. Very successful'; 1987 'our major training event for senior staff, at Kamp Kanawana', with topics listed and the organiser noting it cost 14 days of his time and 'no real time was spent on development. All we have time for is maintaining'. AND IN FEBRUARY 1988 THEY ASKED FOR A PERMANENT SITE: 'we need to develop a site on Kamp Kanawana for the use of Day Camps -- Summer 89', plus 'Day Camp should be tied into the promotion of Kamp Kanawana'. Whether the site was developed is not in these documents and this project has nothing on either side of it. THIS IS OFF-SEASON INSTITUTIONAL USE OF THE PROPERTY a decade before year-round operation is usually dated, and it is now a section in winter-programming (f_5117, source 20).
priorities.notes: Raised 2026-09-06 at the end of a session that spent its day on external corpora. The finding that closes that session is that the biggest untouched seam is internal. Weight 10: nothing else in the queue is this large, this certain to contain material, or this cheap to reach.

priorities.description: FIND THE DOUBLE-REGISTERED DOCUMENTS. The 1928 Report on Camp Dorval has TWO source records for one document: src_camp_dorval_1928, which carries the content, is marked 'extracted' and has NO cache_path; and src_cache_1928_report_on_camp_dorval, which points at the cached text and was marked 'unread'. NEITHER POINTS AT THE OTHER. So the same document was simultaneously extracted and unread depending on which record you happened to read, and it appeared in neither a 'skimmed' count nor an 'extracted' one consistently. This was found by accident on 2026-09-06 while citing it, when data_integrity rejected a made-up source id. HOW MANY OTHERS ARE LIKE THIS IS UNKNOWN. WHAT TO DO: for every source record with a cache_path, look for another record whose title or date matches the same document but which has no cache_path, and vice versa. The src_cache_* prefix is a strong signal -- those records appear to have been generated from the cache directory, while the substantive records were created by hand when the document was read, so the pair is probably systematic rather than a one-off. Report the count first, before merging anything: MERGING IS NOT OBVIOUSLY RIGHT, since the two records may carry different provenance, and the no-silent-overwrite rule applies to source records as much as to facts. The useful output is a list, and a decision from the operator about whether to merge, cross-reference, or leave them and fix the read_state on the cache copies. RELATED: this bears directly on p_441, whose whole premise is that read_state tells you what to read. It does not, in either direction. [COUNTED 2026-09-06, and the answer is systematic. 236 records carry the src_cache_ prefix; 69 have a twin elsewhere under the same name without it -- src_cache_X / src_X. IN 68 OF THE 69 THE CACHE RECORD IS 'unread' WHILE ITS TWIN IS ALREADY 'extracted' (58) or 'skimmed' (10). So of 72 records marked unread in the whole corpus, 68 ARE SHADOWS OF DOCUMENTS ALREADY READ, and only four are unaccounted for: src_cache_the_lookout_vol_1_no_3, src_cache_ymca_history_1873, src_cache_p0145_ymca_of_montreal_fonds_findingaid_2023_11_24, and src_ymca_yearbook_hathitrust_holdings_2026 (created today and unread by design, HathiTrust refusing this environment). 'UNREAD: 72' MEANT 'UNREAD: 4'. f_5006. NOTHING WAS MERGED, as this priority required. THE DECISION IS THE OPERATOR'S: merge the pairs, cross-reference them, or leave them and simply fix the read_state on the cache copies. Note that the two records in a pair may carry different provenance -- one hand-made when the document was read, the other generated from the cache directory -- so a merge would lose something. WHAT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH: the 734 'skimmed' records are a different population, the src_ymf_* fonds items with the blanket keyword-sweep note, and only ten of the twins are among them. p_441 stands.] [EXTENDED 2026-09-06, and the count is now known to be a floor. The Lookout is a twin the name-matching pass CANNOT see: src_cache_the_lookout_vol_1_no_3 and src_ia_the_lookout_1993 are the same digitized issue under names that differ by more than the prefix. So one of f_5006's 'only four genuinely unread' records was itself a shadow, and the real double-registration count is unknown and larger than 69. [CORRECTED same day by running it: that sentence said the right detector is the cache path, and that a cache_path comparison would have caught this pair since both records point into the same file. BOTH HALVES WERE WRONG -- src_ia_the_lookout_1993 has cache_path null, as does src_camp_dorval_1928. THE SUBSTANTIVE RECORD NEVER HAS THE PATH.] The detector that works matches the cache FILENAME STEM against the TITLE of pathless records: 201 candidate pairs, 50 disagreeing about read_state, 32 of those invisible to name matching (f_5013). See f_5012. The two records were cross-referenced in their notes, NOT merged; the operator decision p_442 asks for is unchanged.] [EXTENDED AGAIN 2026-09-06: a THIRD hiding pattern, found by walking into it. src_ymf_the_green_triangle_1933_07_08 (skimmed, has the file) shadows src_green_triangle_1933_07_08 (extracted, no path), and the stem detector missed it because the FILENAME DATES THE ISSUE 1933-07-08 WHILE THE TITLE DATES IT 'July 8, 1933'. Month names and zero-padded digits do not compare. duplicate_sources.py now folds months to numbers and strips leading zeros: 201 pairs becomes 207, and 50 read_state disagreements become 54. See f_5063.] [ADVANCED 2026-09-06: the detector was too strict and is now relaxed. It required a cache filename's tokens to be a SUBSET of another record's title, which cannot see a pair whose filename carries a token the title lacks -- 'sgw-ymca-annual-report-1966-67' against 'YMCA Montreal Annual Report 1966-67'. MIN_OVERLAP set to 0.75. CANDIDATE PAIRS WENT 207 TO 283 AND READ-STATE DISAGREEMENTS 54 TO 117. Still nothing merged, and merging is still an operator decision. But the disagreements are now known to be worse than a bookkeeping annoyance: see p_451 and f_5098, where an 'extracted' record derived from the citation graph was hiding the 1967 co-ed camping announcement.]
priorities.notes: Raised 2026-09-06 out of a data_integrity failure. Weight 7: it does not add facts, but every planning decision about what to read next depends on read_state being meaningful, and right now it is not.

priorities.description: WHEN DID MAUREEN McBRIDE DIRECT CAMP OOLAHWAN, AND WHO WAS SHE? Her 1993 obituary in The Lookout calls her 'a Camp Director at Camp Oolahwan' and gives no dates, which makes her the fourth named director of that camp and puts her in one of two blank spans (1919-1945, or after 1979) without saying which (f_5009). Independently, the YMCA of Montreal's annual reports put her on the Kamp Kanawana Committee 1988-1992 and on the association's board in 1991-92 (f_5010). WHAT IS UNTRIED: the Montreal Gazette for May 1993 (a death notice is likely and the Gazette of that year is not freely searchable from this environment -- record any failure as an access result, not a null); Dawson College's own records for the teaching post, which the annual reports pointedly do NOT corroborate since her board entry alone carries no employer; the LAC series 'Camp Oolahwan committee minutes, reports and training programmes, 1916-1974', which will only help if her tenure falls before 1974; and the YWCA of Montreal directly. FOUR WEB QUERIES ACROSS THREE SURFACES RETURNED NOTHING on 2026-09-06 -- that is four short of the Phase 2 exhaustion standard and is logged as such. SECOND TARGET IN THE SAME PLACE: her song sessions are described as the thing she was known for, which makes her the strongest named lead this project has on where the camp's later song repertory came from -- p_048.
priorities.notes: Raised 2026-09-06 with the maureen-mcbride article, which is at draft. Weight 6: two of the four leads are institutional-contact leads rather than agent-retryable ones.

priorities.description: REBUILD THE DOUBLE-REGISTRATION DETECTOR ON CACHE PATHS, NOT NAMES. f_5006 counted 69 duplicate source records by matching names either side of the src_cache_ prefix; f_5012 shows that method missed at least one (src_cache_the_lookout_vol_1_no_3 / src_ia_the_lookout_1993), and both of those records point into the SAME cache file, so a cache_path comparison would have caught it. [DONE 2026-09-06, and the premise was wrong. Grouping by cache_path finds 16 groups in 1,668 records and ONE read_state disagreement, because the substantive record in these pairs has no cache_path at all -- not the Lookout's, not the 1928 Camp Dorval report's. scripts/reread/duplicate_sources.py implements both the path grouping (kept, so the negative result stays visible) and --stems, which matches the cache FILENAME STEM against the TITLE of pathless records and is the mode that works: 201 candidate pairs, 50 disagreeing about read_state, 32 of those invisible to name matching. f_5013.] f_5006 already noted 16 shared paths and dismissed most as legitimate collection-plus-item pairs; that dismissal was made by eye and should be redone against the full list, because the legitimate case (a collection record and its items) and the broken case (two records for one document disagreeing about whether it has been read) look identical until you check the read_state. THE OUTPUT IS A LIST AND A COUNT, NOT A MERGE -- p_442's operator decision still stands and nothing should be merged before it.
priorities.notes: Raised 2026-09-06 from the Lookout case. Weight 8: this is the measurement that tells the project how much of its own read_state it can trust, and p_441's whole premise depends on it. | Completed 2026-09-06 the same day it was raised; the correction is recorded in place because the priority as written asserted a detector that does not work.

priorities.description: FIND THE LES VOYAGEURS DIRECTORS' REPORTS FOR 1963, 1964 AND 1965. The 1967 report tells the reader to 'see the comments of 1963-64-65 Directors', so three more annual reports of the satellite camp existed and each would name a director and his trippers, exactly as the 1967 one does (f_5020). WHERE TO LOOK FIRST, and it is cheap: this repo already holds src_ymf_1963_les_voyageurs_de_la_verendrye_annual_report and src_ymf_1966_les_voyageurs_de_la_verendrye_report and src_ymf_1960_les_voyageurs_de_la_verendrye_report, all marked skimmed and all unread -- so at least one of the three named years is ON DISK NOW. Read the whole 1960-1979 Voyageurs run in order; there are nine such items in the fonds cache. Then Concordia P145 sub-series 12K (Les Voyageurs de la Verendrye), which the canoe-trips article already cites for exploratory trip logs of 1958 and a c.1959 budget, for 1964 and 1965 if they are not in the cache. EXPECTED YIELD IS HIGH: the satellite ran its own staff, and until today this project had not one of their names. [WORKED 2026-09-06, SIGNATURE BLOCKS ONLY, and it produced EIGHT DIRECTORS where this project had none: Gus Oki (1960), unsigned (1963), Jack Soule (1966), David Blake (1967-69), Yves St. Pierre (1970), John Evans (1973), Paul Mongraw (1974) and Robert D. Woodhouse (1979) -- f_5024. Plus the satellite's founding staff, hired by Kanawana's own director A. Ross Seaman with Jack Organ, the director engaged LAST (f_5025), and a counting problem: the 1963 report calls that year the largest of a THREE YEAR history, which cannot be squared with a 1959 'initial year of operation' and a full 1960 season, and is flagged rather than resolved (f_5026). WHAT REMAINS AND IT IS MOST OF IT: eight of these reports were read for their signatures and one or two passages and NOTHING ELSE, and their source records now say so in read_state_basis. The 1974 and 1979 reports carry INDIVIDUAL STAFF ASSESSMENTS and will need the CLAUDE.md embargo treatment when read properly. 1964 and 1965 are still not located; 1961, 1962, 1971, 1972 and 1975-78 are not in the cache at all.]

priorities.description: WHICH ISLAND WAS CAMP THUNDERBIRD ON, AND DID IT RUN AFTER 1944? The new wiki/site/camp-thunderbird.md has three place-names bracketing a few kilometres of the riviere des Mille Iles -- 'near Ste. Eustache' (brochure text), 'c/o Mme. Lupi, Ste. Rose West' (the camp's mail address) and 'near Plage Laval' (1944 annual report) -- and no island name (f_5036). WHAT TO TRY: NRCan historical topographic maps for the Laval / Deux-Montagnes sheets of the 1940s, which name the river's islands; the Commission de toponymie du Quebec; BAnQ's cartographic collection; and Sainte-Rose parish or municipal records, where 'Mme. Lupi' may also be findable. SECOND AND CHEAPER JOB, DO IT FIRST: the annual reports for 1945 onward are cached in this repo and their camper-numbers tables have a line per camp. Check whether 'Thunderbird' appears in them. That settles open question 2 of the new article in minutes and needs no external source. THIRD: whether Camp Perrot is documented anywhere as Thunderbird's successor -- P0145/12H and the 1944-45 camp committee minutes (f_5037). [SECOND JOB DONE 2026-09-06, same hour: 'Thunderbird' occurs ZERO TIMES in the annual reports for 1945 through 1952, and the 1945 camper table carries Perrot where Thunderbird had been. Two summers, then. BUT IT OPENED A BIGGER QUESTION: those tables appear to LAG THE SEASON BY A YEAR -- the 1945 report's Kanawana 400 is this wiki's 1944 figure and the 1947 report's 302 is its 1946 figure -- which decides whether Thunderbird ran 1942-43 or 1943-44 and bears on every 1940s row of the attendance series (f_5038). THE FIRST AND THIRD JOBS STAND: which island, and whether Perrot is documented as the successor.] [OPEN QUESTION 2 AND ITS SUCCESSOR BOTH CLOSED 2026-09-06 (f_5039). WHAT REMAINS IS THE ISLAND, AND JOB THREE: whether Perrot is documented anywhere as Thunderbird's successor. The handover is now exact to the season -- Thunderbird's last summer is 1943, Perrot's first is 1944, and the 94th annual report is the first to carry Perrot and the first not to carry Thunderbird -- which makes the succession more likely and no better documented.]

priorities.description: DO THE ANNUAL REPORTS' CAMPER TABLES REPORT THEIR OWN YEAR OR THE ONE BEFORE? Two clean anchors say the year before: the 1945 report's 'Kanawana for boys 400' is this wiki's figure for the 1944 SEASON, and the 1947 report's 302 is its figure for 1946 (f_5038). A third is OCR-unreadable rather than contradictory. THIS IS NOT BOOKKEEPING. wiki/meta/attendance-series.md is one of this project's spine documents and nothing in it says which convention its 1940s rows were entered under; and the answer decides whether Camp Thunderbird's two summers were 1942-43 or 1943-44, since that camp is known almost entirely from these tables. WHAT TO DO, AND IT IS CHEAP: READ THE FRONT MATTER of the cached annual reports -- cover date, the treasurer's statement, any 'for the year ended' line. The tables were reached by GREP, not by reading the volumes, which is the exact failure p_441 exists to fix, so this is p_441 work as much as verification. Then check the offset against every attendance-series row sourced to an annual report, not just the three tested, and write the convention into the article so the next person greps safely. [DONE 2026-09-06, the same hour it was raised, and it took reading five title pages. EVERY ONE OF THESE REPORTS IS 'FOR THE YEAR ENDING MARCH 31st', so its camping season is the previous summer. The offset is documentary, not inferential. The attendance series' 1940s rows are entered on that basis and are right; a note now says so in the article, because the offset is a trap for the next person who greps a report for a number. And it dated Camp Thunderbird's two summers to 1942 and 1943, ending in the season Camp Perrot began (f_5039). The third, OCR-unreadable anchor resolves the same way: the 1946 report's summer is 1945, for which the series has 324, so its '52h' is a misread 324.]
priorities.notes: Raised 2026-09-06 out of the Camp Thunderbird work. Weight 8: it touches a spine article and a new one, and the evidence needed is already on disk.

priorities.description: WAS THE 1976 ECOLOGY CENTRE AT KANAWANA EVER BUILT? The YMCA of Montreal's 125th-anniversary campaign of 1976 asked for $9.5 million and listed, under Camping & Outdoor Education, 'Development of an Ecology Centre at Kamp Kanawana', 'Development of year-round facilities... at Kamp Kanawana', and 'Development of a northern base camp for tripping and wilderness survival programs' -- promising to make Kanawana 'a year-round camping and outdoor education centre' (f_5044). wiki/traditions/environmental-history.md currently dates that repositioning to a 'virage vert' beginning in 2006, thirty years later, which means EITHER THE 1976 PLAN FAILED OR THE ARTICLE HAS A THIRTY-YEAR HOLE. WHAT TO DO, AND MOST OF IT IS ON DISK: read the YMCA of Montreal annual reports for 1977 through 1985 for the campaign's progress and for any ecology centre, year-round facility or northern base camp at Kanawana; then the Kanawana season reports of the same years, which this repo also holds. THE NORTHERN BASE CAMP IS THE SAME QUESTION FROM ANOTHER SIDE: Les Voyageurs already had a base at Lac Landron by then, so either this is money for that or it is a second site. ALSO WORTH SETTLING: the campaign's actual total raised, and the amount allotted to camping, which is illegible in the 1976 scan and must not be guessed from it. [WORKED 2026-09-06, THE SAME DAY. THE ANSWER IS A NULL ACROSS THIRTEEN DOCUMENTS: the annual reports for 1977-78 through 1986 and Kanawana's own directors' reports for 1976-1979 contain NO ecology centre, NO year-round facility and NO northern base camp. 'Ecolog' occurs in exactly one of the thirteen and it is a staff training course, the 1976 director's report sending Misty McKay to the Vermont Ecology School. The 'Camping and Outdoor Education' that does appear is a branch committee's name (f_5046). THIS SHOWS THE ASSOCIATION NEVER REPORTED BUILDING IT, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS SHOWING IT WAS NOT BUILT -- the searches were keyword searches across volumes that remain unread, and their read_state says so. WHAT THE MONEY DID: the 1980-81 balance sheet still carries 'Due to 1976 Capital Campaign Fund -- 342,526'; the 1984 report has the Foundation preparing a SECOND campaign 'to commence in 1985'; and the 1985 report applies funds 'exclusively to repair the buildings and replace equipment at our branches and Kamp Kanawana'. Repair and replacement, not a centre. WHAT REMAINS: the campaign's total raised, the illegible camping allotment, and reading these volumes rather than searching them. AND AN UNRELATED FINDING FELL OUT OF THE SAME SEARCH -- see f_5047, the camp's 75th anniversary in 1983.]
priorities.notes: Raised 2026-09-06. Weight 8: it bears on a spine article's central date and the sources are cached.

priorities.description: DID THE CAMP COUNT NATIONALITIES IN ANY OTHER YEAR? The annual report for the year ending 31 March 1927 lists the nationalities of Kanawana's 1926 campers -- 'French, American, German, Dutch, Negro, Greek, Italian, Syrian, besides our British boys' -- and frames it as progress in 'inter-racial relationships' (f_5068). IT IS THE EARLIEST STATEMENT THIS PROJECT HAS ABOUT WHO WAS AT THE CAMP BEYOND ITS ANGLO-PROTESTANT CORE and it is a single data point. WHAT TO DO: the annual reports for 1920-1940 are largely cached; read their Kanawana sections for any comparable list, for the word 'nationalities', and for the phrase 'inter-racial'. A run of such counts would turn one sentence into a series and would say something this wiki currently cannot say about the camp's composition between the wars. ALSO WORTH ASKING: whether the Fossils Club scholarships 'chosen through the Branches' (f_5066) were the route by which some of these boys came, which would connect the diversity to the campership arrangement rather than to open enrolment; and whether the camp's own publications -- the Gas Bag, the Green Triangle -- ever name a camper in a way that corroborates the list. HANDLE THE LANGUAGE AS f_5068 DOES: quote the period terms exactly, mark them as the period's, and supply the context rather than paraphrasing them away. [ANSWERED 2026-09-06, the same hour, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. All cached annual reports 1901-1948 searched for 'nationalit' and 'racial'. Every other nationality count in them belongs to the EASTERN BRANCH, the association's immigrant-serving city branch -- eighteen nationalities in 1925, nineteen in 1926, twenty-six in 1928 as 'an international unit', a full country-by-country table of 601 members across 34 countries in 1929, and by 1931 'OUR LITTLE LEAGUE OF NATIONS' in capitals -- and not to any camp. The 1930s and 1940s 'racial' hits are the association's standing formula for its world programme. SO THE 1926 CAMP LIST IS A SINGLE DELIBERATE ACT OF COUNTING that borrows the vocabulary the institution had already built for its immigrant branch, which is a more interesting answer than a series would have been (f_5069). WHAT REMAINS OPEN from the original priority: whether the Fossils Club scholarships were the route by which some of those boys came, and whether the camp's own publications name a camper who corroborates the list.]

priorities.description: AUDIT EVERY SEASON ATTRIBUTION DRAWN FROM A YMCA OF MONTREAL ANNUAL REPORT AFTER 1950. Raised 2026-09-06 out of p_441. f_5039 said 'every one of these annual reports covers the year ending 31 March' on the strength of five title pages (1943-1947), and this project has cited it as a general rule. IT IS NOT ONE. The association's year-end moved from 31 MARCH (through the 99th report, ending 31 March 1950) to 31 DECEMBER (the 100th, ending 31 December 1951, still in force in 1962) to 31 MAY (in force by the mid-1960s and through 1984). See f_5081 for what was verified from title pages and what was not. THE CONSEQUENCE: a report from the December era describes THE SAME SUMMER as its cover year, not the previous one, so any citation applying the 31 March rule to a 1951-1962 report is off by a year. THE WORK: (1) read the title page or auditors' statement of every annual report this project cites for a camping season, and record the year-end in its source record; (2) find every place in the wiki and the KB where a report's season is asserted and check it against that year-end; (3) correct in place and visibly. ONE CHECK ALREADY DONE: oldest-camp-question.md note 23 gives the 1984 and 1985 reports the summers of 1983 and 1984 and cites f_5039 for it -- the seasons are right but the stated reason is wrong, since it follows from a 31 May year-end. NOT YET CHECKED: everything else. ALSO IN SCOPE: the cache filenames are not a reliable guide in the May era -- the file named 1967 is the report for the year ended 31 May 1968 while the file named 1984 is for the year ended 31 May 1984 -- so the audit must read title pages, not filenames. AND TWO OPEN QUESTIONS THE AUDIT SHOULD SETTLE: exactly when the December-to-May change happened (between the year ended 31 December 1962 and the one ended 31 May 1965), and whether the summer of 1950 is described in any report at all -- the 100th report mentions 'an unusually wet summer' without dating it, and April to December 1950 may fall in a twenty-one-month transitional span. [WORKED 2026-09-06, SAME DAY IT WAS RAISED. Wrote scripts/reread/annual_report_year_ends.py, which reads the year-end statement out of every cached annual report; the table is project-docs/annual-report-year-ends.md. IT FOUND A FOURTH REGIME THE FACT DID NOT KNOW ABOUT: a 30 APRIL year-end through the 1925 report, with the 1926 volume the first to say 'For the Year Ending March 31st'. April, March and May years all contain the PREVIOUS summer, so THE ONLY WINDOW THAT INVERTS IS 1951 TO ABOUT 1962. That is a much smaller audit than this priority assumed. FOUR MISDATINGS FOUND AND CORRECTED IN PLACE: f_5047 and the notes in oldest-camp-question.md and centennial-1994.md dated the 1984-85 reports to March (right seasons, wrong reason -- 31 May); f_5080 and the directors-index note I wrote earlier the same day dated the 1956 and 1959 reports to March when both are 31 December, which DID move the chairmen by a year and is now fixed. STILL OPEN: 33 volumes come back UNREAD from the scanner because the OCR defeats the regex, and their title pages need an eye -- among them 1946, 1947, 1956, 1957, 1959, 1960, 1961, 1962, 1964, 1965, 1966-67, 1967 and every 1970s span file. THE 1959 AND 1962 YEAR-ENDS ARE ALREADY CONFIRMED BY HAND (both 31 December) even though the scanner misses them. Also still open: exactly when December became May, and whether the summer of 1950 is described anywhere.] [ADVANCED 2026-09-06, SECOND PASS. BOTH CHANGEOVERS ARE NOW DATED TO A VOLUME, from the report ordinals, which run consecutively across both, so NO VOLUME IS MISSING: 97th (31 March 1948) through 100th (31 December 1951) is three volumes for three years, so THE 100TH SPANS TWENTY-ONE MONTHS, 1 April 1950 to 31 December 1951; 109th-111th are the December years 1960-1962 and the 112th is the year ended 31 May 1964, so THE 112TH SPANS SEVENTEEN MONTHS and contains one summer, 1963. AND THE 1950 QUESTION IS ANSWERED NEGATIVELY: the summer of 1950 sits inside the 100th report's span and the report describes one summer, 'an unusually wet summer' with attendance 'above the previous year', which reads as 1951 against 1950. THE 1950 SEASON IS NOT DESCRIBED ANYWHERE IN THIS SERIES; the hole in the attendance table is real and no further reading of these reports will fill it. That is now stated in meta/attendance-series.md so nobody hunts for it again. ONE LOOSE END KEPT: the 100th report's balance sheet carries a 1950 comparative and a line 'Balance December 31, 1950', so accounts were struck at that date though no report covers a year ending then -- consistent either with an interim comparative inside a 21-month report or with an unissued nine-month stub. Not resolvable from this volume (f_5090). STILL OPEN: the 33 volumes the scanner cannot read, and the wiki-wide sweep of season attributions outside the articles already checked. [MOSTLY CLOSED 2026-09-06 IN THE SCANNER, NOT BY EYE (f_5130). This priority said 33 volumes needed a human eye on the title page; the real number in the output was 116, and nearly all of it was the tool. Nineteen were French editions against an English-only regex; thirteen were camp-level reports, a different document class where the question does not arise, now excluded; several state the year-end only past the 20,000-character window, now 120,000; several were defeated by one OCR character, so the day is no longer matched at all; and the 1960s volumes state only a span with the opening year OCR'd to nonsense, which now has its own pattern. 63 of 179 became 140 of 166 association volumes. A REGRESSION WAS CAUGHT AND FIXED IN PASSING: widening the window flipped the 1989 report to May 1988, because the function returned the first PATTERN matching anywhere instead of the match nearest the document's start. Every reading was diffed against the previous run and none that had a value changed. REMAINING: 26 volumes, mostly pre-1900 and so before Kanawana existed; the ones that matter are 1959, 1960, 1961 and 1966-67, which sit in the December-to-May transition and are worth an eye.] [CLOSED 2026-09-06 (f_5131). The four volumes that actually mattered -- the ones either side of the December-to-May change -- are read. 1959 and 1960 now read by the scanner after de-hyphenation ('year ending Dec-\nember'), both December year-ends. 1961 read BY EYE and deliberately left UNREAD in the tool: its text is 'Dec-\nember 4lst, I96I1', and a pattern loose enough to take 'I96I1' for 1961 would misread a year somewhere else. 1966-67 states no year-end at all, so its reading is an INFERENCE from the ordinal series, flagged as one, resting on no skipped or doubled report between the 112th and the 115th. 142 of 166 association volumes now read. The 24 remaining are pre-1900 or later administrative volumes and none of them bears on a Kanawana season.]

priorities.description: 635 SOURCE RECORDS ARE MARKED 'EXTRACTED' BY INFERENCE RATHER THAN BY READING, AND AT LEAST TWO OF THEM WERE HIDING SUBSTANTIVE MATERIAL. Of 1,668 source records, 639 carry a derived read_state basis: 635 read 'extracted' with basis 'derived:cited-by-fact' and 4 read 'unknown' with 'derived:named-in-article-only'. Thirty-eight per cent of the corpus. WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is not a claim that 635 documents are unread. Many were certainly read and extracted properly and only the basis string is uninformative. WHAT IT IS: the basis cannot distinguish a document somebody read from a document one fact happens to cite, so the corpus has no way to tell those two apart, and 'extracted' on such a record is not evidence of anything. HOW IT WAS FOUND. On 2026-09-06 the annual reports for 1966-67 and 1967 were skipped as done because their Internet Archive records read 'extracted'. Six facts cited one and two cited the other; neither volume had been read through. Reading them produced f_5095, f_5096 and f_5097, INCLUDING THE 1967 REPORT'S 'CO-ED CAMPING' SECTION -- the public announcement of coeducation with an age band of 9-11 and A. Ross Seaman's stated reason in his own words, which is among the most consequential documents this project has found for history/coeducation-gender.md. It sat behind a record that said the volume was finished. THE WORK. (1) Count how many of the 635 have a substantial number of facts genuinely drawn from them versus one or two incidental citations -- a record cited by fifteen facts is likely a real extraction, one cited by a single bibliographic fact almost certainly is not. (2) Rank by expected yield and re-read from the bottom. (3) Rewrite each basis honestly as it is checked. (4) DO NOT run scripts/verify/seed_read_state.py to fix this in bulk -- that script is what produced these strings and it clobbers hand-written provenance across 1,563 records (p_411). RELATED: the duplicate detector was relaxed the same day (MIN_OVERLAP 0.75 instead of strict containment) because it could not see a pair whose filename carried a token the title lacked; candidate pairs went 207 to 283 and read_state disagreements 54 to 117. Many of those disagreements will be this same problem seen from the other side. See f_5098. [NARROWED THE SAME DAY IT WAS RAISED, AND THE FIRST FRAMING WAS TOO ALARMING. Counting citing facts and cache paths: OF THE 639 DERIVED-BASIS RECORDS, EXACTLY ONE HAS A CACHE FILE ON DISK. The other 638 are records for documents this project holds no text of, so their 'extracted' cannot be tested by re-reading and there is nothing to re-read. Citing-fact distribution: 298 records cited by one fact, 124 by two, 107 by 3-5, 88 by 6-15, 18 by 16+, 4 by none. THE ACTIONABLE POPULATION IS THEREFORE THE DUPLICATE CASE SPECIFICALLY -- a cached file marked unread or skimmed under one record, shadowed by a pathless record marked 'extracted' by citation inference -- AND THAT LIST IS 79 PAIRS. Some are false positives where a collection-level record (src_ia_ymca_reports) matches many individual volumes. GENUINE-LOOKING AND HIGH VALUE: 1969-camp-perrot-family-centre.txt (unread), which bears directly on the family recreation centre finding of the same morning; 1959-a-fresh-look-at-camp-perrot.txt (unread); 1919-08-brief-autobiographical-sketch-of-association-car... (unread); historical-sketch-ymca-of-montreal-1901.txt (unread). THE WORK IS NOW: walk the 79, skip the collection-level false positives, read the rest, and rewrite each basis honestly. Steps (1) and (2) of the original description are done and superseded by this list. [FIRST DOCUMENT OFF THE 79-PAIR LIST, 2026-09-06, AND IT PAID. '1969-camp-perrot-family-centre.txt' was marked UNREAD under src_cache_1969_camp_perrot_family_centre while the pathless src_camp_perrot_1969_family_centre read 'extracted' by citation inference. Read end to end. IT DESCRIBES CAMP PERROT'S WHOLE SECOND LIFE: 48 acres in 1968, two swimming pools, a lodge seating 200, and 'Hospital - program area', which is the John W. Ross Memorial Hospital still standing twenty years on; a day camp of 1,353 campers at $19.00 a child across three branch districts, a Summer Centre of 100 families at $15.00, and a tent and trailer area taking 600 families at $2.50 to $3.50; and a plan for a 'day camp centre for French and English program'. IT ALSO SUPPLIES THE ONLY STATED REASON FOR THE CLOSURE THIS PROJECT HAS -- 'financial difficulties forced the camp to close' -- against which open question 6 had only the 1958 committee's list of complaints. AND ITS HISTORY IS WRONG: by its own arithmetic the resident camp closed in 1952 with six dormant years, while the annual reports for 1953, 1954, 1955 and 1957 all describe it running, with attendance figures. Recorded as a demonstrably weak retrospective, which is a reason to weight contemporaneous reports over retrospectives throughout the closure question rather than a reason to be confused (f_5099). ALSO CHECKED: '1959-a-fresh-look-at-camp-perrot.txt', also marked unread, IS already quoted in camp-perrot.md -- so that pair is a bookkeeping duplicate and not a missed read. Both source records annotated. 77 pairs left. [MORE OFF THE LIST, 2026-09-06. Checked and cleared as bookkeeping duplicates rather than missed reads: '1959-a-fresh-look-at-camp-perrot.txt' (already quoted in camp-perrot.md), 'historical-sketch-ymca-of-montreal-1901.txt' (25 facts, 10 articles) and '1919-08-brief-autobiographical-sketch-of-association-career.txt' (Patton's memoir, quoted in founding-1894 and t-duncan-patton). THE RANKED LIST IS NOW A FILE: kb/reread/derived_duplicates.md, 78 rows sorted by how many facts cite the shadow record. Forty rows have a shadow cited by exactly one fact -- that is the risk band, and it is where the 1969 Camp Perrot proposal sat. AND THE NEWS RELEASES ARE A PILE OF THEIR OWN: 170-odd cached Montreal YMCA releases from 1962 to 1980, most with no Kanawana mention at all, a dozen with hits. TWO READ TODAY AND BOTH PAID. The 13 May 1969 release gives a FRENCH IMMERSION SECTION at the residential camp -- a converted farm building, one French-speaking counsellor to five boys, a language co-ordinator, part of each day for study -- which appears nowhere in this wiki; plus HORSES ARRIVING IN 1968 with the girls, the CO-ED CAPACITY DOUBLED FOR 1969 in response to parents (which explains the competing 1969 date without reopening 1968), skin diving and riflery, and 'Canada's longest established summer camp' as association publicity (f_5100). The 29 January 1970 bulletin gives a WEST ISLAND BRANCH FAMILY SKI DAY running Saturdays at Kanawana AND ALREADY AT CAPACITY -- groomed downhill runs, instruction, a supervised nursery, free soup -- THREE YEARS BEFORE the date winter-programming.md gives for the start of winter family programming. That open question is qualified rather than reopened: the 1972-73 report describes infrastructure this bulletin does not (f_5101). STILL WORTH READING among the releases with Kanawana hits: 1963-04-22, 1964-09-25, 1964-10-14, 1967-07-28, 1969-04-24, 1969-11-28, 1970-08-05, p0145-1970-05-28, 1971-01, 1973-10-26. [THREE MORE RELEASES, 2026-09-06. 28 July 1967: the fur trade trip has SEVEN boys where centennial-1967.md has six from McMorris -- two association documents agreeing against a thesis, flagged and not resolved -- plus the truck-to-Deep-River logistics, the CCA Centennial Project framing, and a planned reception of 200 campers with a chuckwagon lunch and a Parliament Buildings tour (f_5102). 24 April 1969: the French section is named 'LIVING-IN-FRENCH', immersion style, boys 12-16, with pre-registration 15% ahead and 'a flood of applications for the Girl's Section' (f_5103). 28 November 1969, French column: the LONG HOUSE OPENED FOR THE WINTER of 1969-70 under a policy of aid to disadvantaged families; 170 francophone people from PETITE-BOURGOGNE spent two weeks at Otoreke in July 1969, a district absent from this whole project; and the three camping sites became a SPECIAL BRANCH under A. Ross Seaman, dating the Camping Branch to November 1969 or earlier and confirming Perrot active at the end of 1969. That release also calls Seaman a past PRESIDENT of the Quebec Camping Association where this project has him as its SECRETARY -- recorded as a claim, not adopted (f_5104). REMAINING RELEASES WITH KANAWANA HITS, UNREAD: 1963-04-22, 1964-09-25, 1964-10-14, 1970-08-05, p0145-1970-05-28, 1971-01, 1973-10-26. [THE NEWS RELEASES WITH KANAWANA HITS ARE NOW ALL READ, 2026-09-06. The last five: the 1964 letterhead prints Kanawana as a BRANCH two years before the annual reports do (both 1964 releases otherwise NULL for camp content, recorded as such); 28 May 1970 has almost 500 already enrolled plus 24 Voyageurs, against the 1970 director's report saying registration 'started slowly'; 5 August 1970 brings 44 British students aged 16-19 and two masters from the W.H. Rhodes Canada Education Trust for the first two and a half days of an 11-16 August visit, echoing the 133 'Old Country' boys of 1939; and the January 1971 year-in-review corroborates the West Island family ski programme (f_5106). WHAT REMAINS IN THE RELEASE PILE: about 155 files with ZERO Kanawana mentions, which are not worth reading for this project and should be marked as swept rather than read. THAT SWEEP IS THE NEXT CHEAP WIN -- a grep-and-annotate pass that turns 155 'skimmed' records into honest 'null for Kanawana' ones, so nobody works through them one at a time. [THE NEWS RELEASE PILE IS NOW SWEPT, 2026-09-06. Wrote scripts/reread/sweep_news_releases.py, which classifies all 172 cached releases against a pattern covering Kanawana and its OCR variants, Otoreke, Perrot, Voyageurs, Becsies, Weredale, Thunderbird, Christieville and the phrases day camp / summer camp / camping. RESULT: 13 name Kanawana, 16 name another camp but not Kanawana, 143 MATCH NOTHING. The 143 are now read_state 'swept' with a basis saying exactly what was matched and that THE DOCUMENT WAS NOT READ -- a fact about the pattern, not about the release. Skimmed records across the whole corpus fell from 657 to 520. ALSO FIXED A STALE CHECKER: verify_harness.py's VALID_READ_STATES was {extracted, skimmed, unopened, unavailable, unknown} and had been printing 223 records as INVALID because the corpus has used 'partial', 'read', 'unread', 'snippet' and 'unverified_backfill' for months. The set now names all eleven values in use with a one-line gloss each. THE 16 CAMP-BUT-NOT-KANAWANA FILES WERE READ and two paid: 5 December 1966 is headed 'ILE PERROT DAY CAMP TO HOUSE EXPO VISITORS' and gives the Expo build a start date of 8 November 1966, a target of 120,000 VISITORS, 90 trailer sites, 100 camp sites and an outdoor pool, with Charles Morrison turning the sod; and a 2 September 1969 staffing release has MURRAY HORN 'in charge of the YMCA's day camp complex on Ile Perrot'. Neither name appears anywhere else in this project (f_5107). An undated 1970 Voyageurs recruiting release gives the ENTRY BAR -- sound health and a 150-yard swim, crews of five under 'a skilled outdoorsman, usually a mature university student', several days at base camp first -- and dates the programme to '13 years ago', i.e. 1957, against this project's 1959. THE 1959 DATE STANDS; the release is loose arithmetic and the camp's own report is the better witness (f_5108). [WORKED 2026-09-06 (f_5132). The list was polluted by name collisions from duplicate_sources.py's loosened 0.75 overlap threshold: a February 1970 record shadowing September 1970 releases, 1964 and 1965 releases shadowed by a 1970 record. The generator was an UNVERSIONED SNIPPET IN A PIPELINE LOG ENTRY and is now scripts/reread/derived_duplicates.py, which classifies each pair by the dates in its two names -- 12 candidates, 4 provable collisions, 45 undecidable from names. (It reports 61 pairs where the snippet reported 78; the snippet's criteria are unrecoverable, so no equivalence is claimed.) VERIFICATION IS ONE-DIRECTIONAL: a phrase quoted in a citing fact and found in the cached file proves the pair; not finding it proves nothing, because the OCR mangles words and a multi-source fact may be quoting its other source. The probe confirmed 4 of 20 and three records were updated on that evidence; the fourth was already 'partial', so the old list was stale. Corpus unread 52 -> 49. The pairs themselves remain p_442's operator decision.]
priorities.notes: Raised 2026-09-06 out of p_441. Larger in scope than p_441 itself.

priorities.description: SPIN OUT THE SECTIONS THAT HAVE OUTGROWN THEIR ARTICLES. OPERATOR DIRECTION, 2026-09-06: 'I want a very robust wiki, with articles that link to new articles when topics get too complicated to fit in an original article, because there are too many points of contact or there's a deep depth of information about a specific reference point in the original article that needs its own article to explain.' The example given: a significant director is mentioned in the general historical overview, but their whole career and life live in their own article. THAT PATTERN ALREADY WORKS FOR DIRECTORS and for nothing else. I have been accreting into whatever article was nearest, and the numbers show it: MEDIAN ARTICLE 1,892 WORDS, LARGEST 36,649. THE AUDIT: scripts/wiki/spinout_audit.py, output committed as project-docs/spinout-audit.md. 63 sections across 36 of the 108 articles are over 900 words; 29 sections across 21 articles are over 1,500. IT MEASURES SECTION WORD COUNTS, WHICH IS A PROXY -- a long section that is one argument belongs where it is, and a short section about a person with a career elsewhere may still want its own article and will not appear in the list. THE WORST CASE, AND IT IS ALSO IN THE WRONG FOLDER: connections/institutional-lineage/canadian-camping-movement.md is 36,649 words, of which 25,891 -- SEVENTY-ONE PER CENT -- are one section, 'Kanawana's Place in the Movement'. Under the hub-and-spoke rule Kanawana's own story belongs in CORE folders, not inside a spoke article about another institution's history. That section holds at least four distinct articles: (1) the oldest-camp argument, across three subsections, WHICH IS NOT A NEW ARTICLE AT ALL -- history/oldest-camp-question.md already exists and this is its material in the wrong file; (2) HAY FINLAY, eighty lines as 'the named individual on both sides', a person article by the director rule; (3) THE DECLINE OF THE CAMPING ASSOCIATIONS, across 'The money stops: why the national record thins after 1985', 'The association after the money stopped' and 'Will we survive?'; (4) THE ANNUAIRE, the province's own camp directory, which CLAUDE.md's own thresholds already name as spawnable ('publication or media'). ALSO OVERDUE, both crossed the five-fact line on 2026-09-06 and were written into programs-activities.md instead: THE FRENCH-LANGUAGE PROGRAMME 1967-1972 (6 facts: f_5100, f_5103, f_5111, f_5113, f_5114, f_5115) and VALUES FOR LIVING / PLANNED GROUP DEVELOPMENT 1956-1961 (6 facts: f_5084, f_5086, f_5087, f_5088). Close but not over: the family ski programme (4) and the Otoreke Project (2, and arguably Otoreke's story rather than Kanawana's). THE RULE TO WRITE INTO CLAUDE.md SO THIS STOPS BEING A JUDGEMENT CALL EACH TIME: a reference point spins out when it has its own arc rather than a role in this article's arc, when three or more articles would want to link to it, or when its section passes roughly a thousand words. The parent keeps a paragraph and a link and must still read whole. NOT STARTED. Moving 26,000 words out of an E1-reviewed article is a larger editorial act than spawning a stub, and the operator has been given two starting points -- the big article, or the two cheap programme stubs -- and has not yet chosen. DO NOT BEGIN THE RESTRUCTURING ON A SCHEDULED CHECK-IN; a trigger firing is not the operator answering. [STARTED 2026-09-06 ON OPERATOR INSTRUCTION 'start with the big article'. FIRST SPINOUT DONE: connections/institutional-lineage/association-founding-dates.md, 1,855 words, draft. WHAT WAS MOVED: nine paragraphs, 1,298 words, on the CONTESTED FOUNDING DATES of the Canadian Camping Association (1936 in its own 1980s literature, c.1947 from President Douglas McEwen in 1967, 1938 from Adele Ebbs who kept the founding circle's minutes and was TALKED OUT OF IT IN PRINT) and of the Quebec association (1937 English Section, 1958 French section, JANUARY 1961 amalgamation which it actually commemorated, and 1938 per Ken Willis, who had a fiftieth anniversary being planned around it for 1988). Plus the finding that the 'founding six' Ebbs named were the ONTARIO association's circle, not the national one, which removes a recurring source of confusion from c_029. THE PARAGRAPHS WERE NOT CONTIGUOUS -- they were interleaved with funding-appeal material at lines 522-577, which is itself evidence of how the parent grew. CITATIONS: markers ^8bh, ^8bj and ^8bl renumbered to ^1, ^2, ^3 in the new article and their entries written out in full; all three are STILL CITED in the parent, so nothing was orphaned by the cut. Verified by diffing orphan lists before and after -- the five entries the parent lists but never cites (8ag, 8ba, 8g, 8r, 8u) ARE PRE-EXISTING and were not caused by this edit. THE PARENT keeps a five-sentence summary and a link. Cross-linked both ways, and from ymca-quebec-history.md so it is reachable from the hub. Entered as DRAFT rather than E1-reviewed: the material was E1-reviewed inside the parent but the new article's structure, overview and open questions are new and unverified as a whole. PARENT IS NOW 35,476 WORDS, DOWN FROM 36,649. That is the measure of how much is left: this cut was 3% of it. STILL IN THERE: the 11,117-word 'A textbook says Kanawana was first' subsection, which on inspection is FOUR OR FIVE ARTICLES under one heading -- the Quebec association's institutional history, the movement's national statistics, bilingualism and the French-Canadian side, the 1983 congress and promotion, and the Quebec association's decline; the national office and Fitness Canada funding arc; Hay Finlay; and the Annuaire, which at 320 words is a paragraph and should fold into a Quebec association article rather than becoming its own, correcting what I proposed earlier. [SECOND CUT, 2026-09-06, AND IT WAS NOT A SPINOUT. The two oldest-camp subsections in canadian-camping-movement.md (1,463 words) turned out to be A DUPLICATE of the argument in history/oldest-camp-question.md, not material in the wrong file. I had planned to move them; checking the destination first showed it already had everything, in better form, with fact citations -- and the copy in the movement article was the WEAKER one, floating as open speculation ('the 1891 Lake of the Woods Institute MAY have been a men's conference-encampment') a question the other article settles from a source ('it wasn't until 1911 that the first boys' camp was organized at Camp Stephens'). DELETED, not merged, after a paragraph-by-paragraph comparison. Parent keeps a summary, a link and a note saying what happened; oldest-camp-question.md is now marked in its own text as the canonical home. Sources 14-18, orphaned by the cut, removed and 19-22 renumbered to 14-17 -- all four source ids are cited in the destination, so nothing left the corpus; the header count was corrected from 22 to 17 after verify_harness caught it. Parent 35,476 -> 34,023. THE FINDING IS BIGGER THAN THE CUT (f_5118): NOTHING IN THIS PROJECT DETECTS AN ARGUMENT MADE IN TWO ARTICLES. duplicate_sources.py finds documents catalogued twice; there is no equivalent for prose, copies drift, and a reader has no way to tell which is current. HOW MANY OTHER PAIRS EXIST HAS NOT BEEN MEASURED, and measuring it should come before more spinouts -- cutting an article into pieces is the wrong move if the piece already exists elsewhere. [MEASURED FIRST, THEN CUT, 2026-09-06. scripts/wiki/prose_dupes.py written and run over all 112 articles (f_5119): 40 pairs share 25+ words and ALMOST ALL OF IT IS SHARED QUOTATION of a common primary source, which is the citation graph working. Largest overlap 160 words against f_5118's 1,463. All three pairs involving the parent are shared quotation, SO THE REMAINING BLOCKS ARE SPINOUTS AND NOT DELETIONS. THIRD CUT, AND THE SECOND REAL SPINOUT: connections/institutional-lineage/quebec-camping-association.md, 6,294 words, draft. 4,434 words moved out of the 'A textbook says Kanawana was first' subsection -- the Quebec Camping Association's founding by F. M. Van Wagner in 1937, its two incorporations (Federal Charter 1949, Quebec law 23 January 1961), Alta R. Kahn and the officers, the accreditation regime and Van Wagner's 1955 Manual of Standards, the ACQ's own director-training curriculum of February 1976, the arrival of the Quebec government as a second regulator in 1976-77, and the disappearance of the English Section from the national printed lists between 1978 and 1982. THE PARAGRAPHS WERE INTERLEAVED with national material -- statistics, bilingualism, the 1983 Congress, the certification debate -- which all stays in the parent; the move set was 34 non-contiguous paragraphs. Lettered markers remapped to ^1-^21 and the entries written out in full; seven entries (8w, 8z, 8ad, 8ai, 8aj, 8al, 8am) were orphaned by the cut and removed, and the five PRE-EXISTING orphans (8g, 8r, 8u, 8ag, 8ba) were restored after a first pass wrongly dropped them -- 8ag is cited inside another source note, not in the body, so a body-only citation test is wrong. Four back-references that broke on the move were rewritten. Cross-linked from the parent, association-founding-dates, derek-walsh and quebec-camp-landscape. PARENT 34,023 -> 29,524. CAUGHT ON THE WAY (f_5120): the parent cited [src_kk_preparation_guide_2025], an id that has never existed -- the record is src_kk_prep_guide_2025. It survived in an E1-REVIEWED article because verify_harness checks [src_] existence on DRAFT articles only, and only surfaced when the note was carried into a new draft. Fixed in both files. STILL IN THE PARENT: the national statistics run, bilingualism and Belanger, the 1983 Congress and National Camping Day, the director-certification debate, the staff-manual specification and the Wilkinson textbook, Hay Finlay (4,056 words), and the Fitness Canada funding arc.] [FOURTH CUT, 2026-09-06: people/hay-finlay.md, 1,190 words, draft -- THE OPERATOR'S OWN EXAMPLE OF THE PATTERN, a person named in the overview whose career gets its own article. priorities.description: WHY WAS THE YMCA'S EASTERN DISTRICT USING CAMP LEWIS IN 1921? Raised out of a mistake worth recording. The annual report for the year ending 30 April 1922, under EASTERN DISTRICT, lists 'many agencies have been used for our Boys' Work, including Churches, the Macdonald Playground, Fletcher's Field, tennis courts, Maisonneuve Protestant School, and CAMP LEWIS.' I nearly filed this as an unknown third YMCA camp. THE GREP SAYS OTHERWISE and the grep was run: Camp Lewis is already in this project in nine places -- the Boys' Home of Montreal's camp, sponsored in 1918 as 'Camp Boy' and renamed in 1919 for Major John Lewis, killed in the First World War; the predecessor of CAMP WEREDALE (1934); taking five hundred boys a year under Mr. Wylie by 1949. See f_5174 and connections/related-camps/camp-weredale.md. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN: the report does not say what the use was -- whether the YMCA sent Eastern District boys there, ran programme in it, shared staff, or merely counted a partner agency. The Eastern District paragraph around it is about the foreign-speaking districts, Italian and Syrian Boy Scout work, employed boys of foreign parentage and co-operation with the Juvenile Court, which suggests boys placed rather than programme run, but the report does not say so. WHERE TO LOOK: the other 1920s annual reports for 'Camp Lewis' (only the 1921-1922 volume carries it in this cache); the Weredale House fonds at Library and Archives Canada, whose Camp Lewis/Weredale records run 1919-1966; Concordia P0145 for Eastern District boys' work. || WORKED 2026-09-06, PARTLY ANSWERED (f_5202). WHAT WAS RUN: greps for 'Camp Lewis' across the cached YMCA Year Books (nil), the 1920s annual reports (only the 1921-1922 volume), the Canadian Camping run and the news releases. WHAT THEY GIVE: Canadian Camping, June 1949 -- 'Camp Lewis, under the direction of Mr. Wylie, offers good camping to five hundred boys for two weeks or longer each year' -- and a 1964 Montreal YMCA news release listing Camp Lewis among twenty-odd participating agencies in a Rotary inter-agency youth project, one line above the Negro Community Centre, with Ross Seaman of the Metropolitan Office on staff. SO THE 1921 'USE' READS AS INTER-AGENCY COOPERATION, not a YMCA camp -- Camp Lewis was a substantial operation with its own director. STILL OPEN, and the reason this stays pending: WHAT KIND of use (boys sent, programme run, staff shared) and for how long. The held sources cannot answer it. LAC's Weredale House fonds, Camp Lewis/Weredale records 1919-1966, is the named target -- and LAC refuses this environment at the gateway (see p_428), so this is an ACCESS FAILURE WITH A NAMED TARGET rather than an unsearched question. || CHARACTERISED 2026-09-06 (f_5213): LAC's Collection Search is behind a **CLOUDFLARE JAVASCRIPT CHALLENGE** -- 403 with `cf-mitigated: challenge` and a 'Just a moment...' body -- not a policy refusal. Same mechanism as HathiTrust's babel and the same class as Concordia's AtoM challenge. NOBODY IS REFUSING THIS PROJECT; this environment cannot solve a JS challenge because its browser dies at the proxy tunnel. A PERSON WITH AN ORDINARY BROWSER REACHES IT IN ONE CLICK, and no letter or permission is needed. The federal open-data CKAN API does answer (200) but publishes only LAC's ADMINISTRATIVE datasets -- 71 of them, none collection-level -- so it is not a substitute.

WHAT WAS CAMP MACAULAY, AND WAS IT NAMED FOR THE SUN LIFE MACAULAYS? The YMCA of Montreal annual report for the year ending 31 March 1933 says 'the boys' section at CAMP MACAULAY was under the charge of C. J. McGerrigle, who chose his staff of councillors from members of this branch' -- the branch being the one whose section the passage sits in. GREPPED: 'Camp Macaulay' appears nowhere else in wiki/ or kb/facts.json. That makes it a fourth or fifth Montreal YMCA camp operation for the early 1930s alongside Kanawana, Otoreke and the day camps, and this project has nothing on it. THE HOOK IS THE NAME. FIND GORD LOGAN'S 'CANOE TRIPPING WITH GIRLS' IN OUTDOORS CANADA, SPRING 1979. Ka-News for December 1978 reports that "Gord has left CFCF to take up writing fulltime - a story of his on 'Canoe Tripping with Girls' will be published next spring in 'Outdoors Canada' magazine", with photographs possibly by Steve Reizes and Marie Therien; the May 1979 issue names him -- "Gord Logan buzzed into our office last month to reminisce about his experiences leading a senior girls trip" -- and says he was returning to camp that summer (f_5225). So the author is a Kanawana senior-girls trip leader and ex-CFCF employee writing from his own camp experience, in a national outdoor magazine, in the years this project's coeducation article is thinnest. GREPPED: 'Outdoors Canada' occurs nowhere else in wiki/ or kb/facts.json. WHETHER THE PIECE NAMES KANAWANA IS UNKNOWN AND IS NOT ASSUMED. WHERE TO LOOK: Outdoors Canada was published in Toronto; try Library and Archives Canada's serials holdings, the Internet Archive and Open Library search-inside on the exact phrase 'Canoe Tripping with Girls' and on 'Gord Logan', Google Books, the Toronto Public Library and Toronto Reference Library periodical holdings, WorldCat for library runs of the magazine, and any Canadian Camping notice of the article (the camping press covered its own people's publications). ALSO SEARCH FOR GORD LOGAN HIMSELF -- CFCF staff lists, later bylines, the CCA convention in Minnesota he attended with Derek Walsh in March 1979. || WORKED THE SAME DAY, f_5228. THE TITLE IN THE NEWSLETTER IS PROBABLY WRONG BY ONE LETTER: the target is OUTDOOR CANADA (Toronto, published since 1972, six issues a year, fishing/hunting/canoeing/camping), not 'Outdoors Canada', which in the Open Library corpus resolves to a Reader's Digest Association (Canada) BOOK of 1977 (item outdoorscanada00read). Search the magazine's 1979 volume, not the book. The exact phrase 'Canoe Tripping with Girls' returns zero in the Open Library corpus, which is uninformative -- that corpus is books. THE AUTHOR IS CORROBORATED ONCE: Howard Galganov's Bastards has "Gord Logan of CIQC AM 600", CIQC being CFCF 600 renamed in 1991, which matches Ka-News's "Gord has left CFCF". BEWARE A NAME COLLISION: most corpus hits on Gord Logan are the boy witness in the Steven Truscott case. broadcasting-history.ca's CFCF page was fetched and does not contain the name Logan. UNTRIED: Outdoor Canada's own archive and back-issue index, Library and Archives Canada and Toronto Public Library serial holdings, WorldCat for library runs, eBay and used-magazine sellers for 1979 issues, and the Canadian Camping notices, which covered members' publications.

ASK FOR KANAWANA'S 1986 ACQ ACCREDITATION VISITATION REPORT BY NAME. The Association des Camps du Quebec's own column for the summer of 1986 states the rule: accredited camps were visited every two years by a team of four consultants, AND a camp that had a major change in the year -- 'le changement de directeur, par exemple' -- was visited regardless of where it stood in the cycle (f_5236). Kanawana's directorship passed from Peter Goddard to Jay Netherwood inside the YMCA's FY1986. So on the association's own stated rule a 1986 visitation of Kanawana happened and a report was written. WHERE TO ASK: the ACQ itself, which still exists (campsquebec.com) and whose earlier records may be with it or deposited; Concordia's YMCA of Montreal fonds P0145, where the camp's own copy of an accreditation report would sit with camp committee papers rather than under the association's name; and the camp itself. WHAT IT WOULD GIVE: an outside inspector's description of the site, the programme and the staffing in a single year of the 1980s, which is a kind of document this project holds none of. THE SAME RULE MEANS OTHER YEARS ARE PREDICTABLE TOO: any year Kanawana changed director should have produced one. Raised 2026-09-06 out of the eleventh spinout.

DID KANAWANA WRITE ITS OWN HISTORY IN 1985 OR 1986, BECAUSE IT WAS ASKED TO TWICE? The Canadian Camping Association mailed every member camp in Canada a kit of camp-history activities for International Youth Year in MAY 1985, and for its fiftieth anniversary invited every camp to stage its own history in the summer of 1986 under the title 'An Adventure into the Past' (f_5237, now written up at connections/institutional-lineage/movement-archive-turn.md). KANAWANA WAS A MEMBER CAMP IN BOTH YEARS. If it answered either call, a camp-written history of Kanawana exists from the middle 1980s -- the decade between-centennials.md is thinnest on, and a period for which this project holds directors' reports and almost nothing else the camp wrote about itself. WHERE TO ASK: Concordia's YMCA of Montreal fonds P0145, where a 1985 or 1986 camp history would sit with the camp committee papers rather than under any obvious heading; the camp itself; the Kanawana alumni network, since a staged camp history is the kind of thing photographed; and the Lookout alumni newsletter, whose 1993 issue this project holds and whose earlier numbers it does not. ALSO WORTH ASKING: whether the association's own copy survives in the CCA fonds at Trent, since the 1986 invitation asked camps to report back. NOTE THE PRECEDENT ALREADY IN HAND: the 'Kamp Kanawana History' read at a staff training course in 1951 shows the camp did produce documents of exactly this kind when prompted. Raised 2026-09-07 out of the twelfth spinout.

WATCH THE 2013 CUTV FILM OF KANAWANA, AND FIND THE SUMMIT IT COVERS. THE FILE IS FREELY DOWNLOADABLE -- .mp4 at 11 MB and .mp3 at 1.5 MB -- SO THIS NEEDS NO PERMISSION, ONLY THE ABILITY TO WATCH OR LISTEN, WHICH THIS ENVIRONMENT DOES NOT HAVE. What it would give is the interview at the centre of the piece, which neither caption track transcribes and which is where the summit's own organisers speak; the names of the people on screen, none of which the machine captions render reliably; and roughly two minutes of moving footage of the site in the 2010s, which this project holds nothing else of. SECOND HALF, AND IT IS SEPARABLE: the summit is described on film as being IN ITS SECOND YEAR, so a first edition exists and nothing in this project records either. Search the YMCA of Montreal's and YMCAs du Quebec's own press releases and annual reports for 2011-2015, the ymcaquebec.org site and its Wayback captures, Concordia's student press (The Link and The Concordian, both partly online), and CUTV's own channel for related items. THE CUTV CHANNEL IS ITSELF WORTH SWEEPING: this item was found only because it surfaced in an Internet Archive search on 'kanawana', and a station that sent a crew to the camp once may have gone back. Raised 2026-09-07.

An untitled 1928 clipping reports 'the arrival on the scene of a "movie" man, with cameras and several hundred feet of film' at the Montreal YWCA's Laurentian camp, with the girls performing fancy dives, tennis and basketball for the camera (f_5241). SEVERAL HUNDRED FEET OF 1928 FILM OF A LAURENTIAN GIRLS' CAMP THEREFORE EXISTED. The clipping does not say who shot it, for whom, or what became of it. WHERE TO LOOK: the YWCA of Montreal's own records (its fonds, and whatever the YWCA holds itself); Library and Archives Canada's moving image collection; the Cinematheque quebecoise; the McCord Museum; and the commercial newsreel and industrial-film producers working in Montreal in 1928, since 'a movie man' with several hundred feet of stock is a professional, not a camper with a Brownie. READ THE FORTY-SEVEN UNREAD MONTREAL YMCA SERIALS ON THE INTERNET ARCHIVE. The fonds there holds 942 items; this project has read or cited 458 and not 484, and 47 of the unread are TEXTS -- whole serial runs nobody here has touched (f_5243). The list is cached at sources/cache/ymca-montreal-fonds/2026-09-07-ia-fonds-enumeration-what-is-unread.txt. ORDER OF ATTACK, by likely camp content. (1) THE NEWS BULLETIN, about twenty issues 1931-1949: this is the association's own staff and member bulletin across the years the camp record is thinnest, and a sample issue already produced a find (f_5244, the 1939 World Service table listing Camp Kanawana and Camp Otoreke as their own contributing units). (2) THE NATIONAL COUNCIL BULLETIN, about ten issues 1950-1968, which is the national body's organ and covers the postwar gap. (3) THE QUARTERLY REPORTER No. 1 of 1856 and the 1874 ANNUAL REPORT, both pre-camp, for the association's own early shape and for the Cushing and Budge generations. (4) The 1959 short-version annual report, the 1970 and 1982 bulletins, the 2001-2002 French annual report. DEPRIORITISE CANADIAN MANHOOD (1914-1919): tested, and its camps are MILITARY camps, so read it for the war and Kanawana's wartime staffing rather than for camp programme. THE FILENAME TRAP IS IN f_5243 AND IN THE CACHED LIST -- the djvu.txt is named after the item's TITLE, not its identifier, and the obvious URL 404s. ALSO OPEN, AND SEPARABLE: the 437 unread IMAGE items are city-branch photographs catalogued with generic titles and NOT by camp, so a Kanawana photograph among them would not surface in any search on the camp's name. Checking them means looking, not searching. Raised 2026-09-07. || STARTED THE SAME DAY, AND THE TWO BULLETIN RUNS ARE NOW SWEPT FOR THE CAMPS' NAMES. All twenty-six News Bulletin and National Council Bulletin issues were downloaded and grepped for 'Kanawana' and 'Otoreke' with OCR variants. THREE HITS, in three issues, all of them new to this project: (1) The News Bulletin Vol 15 No 1 (1939), the World Service objectives table listing both camps as their own contributing units (f_5244); (2) the National Council Bulletin for October 1962, 'F. William Halliday, from Calgary to Ass't and Camp Kanawana, Montreal-North Mount' -- a named 1962 staff arrival inside the directorial gap, written into directors-index.md (f_5245); and (3) the National Council Bulletin Vol 40 Nos 2 and 3 (1967), 'So-Ed Youth Cultural Exchange, Otoreke, Montreal, P.Q.', July 9-15, on the national calendar beside Geneva Park and the Pan-American Games, written into camp-otoreke.md (f_5246). SO THE NAME SWEEP OF THESE TWO RUNS IS DONE AND SHOULD NOT BE REPEATED. WHAT IS NOT DONE: reading the issues themselves. A name grep finds the camp where it is named and misses everything about Montreal boys' work, staff, budgets and programme that bears on the camp without naming it -- which, on the evidence of this project's annual-report work, is where most of the value is. The 1856 Quarterly Reporter, the 1874 annual report, the 1959 short-version report, the 1970 and 1982 bulletins and the 2001-02 French report are all still unread, and so are the 437 images. || THE NEWS BULLETIN AND NATIONAL COUNCIL BULLETIN RUNS ARE NOW READ FOR THEIR CAMPING CONTENT, 2026-09-07, not merely grepped. Twenty-six issues opened; the camping passages in every one with a non-trivial count were read. WHAT CAME OUT, all in the KB and in articles: the 1936 Institute for Camp Leaders and the CCA's pre-history (f_5247, f_5248); the 1944 firsts list conceding Canadian primacy to Chance Harbour 1889 (f_5249); the 1931 national Boys' Work Committee's 'camps would then be laboratories for the training of leaders' (f_5250); the 1932 Toronto camp-leader training syllabus with Indian Lore in the practicum (f_5251); the national camp counts of 1964 and 1965 with the same figure printed twice (f_5252, corrected in place); the Expo 67 explanation for the Eastern Canadian attendance dip (f_5253); and the June 1946 Montreal statement of what camping is for, plus the 1949 Handbook of Y.M.C.A. Camp Administration (f_5254). ISSUES WITH NOTHING: vol 9 nos 1 and 2, the December 1934 issue, and vol 21 no 1 contain no camp word at all; vol 7 nos 3 and 7 have one each and both are incidental; vol 20 no 7 and vol 19 no 2 are prisoner-of-war and military-camp material. THE 1950 NATIONAL COUNCIL BULLETIN'S interracial-camping report IS AMERICAN -- 77 of 167 associations, camps in sixteen US states and Hawaii -- and must not be read as Canadian. STILL UNREAD FROM THE 47: the Quarterly Reporter of 1856, the 1874 annual report, Canadian Manhood (deprioritised, military camps), the 1959 short-version annual report, the 1970 and 1982 bulletins, the 2001-02 French annual report, and the 437 images.

queue_ordering.scheme: Three tiers per operator direction 2026-08-25. (1) YIELD -- what returns the most new information per unit of effort: whole seams, not single facts.
